name: Smash Burgers
blurb: Thin, crispy-edged beef patties with melted cheese in a soft bun.
ingredients: 600g beef mince (20% fat), loosely formed into 8 balls
Burger sauce: 4 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp mustard, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin
method: Get a heavy pan or flat griddle smoking hot.
Put a ball of mince in the pan, scatter with a little onion, and smash flat with a spatula for 15 seconds. Season.
Cook 2 minutes until the edges are lacy and crisp, flip, add cheese and cook 1 minute more.
Stack two patties per toasted bun with sauce, pickles and lettuce.

name: Baked Mac & Cheese
blurb: Ultra-cheesy macaroni with a crunchy buttered crumb, US diner style.
ingredients: 200g sharp cheddar, 100g Monterey Jack or mozzarella, 40g parmesan
1 tsp mustard powder, 1/2 tsp smoked paprika
method: Cook the macaroni 2 minutes under, then drain.
Make a roux with the butter and flour, whisk in the milk and simmer to a smooth sauce.
Off the heat stir in the cheeses, mustard powder and paprika.
Combine with the pasta, tip into a dish, top with the panko and bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes.

name: Buffalo Wings
blurb: Baked-then-tossed wings in a buttery hot sauce with blue cheese dip.
ingredients: 80g butter, 120ml hot sauce (Frank's style), 1 tsp Worcestershire
Blue cheese dip: 80g blue cheese, 3 tbsp soured cream, 3 tbsp mayo, splash of milk
Celery and carrot sticks to serve
method: Pat the wings very dry, toss with the baking powder and salt, and arrange on a rack.
Bake at 220C fan for 40-45 minutes, turning once, until deeply crisp.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and Worcestershire.
Toss the hot wings in the sauce and serve with the blue cheese dip and crudites.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork
blurb: Low and slow pork shoulder with a dry rub, pulled and sauced, in buns.
ingredients: Rub: 3 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp each salt, pepper, garlic powder, mustard powder
BBQ sauce: 200ml ketchup, 3 tbsp cider vinegar, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp smoked paprika
Soft buns and slaw to serve
method: Rub the pork all over and leave overnight if you can.
Sit it in a deep tray, pour the cider around, cover tightly with foil and cook at 140C fan for 5 hours until it shreds with a fork.
Rest 30 minutes, then pull the meat, discarding excess fat.
Simmer the sauce ingredients for 10 minutes and toss enough through the pork to coat.
Pile into buns with slaw.

name: Classic Meatloaf
blurb: Herby beef and pork loaf with a sticky ketchup glaze, with mash.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tsp thyme
Glaze: 100ml ketchup, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp cider vinegar
Mash and green beans to serve
method: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk. Mix with the minces, onion, garlic, eggs, Worcestershire, mustard and thyme. Season.
Press into a loaf tin or shape on a lined tray.
Bake at 180C fan for 40 minutes, then brush with the glaze and bake 20 minutes more.
Rest 10 minutes, slice, and serve with mash and beans.

name: Chicken & Sausage Jambalaya
blurb: One-pot Louisiana rice with chicken, smoked sausage and the holy trinity.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 green pepper, 2 celery sticks, diced
2 tbsp Cajun seasoning, 1 tsp smoked paprika
method: Brown the chicken and sausage, then set aside.
Soften the onion, pepper and celery, then add the Cajun seasoning and paprika.
Stir in the rice, then the tomatoes and stock, and return the meat.
Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Rest 5 minutes and finish with spring onions.

name: Philly Cheesesteak
blurb: Thin-sliced steak with onions and molten cheese in a soft sub roll.
ingredients: 600g rump or ribeye, part-frozen and shaved thin
method: Fry the onions (and pepper) in a hot pan until soft and browned, then push to one side.
Add the shaved beef, season, and cook quickly, chopping it up with the edge of a spatula.
Mix the beef and onions, divide into roll-sized piles, lay cheese over each and let it melt.
Scoop each pile into a buttered, toasted roll.

name: Chili with Cornbread
blurb: A thick beef and bean chili baked under a cornbread topping.
ingredients: 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp chipotle paste
400g tin chopped tomatoes, 400g tin kidney beans
Cornbread: 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 1 egg, 250ml buttermilk, 40g melted butter, 1 tsp sugar
method: Brown the mince, add the onion, pepper, garlic and spices, then the tomatoes and beans. Simmer 30 minutes until thick.
Tip into a wide ovenproof dish.
Whisk the cornbread wet and dry ingredients separately, then combine to a thick batter.
Dollop over the chili and bake at 190C fan for 25 minutes until the topping is set and golden.

name: Sloppy Joes
blurb: Sweet-savoury saucy beef mince piled into soft burger buns.
ingredients: 1 onion and 1 green pepper, finely diced
4 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp tomato puree, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp mustard
method: Brown the mince, add the onion, pepper and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the ketchup, puree, sugar, Worcestershire and mustard, then the stock.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes until thick and glossy.
Spoon generously into toasted buns.

name: New England Clam Chowder
blurb: Creamy potato and clam soup with bacon, served with crackers.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins clams in juice (or 1kg fresh, steamed)
Oyster or saltine crackers to serve
method: Fry the bacon until crisp, then soften the onion and celery in the fat.
Stir in the flour, then add the clam juice, potatoes, bay and thyme, and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Add the milk and cream and warm through without boiling.
Stir in the clams, season, and serve with crackers and parsley.

name: Chicken Pot Pie
blurb: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky pastry lid.
method: Brown the chicken, then soften the onion, carrot and celery.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, and simmer to a sauce. Add the cream, thyme, peas, sweetcorn and chicken.
Tip into a pie dish and cool a little.
Top with pastry, crimp, glaze with egg, cut a vent, and bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.

name: Chicken Cobb Salad
blurb: A big composed salad of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado and blue cheese.
ingredients: Dressing: 4 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp honey
method: Arrange the lettuce on a big platter.
Lay the chicken, bacon, quartered eggs, sliced avocado, tomatoes and crumbled blue cheese in rows on top.
Whisk the dressing and pour over just before serving.
Toss at the table.

name: Tuna Melt
blurb: Griddled sandwich of tuna mayo and melting cheese.
ingredients: 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, 2 spring onions, squeeze of lemon
method: Mix the tuna with the mayo, gherkin, spring onion and lemon; season.
Butter the bread on the outside. Build sandwiches with cheese, tuna, cheese.
Griddle in a pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes each side, pressing, until golden and molten.

name: Loaded Hot Dogs
blurb: Griddled frankfurters in soft buns with quick onions and all the sauces.
ingredients: 2 onions, sliced and fried until sticky
method: Griddle or fry the sausages until browned and hot through.
Lightly toast the buns.
Load with the fried onions and sausages.
Finish with mustard, ketchup and whatever toppings you like.

name: Chicken Caesar Salad
blurb: Crisp romaine, garlicky anchovy dressing, croutons and grilled chicken.
ingredients: Dressing: 4 anchovy fillets, 1 garlic clove, 1 egg yolk, 1 tsp Dijon, juice of half a lemon, 6 tbsp olive oil, 20g grated Parmesan
method: Toss the bread with oil and bake at 200C fan for 10 minutes until crisp.
Season and griddle the chicken for 5-6 minutes each side, then rest and slice.
Blitz or whisk the dressing ingredients to a smooth, pourable sauce.
Toss the lettuce with most of the dressing, then top with chicken, croutons and Parmesan.

name: Halloumi, Grain & Pomegranate Bowl
blurb: Griddled halloumi over lemony grains with herbs and pomegranate.
ingredients: Big handful each parsley and mint, chopped
Zest and juice of 1 lemon, 4 tbsp olive oil
method: Toss the warm grains with the lemon, oil, herbs and sumac; season.
Griddle the halloumi for 1-2 minutes each side until bar-marked.
Fold the pomegranate and walnuts through the grains.
Top with the hot halloumi and a final scatter of sumac.

name: Salade Niçoise
blurb: Seared tuna, green beans, new potatoes, egg, olives and a sharp dressing.
ingredients: Dressing: 6 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 small garlic clove, few basil leaves
method: Boil the potatoes until tender; add the beans for the last 3 minutes. Drain and cool slightly.
Soft-boil the eggs for 6-7 minutes, then peel and halve.
Sear the tuna in a very hot pan for 1 minute each side so it stays pink; slice.
Whisk the dressing. Arrange everything on a platter and spoon the dressing over.

name: Salmon Poke Bowl
blurb: Marinated raw salmon over rice with edamame, avocado, cucumber and sesame.
ingredients: 300g very fresh skinless salmon fillet, diced
200g sushi rice, cooked and cooled slightly
Marinade: 2 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp honey, pinch of chilli flakes
2 spring onions, sesame seeds, pickled ginger to serve
method: Mix the marinade and gently fold through the salmon; leave 10 minutes.
Divide the rice between bowls.
Arrange the salmon, edamame, avocado and cucumber on top.
Finish with spring onions, sesame and pickled ginger.

name: Greek Chicken Souvlaki Bowl
blurb: Lemon-oregano chicken with rice, tzatziki, tomato-cucumber salad and olives.
ingredients: Marinade: juice of 1 lemon, 3 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp dried oregano, 3 garlic cloves
Tzatziki: 300g yoghurt, half a grated and squeezed cucumber, 1 garlic clove, splash of vinegar
Salad: 3 tomatoes, half a cucumber, half a red onion, chopped
method: Marinate the chicken for at least 30 minutes, then thread on skewers.
Cook the rice. Mix the tzatziki and the chopped salad separately.
Grill or griddle the skewers for 10-12 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked.
Build bowls with rice, chicken, salad, tzatziki, olives and crumbled feta.

name: Peanut Tofu Buddha Bowl
blurb: Crisp baked tofu, brown rice, raw veg and a lime-peanut dressing.
ingredients: 450g firm tofu, cubed and tossed with 2 tbsp cornflour and soy
Dressing: 3 tbsp peanut butter, juice of 1 lime, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp maple, 1 tsp grated ginger, water to loosen
method: Bake the tofu at 200C fan for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Cook the rice.
Whisk the dressing until pourable.
Build bowls with rice, raw veg, edamame and tofu, then drizzle generously with the peanut dressing.

name: Pork Larb Lettuce Cups
blurb: Zingy Thai minced pork with lime, chilli, herbs and toasted rice, in lettuce.
ingredients: 2 tbsp uncooked rice, toasted and ground
Juice of 3 limes, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar
Big handful each mint and coriander
method: Cook the pork in a dry hot pan with a splash of water, breaking it small, until just done.
Off the heat, add the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and chilli.
Stir through the shallots, spring onions, herbs and toasted rice powder.
Spoon into lettuce cups to eat with your hands.

name: Roast Veg & Feta Quinoa Salad
blurb: Warm roasted vegetables through herby quinoa with feta and a lemon dressing.
ingredients: 1 aubergine, 1 courgette, 1 red pepper, 1 red onion, chopped
Dressing: juice of 1 lemon, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp honey, 1 small garlic clove
method: Toss the vegetables with oil and roast at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes until soft and charred.
Cook the quinoa in salted water for 12-15 minutes, then drain well.
Toss the warm quinoa with the dressing and herbs.
Fold through the roast veg and feta and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Prawn, Mango & Avocado Salad
blurb: Sweet mango, creamy avocado and prawns with a chilli-lime dressing.
ingredients: 1 baby gem or handful of rocket
Half a red onion, thinly sliced
Dressing: juice of 2 limes, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp honey, 1 red chilli chopped
method: Whisk the dressing.
Gently combine the prawns, mango, avocado and onion.
Fold through the leaves and coriander.
Dress just before serving so the avocado stays bright.

name: Tuna Panzanella
blurb: Torn sourdough soaked in tomato juices with tuna, capers and red onion.
ingredients: 2 x 160g tins good tuna in oil
5 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar
method: Salt the tomatoes and leave 10 minutes to release their juices.
Soak the onion in the vinegar for 10 minutes.
Toast or griddle the bread, then toss with the tomatoes, onion, oil and capers.
Leave 10 minutes for the bread to soften, then flake in the tuna and tear through the basil.

name: Chopped Italian Salad
blurb: Everything diced small — salami, provolone, chickpeas, peppers, a red wine vinaigrette.
ingredients: Dressing: 5 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp Dijon
method: Whisk the dressing with plenty of black pepper.
Combine all the chopped ingredients in a big bowl.
Toss with the dressing just before serving so it stays crunchy.

name: Seared Steak with Rocket & Parmesan
blurb: Rested sliced steak over peppery rocket with shaved Parmesan and balsamic.
method: Season the steaks well and sear in a smoking-hot pan for 2-3 minutes each side. Rest 5 minutes.
Dress the rocket and tomatoes lightly with oil and a pinch of salt.
Slice the steak against the grain and lay over the leaves.
Shave over the Parmesan and finish with balsamic and any resting juices.

name: Chicken & Bacon Cobb Salad
blurb: A composed salad of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, blue cheese and tomato.
ingredients: Dressing: 4 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 tsp honey
method: Lay the lettuce on a platter.
Arrange the chicken, bacon, quartered eggs, sliced avocado, tomatoes and crumbled blue cheese in rows.
Whisk the dressing and pour over just before serving; toss at the table.

name: Black Bean, Corn & Lime Quinoa
blurb: A zesty Tex-Mex bowl of quinoa, black beans, charred corn, avocado and coriander.
ingredients: 300g sweetcorn, charred in a dry pan
Dressing: juice of 2 limes, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp maple, pinch of chilli
method: Cook the quinoa, drain well and cool slightly.
Char the corn in a hot dry pan until spotty.
Toss the quinoa with the beans, corn, onion and dressing.
Fold through the avocado and coriander just before serving.

name: Smoked Mackerel & Beetroot Salad
blurb: Peppery leaves, sweet beetroot, horseradish crème fraîche and flaked mackerel.
ingredients: 2 smoked mackerel fillets, skin removed and flaked
Dressing: 3 tbsp crème fraîche, 1 tbsp horseradish, squeeze of lemon
method: Loosen the horseradish crème fraîche with a little water to a drizzling consistency.
Pile the leaves, beetroot and apple on plates.
Scatter over the flaked mackerel and hazelnuts.
Spoon over the dressing and add a squeeze more lemon.

name: Caprese Orzo Salad
blurb: Cooled orzo with mozzarella pearls, cherry tomatoes, basil and balsamic.
method: Cook the orzo, drain, rinse briefly under cold water and drain well.
Toss with the oil, balsamic and garlic.
Fold through the tomatoes, mozzarella and torn basil.
Season and serve at room temperature.

name: Falafel & Tahini Salad Bowl
blurb: Baked falafel over chopped salad and hummus with a lemony tahini drizzle.
ingredients: 1 pack ready falafel (or homemade), baked until crisp
Chopped salad: 3 tomatoes, 1 cucumber, half a red onion, handful of parsley
Tahini sauce: 4 tbsp tahini, juice of 1 lemon, 1 small garlic clove, water
method: Heat the falafel through in a 200C oven for 12-15 minutes until crisp.
Whisk the tahini with lemon, garlic and water until creamy and pourable.
Spread hummus in the base of each bowl.
Top with the shredded lettuce, chopped salad, falafel and pickles, then drizzle with tahini.

name: Vietnamese Chicken Noodle Salad (Bun Ga)
blurb: Cold rice vermicelli with lemongrass chicken, herbs, pickled veg and nuoc cham.
ingredients: Marinade: 2 lemongrass stalks minced, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 garlic cloves
1 carrot and half a cucumber, julienned
Big handful each mint, coriander and Thai basil
Nuoc cham: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 3 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 chilli, 1 garlic clove, 4 tbsp water
method: Marinate the chicken for 20 minutes, then sear in a hot pan until caramelised and cooked.
Mix the nuoc cham until the sugar dissolves.
Divide the noodles between bowls and top with carrot, cucumber and herbs.
Add the hot chicken, scatter with peanuts and pour over the nuoc cham.

name: Roast Salmon & Broccoli Grain Bowl
blurb: Flaked roast salmon, charred tenderstem, avocado and grains with a green dressing.
ingredients: Dressing: big handful of parsley and basil, 1 small garlic clove, juice of 1 lemon, 5 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp capers
method: Roast the salmon and broccoli (tossed in a little oil) at 200C fan for 12-14 minutes.
Blitz the dressing ingredients to a loose green sauce.
Warm the grains and divide between bowls.
Flake over the salmon, add the broccoli and sliced avocado, and spoon over the green dressing.

name: The Full English for Dinner
blurb: Bacon, sausage, eggs, beans, mushrooms, tomatoes and toast — any time.
method: Start the sausages slow in a pan or low oven.
Fry the bacon, then the mushrooms and tomatoes in the fat.
Warm the beans; fry the eggs to order; toast the bread.
Plate everything with brown sauce or ketchup.

name: Shakshuka
blurb: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce with feta and bread.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp caraway, chilli to taste
method: Soften the onion and pepper, add the garlic and spices.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 12-15 minutes until thick.
Make wells and crack in the eggs; cover and cook 5-7 minutes.
Crumble over feta and coriander; serve with bread.

name: Croque Madame
blurb: Grilled ham and cheese under béchamel and gruyère, topped with a fried egg.
ingredients: 20g butter, 20g flour, 250ml milk, 1 tsp Dijon, nutmeg
method: Make a thick béchamel; stir in the mustard, nutmeg and a third of the cheese.
Build sandwiches with ham and cheese, toast in a pan, then transfer to a tray.
Spread the béchamel over, scatter with the rest of the cheese, and grill until bubbling.
Fry the eggs and sit one on each; serve with salad.

name: Bacon & Maple Pancake Stack
blurb: Fluffy American pancakes with crispy streaky bacon and lots of maple syrup.
ingredients: 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tbsp sugar, pinch of salt
Butter for the pan, maple syrup
method: Fry the bacon until crisp; keep warm.
Whisk the dry ingredients, then beat in the egg, milk and butter to a thick batter.
Cook spoonfuls in a buttered pan until bubbles form, then flip.
Stack with the bacon and drown in maple syrup.

name: Eggs Benedict
blurb: Poached eggs and ham on toasted muffins under a quick blender hollandaise.
ingredients: Hollandaise: 3 egg yolks, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 150g melted butter, pinch of cayenne
method: Blitz the yolks and lemon juice, then pour in the hot butter in a thin stream until thick; season.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water for 3 minutes.
Top the toasted muffins with ham (or spinach) and the eggs.
Spoon over the hollandaise and dust with cayenne.

name: Spanish Tortilla
blurb: A thick potato and onion omelette, set soft in the middle.
method: Gently cook the potatoes and onions in the oil over low heat for 20 minutes until soft, not coloured; drain (keep the oil).
Beat the eggs, fold in the potatoes and onions, and season.
Cook in a little of the oil over low heat for 8 minutes, then flip onto a plate and slide back to set the other side.
Rest 5 minutes; serve warm or at room temperature with salad.

name: Breakfast Burrito
blurb: Scrambled egg, sausage, cheese, hash brown and salsa rolled in a big tortilla.
ingredients: 4 sausages or 200g chorizo, cooked and sliced
method: Warm the tortillas.
Layer egg, sausage, a hash brown, cheese and salsa down the middle.
Fold in the ends and roll tightly.
Toast seam-down in a dry pan to seal and crisp.

name: Savoury French Toast with Bacon
blurb: Cheesy fried eggy bread topped with crispy bacon and a fried egg.
ingredients: 3 eggs, 4 tbsp milk, 40g grated Parmesan, chives
method: Whisk the eggs, milk, Parmesan and chives; soak the bread.
Fry the bacon until crisp; set aside.
Fry the soaked bread in butter until golden both sides.
Top with the bacon and a fried egg.

name: Kedgeree
blurb: Curried rice with smoked haddock, boiled eggs, peas and parsley.
ingredients: 1 onion, 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 bay leaf
method: Poach the haddock in simmering water for 4 minutes, then flake.
Fry the onion in butter, add the curry powder and bay, then the rice.
Add 550ml water, cover and cook 12 minutes, adding the peas at the end.
Fold through the fish, halved eggs, parsley and lemon.

name: Menemen
blurb: Soft eggs cooked into a spiced Turkish pepper and tomato base, scooped with bread.
ingredients: 1 tbsp Turkish pepper paste or purée
Butter and olive oil, crusty bread
method: Soften the peppers in butter and oil for 6-8 minutes.
Add the pepper paste and tomatoes and cook to a thick sauce.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over low heat until just set.
Serve straight from the pan with bread.

name: Loaded Breakfast Hash
blurb: Crispy potato, sausage and pepper hash baked with eggs cracked on top.
ingredients: 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp chilli flakes
method: Fry the potatoes and sausage in an ovenproof pan until crisp and browned.
Add the peppers, onion and spices and cook 5 minutes.
Make wells and crack in the eggs; scatter with cheese.
Bake at 200C fan for 8-10 minutes until the eggs are set; finish with spring onions and hot sauce.

name: Roast Veg & Feta Frittata
blurb: An oven-baked frittata packed with roasted vegetables and feta.
ingredients: 1 courgette, 1 pepper, 1 red onion, 200g cherry tomatoes, roasted
method: Beat the eggs with the milk, herbs and Parmesan; season.
Fold in the roasted vegetables in an ovenproof pan.
Pour in the eggs, scatter with feta, and cook on the hob for 3 minutes.
Finish under the grill or in a 190C oven for 10-12 minutes until set; serve with salad.

name: Brunch Toad in the Hole with Bacon
blurb: Sausages and bacon baked in Yorkshire batter, with a fried egg on top.
method: Whisk the batter and rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oil, sausages and bacon in a roasting tin at 220C fan for 8 minutes.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes without opening the door.
Serve topped with fried eggs and a side of beans.

name: Cheesy Crumpets with Poached Eggs & Spinach
blurb: Toasted crumpets loaded with melted cheese, garlicky spinach and poached eggs.
ingredients: 200g spinach, 1 garlic clove, knob of butter
method: Toast the crumpets, top with cheese and grill until molten.
Wilt the spinach with the garlic and butter.
Poach the eggs.
Top the crumpets with spinach and eggs; finish with chilli flakes and pepper.

name: Baked Eggs with Chorizo & Potato
blurb: Sautéed potato and chorizo with eggs baked on top and lots of paprika oil.
method: Fry the chorizo until its oil runs, add the potatoes and fry until crisp.
Add the onion, pepper, garlic and paprika, then the tomatoes; simmer 8 minutes.
Make wells and crack in the eggs.
Bake at 200C fan for 8-10 minutes until set; finish with parsley and serve with bread.

name: Chicken & Waffles
blurb: Crispy fried chicken on fluffy waffles with hot sauce and maple syrup.
ingredients: 200g seasoned flour with paprika, garlic and onion powder, cayenne
Waffle batter: 250g flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 eggs, 350ml buttermilk, 60g melted butter
method: Dredge the chicken and fry at 170C for 6-8 minutes until golden and cooked; drain.
Whisk the waffle batter and cook in a hot waffle iron until crisp.
Stack chicken on the waffles.
Drizzle with hot sauce and maple syrup.

name: Steak & Ale Pie
blurb: Slow-cooked beef in ale gravy under a puff pastry lid.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato purée, 440ml brown ale, 400ml beef stock
method: Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown in batches.
Soften the veg, stir in the purée, add the ale and reduce, then the stock and herbs.
Cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours; cool.
Fill a pie dish, top with pastry, glaze and vent, and bake at 200C fan for 30 minutes.

name: Gammon with Parsley Sauce
blurb: Poached gammon joint with a proper parsley white sauce, mash and greens.
ingredients: Sauce: 40g butter, 40g cornflour, 500ml of the cooking liquor + milk, big bunch of parsley
method: Simmer the gammon with the onion, bay and peppercorns for about 1.5 hours (25 min per 500g).
Rest, then carve.
Make the sauce with butter, cornflour and the strained liquor topped up with milk; stir in the chopped parsley.
Serve the gammon with mash, cabbage and lots of parsley sauce.

name: Faggots with Onion Gravy & Mushy Peas
blurb: Herby pork meatballs baked in gravy — proper old-school comfort food.
ingredients: 80g breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 1 tsp sage, 1 tsp thyme
Onion gravy: 2 onions, 1 tbsp flour, 600ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
Mushy peas and mash to serve
method: Mix the pork, livers, onion, breadcrumbs, egg and herbs; roll into large balls.
Brown, then set aside. Caramelise the onions, stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire.
Nestle the faggots into the gravy and bake at 180C fan for 40 minutes.
Serve with mushy peas and mash.

name: Liver, Bacon & Onion Gravy
blurb: Quick-seared calf's or lamb's liver with crisp bacon and a sticky onion gravy.
ingredients: 2 tbsp flour, 600ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
method: Fry the bacon until crisp; set aside. Cook the onions in the fat until golden.
Stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Dust the liver in seasoned flour and sear 1-2 minutes each side — keep it pink.
Return the bacon, nestle in the liver and serve with mash.

name: Bangers & Champ
blurb: Grilled sausages on spring-onion mash with a mountain of onion gravy.
ingredients: 900g potatoes, 6 spring onions, 60g butter, 100ml warm milk
Gravy: 3 onions, 1 tbsp cornflour, 600ml beef stock, 1 tsp Dijon, Worcestershire
method: Grill or fry the sausages slowly until browned all over.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter and milk; beat in the softened spring onions.
Cook the onions low and slow, add the cornflour, then the stock, mustard and Worcestershire.
Serve the sausages on the champ, drowned in gravy.

name: Smoked Haddock Fish Pie
blurb: Smoked and white fish in a herby sauce under cheesy mash.
method: Poach the fish in the milk with bay for 4 minutes; lift out and flake, keeping the milk.
Make a white sauce with butter, flour and the infused milk; stir in herbs.
Fold in the fish, peas and egg; tip into a dish.
Top with seasoned mash and cheddar; bake at 200C fan for 30 minutes.

name: Corned Beef Hash Pie
blurb: Corned beef, potato and onion baked under shortcrust — a chip-shop classic at home.
method: Fry the onions, add the potatoes, corned beef, stock and Worcestershire; thicken with cornflour and cool.
Line a pie dish with two-thirds of the pastry.
Fill, top with the rest of the pastry, seal, glaze and vent.
Bake at 190C fan for 35-40 minutes until golden.

name: Cauliflower Cheese Baked Potatoes
blurb: Fluffy jackets loaded with sharp cauliflower cheese and a crunchy top.
method: Bake the pricked, oiled and salted potatoes at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes.
Blanch the cauliflower 4 minutes; make a cheese sauce with butter, cornflour, milk, most of the cheese and the mustard.
Split the potatoes, fluff, and pile with the cauliflower cheese.
Top with crumbs and the rest of the cheese; grill 5 minutes.

name: Homemade Scampi & Chips
blurb: Breadcrumbed langoustine tails with chips, peas and tartare.
ingredients: 500g raw peeled langoustine or large prawn tails
Tartare: 5 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, 1 tsp capers, lemon
method: Roast the chips (tossed in oil) at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes.
Coat the tails in flour, egg then breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry for 2-3 minutes until golden and cooked; drain.
Serve with the chips, peas, tartare and lemon.

name: Chicken Kiev
blurb: Crumbed chicken breast that bursts with garlic-parsley butter.
ingredients: 100g soft butter, 4 garlic cloves, big handful of parsley, squeeze of lemon
Mash or new potatoes and greens to serve
method: Beat the butter with the garlic, parsley and lemon; shape into a log and freeze until firm.
Cut a pocket in each breast and push in a chunk of the butter; seal well.
Coat in flour, egg then panko (double the egg and crumb layer).
Fry to colour, then bake at 190C fan for 20-25 minutes until cooked through.

name: Veggie Sausage Toad in the Hole
blurb: Meat-free sausages in crisp Yorkshire batter with red onion gravy.
ingredients: Gravy: 2 red onions, 1 tbsp flour, 500ml vegetable stock, 1 tsp balsamic, Marmite
method: Whisk the batter and rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oil and sausages in a roasting tin at 220C fan for 8 minutes.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes without opening the door.
Caramelise the onions, stir in the flour, then the stock, balsamic and a little Marmite; simmer to a gravy.

name: Lentil Cottage Pie
blurb: Rich lentil and mushroom mince topped with golden mash — no one misses the meat.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tbsp Marmite, 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 300ml stock
method: Soften the onion, carrot, celery and mushrooms for 12 minutes.
Add the purée, Marmite, tomatoes, lentils, stock and thyme; simmer 25 minutes until thick.
Top with olive-oil mash and rough up the surface.
Bake at 200C fan for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Pork Chops with Apple & Cider
blurb: Pan-fried chops with a cream, cider and apple sauce, and mash.
ingredients: Few sage leaves, mash and greens to serve
method: Season and fry the chops for 4 minutes each side; rest.
Soften the onion and apple in the pan, add the sage.
Pour in the cider and reduce by half, then the cream and mustard.
Return the chops and any juices; serve with mash and greens.

name: Salmon Fishcakes
blurb: Flaked salmon and mash patties, crumbed and fried, with a lemon mayo.
ingredients: 3 spring onions, 2 tbsp chopped dill, zest of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp capers
Lemon mayo and salad to serve
method: Mix the salmon, mash, spring onions, dill, lemon zest and capers; season and shape into 8 cakes. Chill 20 minutes.
Coat in flour, egg then breadcrumbs.
Shallow fry for 3-4 minutes each side until golden and hot through.
Serve with lemon mayo and a green salad.

name: Welsh Rarebit with Poached Egg
blurb: Grown-up cheese on toast under ale-and-mustard sauce, with a runny egg on top.
ingredients: 1 tsp English mustard, 1 tsp Worcestershire, 1 egg yolk
method: Make a thick paste with butter, flour and ale; off the heat stir in the cheese, mustard, Worcestershire and yolk.
Toast the bread one side, spread the mixture on the other, and grill until dark and bubbling.
Poach the eggs.
Serve the rarebit topped with a poached egg.

name: Individual Beef Wellingtons
blurb: Fillet steaks with mushroom duxelles and prosciutto in crisp puff pastry.
method: Sear the seasoned steaks 1 minute each side; cool and brush with mustard.
Fry the mushrooms until all the moisture has gone; cool.
Lay prosciutto on cling film, spread with duxelles, sit the steak on top and wrap tightly; chill 20 minutes.
Wrap each in pastry, glaze, and bake at 200C fan for 20-25 minutes for medium-rare; rest 8 minutes.

name: Quick Sausage Cassoulet
blurb: Sausages, bacon and white beans in a rich tomato-thyme sauce with a crumb top.
ingredients: 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 200ml stock, 1 tsp thyme
method: Brown the sausages and lardons in a casserole.
Add the onion and garlic, then the tomatoes, beans, stock and thyme.
Simmer 25 minutes, then top with the breadcrumbs and dots of butter.
Bake at 200C fan for 15 minutes until the crumb is golden; scatter with parsley.

name: Roast Chicken Crown with All the Trimmings
blurb: A chicken crown roasted fast, with roast potatoes, stuffing, carrots and gravy.
ingredients: 1kg potatoes for roasting, 4 tbsp goose fat
Gravy: 1 tbsp flour, 400ml chicken stock, splash of white wine
method: Rub the crown with butter, thyme and lemon; roast at 190C fan for 55-65 minutes until 70C.
Parboil and roughen the potatoes; roast in hot fat 45-55 minutes.
Bake the stuffing balls; boil the carrots, steam the greens.
Rest the chicken 15 minutes; make gravy in the tin. Carve and serve.

name: Cheese & Onion Pasties
blurb: Buttery shortcrust parcels of cheddar, potato and softened onion.
method: Mix the potato, onion, cheese and mustard with a splash of milk; season well.
Roll the pastry and cut into 4 circles.
Pile filling on one half, fold and crimp into pasties.
Glaze with egg and bake at 190C fan for 30-35 minutes until golden.

name: Hunter's Chicken
blurb: Chicken breasts wrapped in bacon, topped with barbecue sauce and melted cheese.
ingredients: Chips or jacket potatoes and salad to serve
method: Wrap each chicken breast in 2 rashers of bacon.
Sear in an ovenproof pan to colour the bacon.
Spoon over the barbecue sauce and scatter with cheese.
Bake at 200C fan for 20-25 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the cheese golden.

name: Lancashire Hotpot
blurb: Sliced lamb and onions under a lid of overlapping, buttery potato slices.
ingredients: 1 tbsp flour, 1 tsp thyme, 2 bay leaves
method: Toss the lamb in seasoned flour and brown, then layer with onions and carrots in a casserole.
Add the thyme, bay, stock and Worcestershire.
Overlap the potato slices on top, brush with butter and season.
Cover and cook at 160C fan for 1.5 hours, then uncover for 30 minutes to crisp the top.

name: Fish Finger Wraps
blurb: Crispy fish fingers, lettuce and tartare rolled in a soft tortilla — dinner in 15.
ingredients: Tartare: 4 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, squeeze of lemon
method: Bake or grill the fish fingers until crisp.
Warm the tortillas.
Spread with tartare and pile on lettuce, cucumber and the fish fingers.
Roll up tightly and cut in half.

name: Minute Steak with Chips & Peppercorn Sauce
blurb: Thin fast-fried steak, oven chips and a creamy peppercorn sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 1 shallot, 150ml beef stock, 100ml double cream, 1 tbsp green peppercorns, 1 tsp Dijon, splash of brandy
method: Roast the chips at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes.
Fry the seasoned steaks 1 minute each side; rest.
Soften the shallot, add the brandy, then stock, cream, peppercorns and mustard; simmer to a coating sauce.
Serve the steak with chips, sauce and watercress.

name: Tomato Soup & Extra-Cheese Toastie
blurb: Silky tomato soup with a griddled three-cheese toastie for dunking.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tsp sugar, 400ml stock
Toastie: 4 slices bread, 60g cheddar, 40g mozzarella, 20g Parmesan, butter
method: Soften the onion and garlic, add the purée, tomatoes, sugar and stock; simmer 15 minutes and blitz.
Season and add a splash of cream and torn basil.
Butter the bread outside, fill with the cheeses, and griddle until golden and molten.
Serve the soup with the toastie cut into fingers.

name: Shepherd's Pie
blurb: Minced lamb in rich gravy under a fluffy mashed potato crust.
method: Brown the mince, then set aside. Soften the onion and carrot for 10 minutes.
Stir in the puree, Worcestershire and thyme, return the lamb, add the stock and simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the peas.
Boil the potatoes, then mash with butter and milk and season well.
Spoon the mince into a dish, top with mash, rough up with a fork and scatter with cheese if using.
Bake at 200C fan for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Cottage Pie
blurb: The beef version: savoury mince and veg topped with golden mash.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato puree, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
method: Brown the mince and set aside. Soften the vegetables for 10 minutes.
Add the puree, Worcestershire and thyme, return the beef, pour in the stock and simmer 25 minutes.
Mash the boiled potatoes with butter and milk, season.
Top the mince with mash, fork the surface and bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.

name: Fish Pie
blurb: Smoked and white fish in a creamy sauce under mash, with peas.
ingredients: 600g fish pie mix (salmon, white fish, smoked haddock)
1 bay leaf, handful of parsley and chives
100g frozen peas, 3 eggs, hard boiled and quartered (optional)
method: Poach the fish in the milk with the bay for 4 minutes, then lift out and flake, keeping the milk.
Make a white sauce with the butter, flour and infused milk; stir in the herbs.
Fold the fish, peas and egg through the sauce and tip into a dish.
Top with seasoned mash and cheese, and bake at 200C fan for 30 minutes until golden.

name: Roast Chicken Dinner
blurb: Whole roast chicken with roast potatoes, veg and proper gravy.
ingredients: 1 lemon, halved, few thyme sprigs, 50g soft butter
Carrots, parsnips and greens to serve
Gravy: 1 tbsp flour, 400ml chicken stock, splash of wine
method: Heat oven to 200C fan. Rub the chicken with butter, season, and put the lemon and thyme in the cavity. Roast 70-80 minutes until juices run clear.
Parboil the potatoes 8 minutes, drain and rough up. Roast in hot fat for 45-55 minutes, turning, until crisp.
Boil the carrots and parsnips; steam the greens.
Rest the chicken 15 minutes. Make gravy in the roasting tin with the flour, wine and stock.
Carve and serve everything together.

name: Toad in the Hole
blurb: Sausages baked in crisp, billowing Yorkshire pudding batter with onion gravy.
ingredients: Onion gravy: 2 onions sliced, 1 tbsp flour, 500ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
method: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth batter and rest 30 minutes. Season.
Heat oven to 220C fan. Put the fat and sausages in a roasting tin and roast 10 minutes until sizzling.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes until risen and deep golden. Do not open the door early.
Meanwhile slowly caramelise the onions, stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Serve the toad in generous squares with the onion gravy.

name: Bangers & Mash
blurb: Grilled sausages, buttery mash and a deep onion gravy.
method: Fry or grill the sausages slowly until browned all over and cooked through.
Boil the potatoes and mash with butter and milk; season generously.
Cook the onions low and slow in butter for 20 minutes until sweet and golden.
Stir the cornflour into a little stock, add to the onions with the rest of the stock, mustard and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Serve the sausages on the mash, drowned in gravy.

name: Beef Stew & Dumplings
blurb: Slow-braised beef in ale gravy topped with fluffy suet dumplings.
ingredients: 2 tbsp plain flour, 2 tbsp tomato puree
500ml brown ale, 500ml beef stock, 2 bay leaves
Dumplings: 150g self-raising flour, 75g shredded suet, pinch of salt, water to bind
method: Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown well in batches in a casserole.
Soften the vegetables, stir in the puree, then add the ale and let it reduce.
Return the beef, add the stock and bay, cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours.
Mix the dumpling ingredients to a soft dough, roll into balls, and sit on top of the stew.
Cover and cook 20 minutes, then uncover for 10 more until the dumplings are risen and golden.

name: Cauliflower Cheese with Bacon
blurb: Cauliflower under a sharp cheese sauce and crisp bacon, baked as a main.
ingredients: 50g butter, 50g plain flour (or cornflour for GF), 600ml milk
method: Blanch the cauliflower for 4 minutes, then drain well.
Fry the bacon until crisp.
Make a white sauce with butter, flour and milk; off the heat stir in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Fold the cauliflower and bacon through the sauce in a dish, top with the rest of the cheese and the crumbs.
Bake at 200C fan for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Loaded Jacket Potatoes
blurb: Crisp-skinned baked potatoes with cheese, beans and whatever else.
ingredients: Optional: tuna mayo, coleslaw, spring onions
method: Heat oven to 200C fan. Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and salt, and bake directly on the shelf for 70-80 minutes until crisp outside and fluffy within.
Warm the beans.
Split the potatoes, fluff with butter and season, then pile on beans and cheese.
Return to the oven for 3 minutes to melt, or add cold toppings and serve.

name: Full English for Dinner
blurb: Breakfast when you want it: bacon, sausage, eggs, beans, mushrooms and toast.
method: Start the sausages in a low oven or slow in a pan; they take longest.
Fry the bacon, then the mushrooms and tomatoes in the fat.
Warm the beans.
Fry the eggs to order and toast the bread.
Plate everything together, with brown sauce or ketchup.

name: Welsh Rarebit
blurb: A grown-up cheese on toast: sharp cheddar, ale and mustard sauce grilled until blistered.
ingredients: 20g butter, 20g flour, 4 tbsp brown ale or milk
1 tsp English mustard, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
method: Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the ale to a thick paste.
Off the heat, stir in the cheese, mustard, Worcestershire and yolk to a spreadable mixture.
Toast the bread on one side under the grill.
Spread the mixture thickly on the untoasted side and grill until bubbling and dark gold.

name: Gammon, Egg & Chips
blurb: Pan-fried gammon steaks with fried eggs and oven chips.
ingredients: Peas or grilled pineapple to serve
method: Heat oven to 220C fan. Toss the chips in oil and salt and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once.
Snip the fat of the gammon so it does not curl, then fry for 3-4 minutes each side until caramelised.
Fry the eggs in the same pan.
Serve the gammon with the chips, eggs and peas.

name: Liver, Bacon & Onions
blurb: Quick-seared lamb's liver with bacon and a sticky onion gravy.
method: Fry the bacon until crisp, then set aside. Cook the onions in the fat until soft and golden.
Stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.
Dust the liver in seasoned flour and sear for 1-2 minutes each side; it should stay pink inside.
Return the bacon, nestle in the liver and serve with mash.

name: Chicken & Leek Pie
blurb: Creamy chicken and leek filling under a puff pastry lid.
ingredients: 30g butter, 30g flour, 400ml chicken stock, 100ml creme fraiche
method: Brown the chicken, then set aside. Soften the leeks in butter for 8 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, and simmer to a sauce. Add the creme fraiche, mustard, thyme and chicken.
Tip into a pie dish and cool slightly.
Top with pastry, seal the edges, cut a steam hole and brush with egg.
Bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes until puffed and golden.

name: Corned Beef Hash
blurb: Crisp fried potato and onion with corned beef and a runny egg on top.
ingredients: Brown sauce or beans to serve
method: Fry the onion in oil until soft, then add the potatoes and press down to crisp.
Turn the potatoes, add the corned beef and Worcestershire, and keep frying until crisp in patches.
Fry the eggs.
Serve the hash topped with a fried egg and brown sauce or beans.

name: Lancashire Hotpot
blurb: Slow-cooked lamb and onions under a lid of sliced potatoes.
ingredients: 800g lamb neck fillet or shoulder, sliced
1 tbsp flour, 1 tsp thyme, 2 bay leaves
method: Toss the lamb in seasoned flour and brown, then layer with the onions and carrots in a casserole.
Add the thyme, bay, stock and Worcestershire.
Overlap the potato slices on top, brush with butter and season.
Cover and cook at 160C fan for 1.5 hours, then uncover and cook 30 minutes more until the top is crisp and golden.

name: Sausage & Root Veg Traybake
blurb: Sausages roasted with potatoes, red onion and carrots in honey and mustard.
ingredients: 2 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard
method: Heat oven to 200C fan. Toss the potatoes and carrots with oil and rosemary in a large tray and roast 15 minutes.
Add the sausages and onions and roast 20 minutes.
Drizzle over the honey and mustard, toss, and roast a final 10 minutes until sticky and golden.

name: Macaroni Cheese
blurb: Proper baked mac and cheese with a crunchy top.
ingredients: 1 tsp English mustard, pinch of nutmeg
method: Cook the macaroni 2 minutes short of the packet time and drain.
Make a white sauce with the butter, flour and milk, then melt in most of the cheese with the mustard and nutmeg.
Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish and top with the crumb mix.
Bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Kedgeree
blurb: Smoked haddock, curried rice, boiled eggs and parsley - dinner or brunch.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 bay leaf
method: Poach the haddock in simmering water for 4 minutes, then flake, discarding skin and bones.
Fry the onion in butter until soft, add the curry powder and bay for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, add 550ml water, cover and cook 12 minutes until tender.
Fold through the fish, halved eggs, parsley and a good squeeze of lemon.

name: Store-Cupboard Tuna Pasta
blurb: Tinned tuna, sweetcorn and a quick tomato sauce — a fiver feeds four.
method: Fry the onion and garlic, add the purée and chilli, then the tomatoes.
Simmer 10 minutes, then flake in the tuna and add the corn.
Toss with the cooked pasta and a splash of pasta water.
Finish with parsley.

name: Egg Fried Rice
blurb: Leftover rice, a few eggs, frozen peas and soy — 10 minutes, barely any money.
ingredients: 1.5 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sesame oil, white pepper
method: Scramble the eggs in a hot oiled pan; set aside.
Fry the onion, garlic and peas, then add the rice and press to heat through.
Return the egg, add the soy, sesame oil and pepper, and toss.
Finish with spring onions.

name: Deluxe Beans on Toast
blurb: Baked beans spiked with smoked paprika, Worcestershire and cheese, on buttered sourdough.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp Worcestershire, dash of hot sauce
method: Warm the beans with the paprika, Worcestershire and hot sauce.
Toast and butter the bread.
Pile on the beans and scatter with cheese; grill 2 minutes to melt.
Finish with chives.

name: 10-Minute Coconut Lentil Curry
blurb: Red lentils, a tin of coconut milk and curry powder — dinner for pennies.
method: Fry the onion, garlic and spices.
Add the lentils, coconut milk, tomatoes and water.
Simmer 18-20 minutes until the lentils collapse.
Stir through a handful of spinach and a squeeze of lemon; serve with rice.

name: Jacket Potato with Cheese & Beans
blurb: The reliable, cheap classic — crisp-skinned potato, butter, beans and cheese.
method: Prick the potatoes, rub with oil and salt, and bake at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes.
Warm the beans.
Split the potatoes, fluff with butter and season.
Top with beans and cheese; return to the oven 3 minutes to melt.

name: Sausage & Tomato Pasta
blurb: Sausage meat browned into a quick tomato sauce with pasta — six sausages, one tin.
method: Fry the sausage meat hard until browned and craggy.
Add the onion, garlic, fennel and chilli, then the purée and tomatoes.
Simmer 12 minutes.
Toss with the pasta and a splash of pasta water; serve with cheese.

name: Chickpea, Spinach & Tomato Curry
blurb: Two tins of chickpeas, a tin of tomatoes, a bag of spinach — proper cheap and healthy.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chilli
method: Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook 8 minutes.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir through the spinach and lemon; serve with rice.

name: Cheese & Herb Omelette
blurb: Three eggs, cheese, a knob of butter — the two-minute dinner.
ingredients: Salt and pepper, toast to serve
method: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan until foaming; pour in the eggs.
Stir briskly for 20 seconds, then let the base set; scatter the cheese and herbs over one half.
Fold and slide onto a plate while still soft; serve with toast.

name: Fridge-Clearout Fried Rice
blurb: Whatever veg is lurking, some rice and an egg — turned into a proper dinner.
ingredients: 300g mixed veg (carrot, pepper, cabbage, peas, whatever)
3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp oyster or hoisin, 1 tsp sesame oil
method: Scramble the eggs in a hot oiled wok; set aside.
Stir-fry the harder veg first, then the softer, with the garlic and ginger.
Add the rice and sauces and toss until hot and coated.
Fold in the egg and spring onions; add chilli sauce to taste.

name: Baked Potato Soup
blurb: Blitzed baked potatoes with stock, milk and cheese — cheap, thick and comforting.
ingredients: Toppings: crispy bacon or croutons, chives, more cheese
method: Bake the potatoes at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes, then scoop the flesh (keep some skin for texture).
Soften the onion and garlic, add the potato, stock and milk.
Blitz roughly, stir in the cheese, and season well.
Serve topped with bacon or croutons, chives and more cheese.

name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
blurb: Spaghetti, garlic, chilli, olive oil and parsley — five ingredients, ten minutes.
method: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente; save a mug of water.
Gently fry the garlic and chilli in the oil until the garlic is pale gold.
Add a splash of pasta water to the oil, then the drained pasta.
Toss hard with more water and the parsley until glossy.

name: Corned Beef Hash
blurb: A tin of corned beef, some spuds and an onion — the cheapest good dinner going.
method: Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the potatoes and press down to crisp.
Turn, add the corned beef and Worcestershire, and keep frying until crisp in patches.
Fry the eggs if using.
Serve with brown sauce or beans.

name: Any-Veg Noodle Stir-Fry
blurb: A pack of noodles, a bag of stir-fry veg and a three-ingredient sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp sweet chilli or honey, 1 tsp sesame oil
method: Cook the noodles and drain.
Stir-fry the vegetables in a hot wok for 3 minutes, add the garlic and ginger.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss over high heat.
Finish with spring onions and sesame.

name: Baked Bean & Cheese Quesadilla
blurb: A tin of beans, some cheese and two tortillas — crisp, molten, done in 8 minutes.
ingredients: Pinch of smoked paprika and chilli
method: Spread beans over half of each tortilla, top with cheese, paprika and spring onion, and fold.
Toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes each side until crisp and molten.
Cut into wedges.
Serve with hot sauce.

name: Tomato & Lentil Soup
blurb: Two tins of tomatoes, a bag of red lentils, an onion — thick, filling and cheap.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp sugar
1 litre vegetable stock, lemon and bread to serve
method: Soften the onion and carrot, add the garlic and spices.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, sugar and stock.
Simmer 20 minutes until the lentils collapse.
Blitz smooth or leave rustic; season and serve with lemon and bread.

name: Sardines on Toast with Chilli & Lemon
blurb: Tinned sardines mashed onto hot buttered toast with lemon, chilli and parsley.
method: Toast and butter the bread.
Mash the sardines with a fork with some of their oil, the lemon and chilli.
Pile onto the toast.
Finish with parsley, lemon zest and pepper.

name: Potato, Onion & Cheese Frittata
blurb: Six eggs, a couple of potatoes and an onion — a whole dinner from the bottom of the fridge.
ingredients: Handful of parsley or chives, oil and butter
method: Fry the onions until soft and golden, add the sliced potato to warm through.
Beat the eggs with the milk, cheese and herbs; season.
Pour into the pan and cook on low for 6-8 minutes until mostly set.
Finish under the grill for 3-4 minutes; slice into wedges.

name: One-Pot Chilli Cheese Pasta
blurb: Beef mince, kidney beans, pasta and cheese cooked together in one pan.
ingredients: 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tbsp purée
400g tin chopped tomatoes, 400g tin kidney beans, 700ml beef stock
method: Brown the mince with the onion, garlic and spices.
Add the purée, tomatoes, beans, pasta and stock.
Simmer 12-15 minutes, stirring, until the pasta is cooked and saucy.
Stir in half the cheese; top with the rest and soured cream.

name: Creamy Chicken & Mushroom Pie
blurb: Chicken, mushrooms and tarragon in a cream sauce under puff pastry.
ingredients: 30g butter, 30g flour, 400ml chicken stock, 100ml double cream
method: Brown the chicken, then set aside. Soften the onion, leeks and mushrooms in butter for 10 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the stock, and simmer to a sauce. Add cream, tarragon, mustard and the chicken.
Tip into a pie dish and cool slightly. Top with pastry, seal, glaze with egg and cut a vent.
Bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes until puffed and deep golden.

name: Bacon Mac & Cheese
blurb: Baked macaroni in a three-cheese sauce with crispy bacon and a crumb top.
method: Fry the bacon until crisp. Cook the macaroni 2 minutes under and drain.
Make a roux with butter and flour, whisk in the milk and simmer to a smooth sauce.
Off the heat stir in the cheeses and mustard, then the pasta and bacon.
Tip into a dish, top with the panko and bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes.

name: Beef Stroganoff
blurb: Strips of beef and mushrooms in a mustard-soured cream sauce with rice.
method: Sear the beef in a very hot pan in batches, then set aside.
Soften the onion and mushrooms, add the paprika and mustard.
Add the stock and let it reduce, then stir in the soured cream and warm gently.
Return the beef and any juices, heat through, finish with parsley and serve with rice.

name: Sausage & Bean Casserole
blurb: Browned sausages braised with beans, tomatoes and smoked paprika.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins mixed beans or cannellini, drained
Crusty bread or mash to serve
method: Brown the sausages all over in a casserole, then set aside.
Soften the onion and peppers, add the garlic, paprika and thyme.
Add the tomatoes, beans and Worcestershire, return the sausages, and simmer for 25-30 minutes.
Season and serve with bread or mash.

name: The Ultimate Fish Finger Sandwich
blurb: Homemade crumbed fish fingers in soft bread with tartare and lettuce.
ingredients: 400g chunky white fish, cut into fingers
Tartare: 4 tbsp mayo, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, 1 tsp capers, squeeze of lemon
method: Coat the fish in flour, egg then panko.
Shallow fry for 2-3 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain.
Mix the tartare.
Build sandwiches with buttered bread, tartare, lettuce and the hot fish fingers.

name: Loaded Cauliflower Cheese
blurb: Whole roasted cauliflower florets in a sharp cheese sauce with a crunchy top.
ingredients: 1 tsp English mustard, pinch of nutmeg
30g pumpkin seeds or crushed crackers for the top
method: Roast the florets with a little oil at 220C fan for 20 minutes until edges char.
Make a white sauce with butter, cornflour and milk; off the heat stir in most of the cheese and the mustard.
Fold the cauliflower through the sauce in a dish, top with remaining cheese and the seeds.
Bake at 200C fan for 20 minutes until bubbling.

name: Beef Chilli Loaded Jacket Potatoes
blurb: Crisp-skinned baked potatoes stuffed with beef chilli, cheese and soured cream.
ingredients: 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp chipotle paste
400g tin chopped tomatoes, 400g tin kidney beans
150g grated cheddar, soured cream and spring onions to serve
method: Bake the pricked, oiled and salted potatoes at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes until crisp.
Brown the mince, add the onion, pepper and spices, then the tomatoes and beans. Simmer 30 minutes.
Split the potatoes, fluff with butter and season.
Load with chilli and cheese, return to the oven for 3 minutes, then top with soured cream and spring onions.

name: Tuna Pasta Bake
blurb: Pasta, tuna and sweetcorn in a cheesy tomato sauce with a golden crust.
method: Cook the pasta 2 minutes under.
Make a cheese sauce with butter, flour, milk, most of the cheese and the mustard, then stir in the passata.
Fold in the pasta, tuna and corn, tip into a dish, top with crumbs and the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 200C fan for 20-25 minutes until golden.

name: Cheesy-Topped Cottage Pie
blurb: Rich beef mince and vegetables under a cheddar-crusted mash.
ingredients: 1 tbsp Worcestershire, 350ml beef stock, 1 tsp thyme
900g potatoes for mash, 60g butter, splash of milk, 80g grated cheddar
method: Brown the mince, set aside. Soften the vegetables for 10 minutes.
Add the purée, Worcestershire and thyme, return the beef, add the stock and simmer 25 minutes. Stir in the peas.
Mash the boiled potatoes with butter and milk; season.
Top the mince with mash, fork the top, scatter with cheddar and bake at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.

name: Proper Chicken Noodle Soup
blurb: Golden broth, shredded chicken, soft noodles and lots of parsley.
ingredients: Big handful of parsley, squeeze of lemon
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in a little oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic.
Pour in the stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook until tender, then stir in the chicken to heat through.
Finish with parsley, lemon and plenty of black pepper.

name: Cheesy Tomato Gnocchi Bake
blurb: Potato gnocchi baked in a rich tomato sauce with mozzarella and basil.
method: Fry the garlic and chilli in oil, add the purée, then the tomatoes and sugar. Simmer 15 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi until they float, then drain.
Fold the gnocchi through the sauce in an ovenproof pan, dot with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake or grill at 220C for 10 minutes until blistered; finish with basil.

name: Corned Beef Hash with a Fried Egg
blurb: Crisp fried potato and onion with corned beef and a runny egg on top.
ingredients: Brown sauce or beans to serve
method: Fry the onion in oil until soft, add the potatoes and press down to crisp.
Turn, add the corned beef and Worcestershire, and keep frying until crisp in patches.
Fry the eggs.
Serve the hash topped with a fried egg and brown sauce or beans.

name: Roasted Vegetable Lasagne
blurb: Layers of roast Mediterranean veg, tomato sauce, béchamel and pasta.
ingredients: 2 aubergines, 2 courgettes, 2 peppers, 1 red onion, chopped and roasted
2 x 400g tins chopped tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, handful of basil
60g butter, 60g flour, 700ml milk, pinch of nutmeg
method: Roast the vegetables with oil at 200C fan for 30 minutes.
Simmer the tomatoes with garlic and basil for 20 minutes.
Make a béchamel with butter, flour and milk; add nutmeg and half the cheese.
Layer tomato sauce, veg, pasta and béchamel, repeating, finishing with béchamel and cheese.
Bake at 190C fan for 35-40 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes.

name: Turkey Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
blurb: Light turkey meatballs simmered in a herby tomato sauce, with spaghetti.
ingredients: 1 small onion grated, 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs, 1 tsp oregano, 2 garlic cloves
1 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tsp chilli flakes
method: Mix the mince with the onion, egg, breadcrumbs, oregano and garlic; roll into small balls.
Brown the meatballs in a pan, then set aside.
Fry the purée and chilli, add the tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes, then return the meatballs for 15 minutes.
Serve over spaghetti with basil.

name: Jacket Potato with Tuna Mayo & Sweetcorn
blurb: The classic quick fix — fluffy jacket, tuna mayo, corn and cheese.
method: Bake the pricked, oiled and salted potatoes at 200C fan for 70-80 minutes.
Mix the tuna with mayo, corn and spring onions.
Split the potatoes, fluff with butter and season.
Pile on the tuna mayo and scatter with cheese.

name: French Onion Pasta
blurb: Deeply caramelised onions, gruyère and stock tossed through pasta.
method: Cook the onions low and slow in the butter and oil for 35-40 minutes until deep brown; add the sugar near the end.
Add the wine and reduce, then the stock and thyme, and simmer 10 minutes.
Cook the pasta and toss through the onion sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Off the heat stir in the cheeses until glossy; season with black pepper.

name: Toad in the Hole with Onion Gravy
blurb: Sausages baked in crisp Yorkshire batter, drowned in onion gravy.
ingredients: Gravy: 2 onions sliced, 1 tbsp flour, 500ml beef stock, splash of Worcestershire
method: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk to a smooth batter and rest 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 220C fan. Put the fat and sausages in a roasting tin for 10 minutes until sizzling.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes without opening the door, until risen and golden.
Caramelise the onions slowly, stir in the flour then the stock and Worcestershire, and simmer to a gravy.

name: Special Fried Rice
blurb: Day-old rice fried with prawns, char siu, egg, peas and spring onion.
ingredients: 150g char siu or cooked ham, diced
2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, white pepper
method: Scramble the eggs in a very hot oiled wok, then remove.
Fry the garlic and peas briefly, add the rice and press to heat through.
Add the prawns, ham, soy, sesame oil and white pepper, and toss.
Return the egg, fold through the spring onions and serve.

name: Chicken Dhansak
blurb: Sweet-and-sour lentil curry with chicken, pumpkin and a hint of pineapple.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin
method: Fry the onion until golden, add garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the lentils, pumpkin and 700ml water and simmer 20 minutes until soft.
Add the chicken and cook 15 minutes.
Stir in tamarind and sugar, blitz half for body, finish with coriander.

name: Beef Massaman Curry
blurb: Mild, rich Thai curry with slow beef, potatoes, peanuts and warm spice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tbsp tamarind
method: Fry the paste in the thick coconut cream with the whole spices for 2 minutes.
Add the beef to coat, then the rest of the coconut milk and 300ml water. Simmer 1.5 hours.
Add the potatoes, onion and peanuts and cook 30 minutes until the beef is tender.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and tamarind; serve with rice.

name: Panang Chicken Curry
blurb: A thick, nutty, slightly sweet red curry with kaffir lime.
ingredients: 3 tbsp panang or red curry paste
2 tsp fish sauce, 1 tsp palm sugar
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the chicken to coat, then the coconut milk and peanut butter.
Simmer 12 minutes, adding the lime leaves.
Season with fish sauce and sugar; finish with Thai basil.

name: Goan Pork Vindaloo
blurb: Fiery, vinegar-sharp pork curry with plenty of chilli and garlic.
ingredients: Marinade: 6 dried Kashmiri chillies, 8 garlic cloves, 3cm ginger, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp black pepper, 4 cloves, 1 tsp cinnamon, 5 tbsp red wine vinegar
method: Blitz the marinade to a paste and coat the pork; leave 2 hours.
Fry the onions until deep golden.
Add the pork and marinade and brown, then add 300ml water.
Cover and simmer 1 hour until tender; balance with the sugar.

name: Thai Red Prawn Curry
blurb: Coconut red curry with prawns, peppers and bamboo shoots.
ingredients: 2 tsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar, juice of 1 lime
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, pepper and bamboo and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes until pink.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and lime; finish with basil.

name: Chicken Korma
blurb: Very mild, sweet and creamy with cashew, coconut and cardamom.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cardamom, cumin, coriander, 1/2 tsp turmeric
method: Fry the onion until soft, add garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the chicken and brown lightly.
Add the cashew paste, cream and coconut milk and simmer gently 20 minutes.
Balance with the sugar; serve with rice or naan.

name: Egg Masala
blurb: Boiled eggs simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy.
ingredients: 1 tsp each turmeric, cumin, coriander, chilli powder
method: Rub the peeled eggs with turmeric and salt and fry until blistered.
Fry the onions until golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a thick masala, then 250ml water and simmer 8 minutes.
Return the eggs, finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: Chickpea & Spinach Curry (Chana Saag)
blurb: Chickpeas and spinach in a quick, spiced tomato sauce.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli
method: Fry the onion until golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook down 8 minutes.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few.
Stir through the spinach and garam masala.

name: Keralan Fish Molee
blurb: White fish poached gently in a mild turmeric-coconut sauce with curry leaves.
ingredients: 600g firm white fish, in large pieces
1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig of curry leaves
400ml coconut milk, juice of half a lime
method: Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, then the onion until soft.
Add garlic, ginger, chilli and turmeric.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes.
Slip in the fish and poach 6-8 minutes; finish with lime.

name: Lamb Saag
blurb: Tender lamb in a silky spiced spinach sauce.
ingredients: 2 tsp each cumin, coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder
method: Brown the lamb, then set aside. Fry the onions until golden, add garlic, ginger and spices.
Return the lamb, stir in the yoghurt a spoon at a time, add 200ml water. Simmer 1.5 hours.
Wilt the spinach with a splash of water and blitz to a purée.
Stir the spinach into the lamb and simmer 15 minutes; finish with garam masala.

name: Thai Yellow Vegetable Curry
blurb: A gentle turmeric-yellow coconut curry with mixed vegetables and tofu.
ingredients: 2 tsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, juice of 1 lime
method: Fry the tofu in oil until golden; set aside.
Fry the paste in a little coconut cream, add the rest with 200ml water.
Add the sweet potato and simmer 10 minutes, then the pepper and beans for 5.
Return the tofu, season with soy, sugar and lime; finish with coriander.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
blurb: Soft paneer in a mild, buttery, tomato-cream makhani sauce.
ingredients: 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp dried fenugreek
method: Fry the paneer in a little butter until golden; set aside.
Melt the butter, fry the onion, then garlic and ginger.
Add the blitzed tomatoes, chilli powder and sugar and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the cream, fenugreek, garam masala and paneer and simmer 5 minutes.

name: Sri Lankan Chicken Curry
blurb: Dark-roasted curry spices, coconut, curry leaf, pandan and lime.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Sri Lankan roasted curry powder
1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig curry leaves, 1 cinnamon stick
method: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp curry powder, salt and pepper.
Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, cinnamon and onion until soft.
Add garlic, ginger, the rest of the curry powder and the tomatoes.
Add the chicken, coconut milk and tamarind, cover and simmer 35 minutes.

name: Aloo Matar (Potato & Pea Curry)
blurb: Potatoes and peas in a simple, homely spiced tomato gravy.
ingredients: 1 tsp each turmeric, coriander, chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the cumin seeds, then the onion until golden.
Add garlic, ginger and ground spices, then the tomatoes and cook to a paste.
Add the potatoes and 300ml water and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the peas for the last 5 minutes; finish with garam masala.

name: Beef Rendang
blurb: Malaysian dry curry — beef slow-cooked in coconut and spice until dark and sticky.
ingredients: Paste: 6 shallots, 6 garlic cloves, 4cm ginger, 3cm galangal, 2 lemongrass, 6 dried chillies
1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves, 3 star anise, 4 lime leaves
method: Blitz the paste and fry in oil with the whole spices until fragrant.
Add the beef to coat, then the coconut milk and lime leaves.
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, for 2-2.5 hours until the liquid has cooked off and the beef is dark.
Stir in the toasted coconut, tamarind and sugar for the last 15 minutes.

name: Tarka Dal
blurb: Yellow lentils cooked soft and finished with a sizzling spiced ghee.
ingredients: Tarka: 3 tbsp ghee or oil, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 4 garlic cloves sliced, 1 dried red chilli, pinch of asafoetida
method: Simmer the lentils with the turmeric and 1 litre water for 25-30 minutes; whisk to a loose porridge and season.
Heat the ghee, add the cumin, then the garlic until pale gold.
Add the dried chilli, asafoetida, tomato and chilli powder and fry 2 minutes.
Pour the tarka over the dal and finish with coriander and lemon.

name: Everyday Chicken Curry
blurb: The reliable, medium-spiced tomato-and-onion chicken curry for any night.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chilli
method: Fry the onions until deep golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook down 8 minutes.
Add the chicken and 200ml water and simmer 20 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: South Indian Prawn Coconut Curry
blurb: Prawns in a tangy, chilli-flecked coconut sauce with curry leaves.
ingredients: 1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig curry leaves
1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp turmeric
method: Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, then the onion.
Add garlic, ginger, chilli powder and turmeric, then the tomatoes.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes until pink.

name: Thai Jungle Curry (Gaeng Pa)
blurb: A fiery, brothy curry with no coconut — just chilli, herbs and vegetables.
ingredients: 3 tbsp jungle or red curry paste
150g green beans, 1 courgette, 100g baby corn, 1 bamboo tin
2 tbsp fish sauce, handful of Thai basil and green peppercorns
method: Fry the paste in a little oil until fragrant.
Add the chicken to coat, then the stock.
Add the vegetables and simmer 8 minutes.
Season with fish sauce; finish with basil and peppercorns.

name: Chicken Chettinad
blurb: Peppery, roasted-spice South Indian curry with plenty of black pepper.
ingredients: Spice roast: 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tbsp black pepper, 1 tsp fennel, 4 dried chillies, 3 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 tbsp desiccated coconut
method: Dry-roast the spice mix until fragrant, then grind.
Fry the onions until golden with curry leaves, add garlic and ginger.
Add the ground spice mix and tomatoes and cook to a paste.
Add the chicken and 200ml water, cover and simmer 30 minutes.

name: Sweet Potato & Lentil Curry
blurb: Red lentils and sweet potato simmered soft with coconut and warm spice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric
150g spinach, juice of half a lime
method: Fry the onion, garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the lentils, sweet potato, coconut milk, tomatoes and 300ml water.
Simmer 25 minutes until the lentils collapse and the potato is soft.
Stir through the spinach and lime.

name: Methi Chicken (Chicken with Fenugreek)
blurb: A medium curry with a distinctive slightly bitter, aromatic fenugreek note.
ingredients: 1 tsp each turmeric, cumin, coriander, chilli
method: Fry the onions until golden, add garlic, ginger and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a paste, then stir in the yoghurt.
Add the chicken and 150ml water and simmer 20 minutes.
Crush in the fenugreek and add garam masala for the last 5 minutes.

name: Sweet Potato Katsu Curry
blurb: Panko sweet potato slabs with a mild Japanese curry sauce and rice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp flour, 1 tbsp garam masala
500ml vegetable stock, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp maple
method: Steam the sweet potato slabs for 6 minutes until just tender; cool.
Soften the onion and carrot, add garlic, ginger and spices, then the flour.
Whisk in the stock, soy and maple; simmer 15 minutes and blitz smooth.
Coat the slabs in flour, milk and panko and shallow fry until golden; serve with rice and sauce.

name: Lamb Keema Pav
blurb: Buttery toasted rolls with rich spiced lamb mince and peas.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the cumin seeds, then the onion until golden; add garlic and ginger.
Add the mince and brown, then the ground spices and tomatoes; cook 8 minutes.
Add 150ml water and simmer 10 minutes, adding the peas for the last 5.
Toast buttered rolls in a pan and serve alongside the keema to scoop.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
blurb: Charred marinated chicken in a creamy, mildly spiced tomato gravy. The nation's favourite.
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt and tikka spice, then grill until charred.
Fry the onions and ginger-garlic, add the passata and garam masala and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the cream and chicken and warm through; serve with rice.

name: Lamb Rogan Josh
blurb: Slow lamb in an aromatic Kashmiri-style sauce deep with dried chilli, fennel and cardamom.
method: Brown the lamb, fry the onions until soft, add the ginger-garlic and spices.
Add the tomatoes and yoghurt a spoon at a time, then the lamb.
Cover and simmer 1.5 hours until tender and the oil rises.

name: Saag Paneer
blurb: Fried paneer folded into a silky spiced spinach purée with garlic, ginger and cream.
method: Fry the paneer in the butter until golden, set aside.
Wilt and blend the spinach; fry the onions with the spices, add the spinach purée.
Stir in the cream and paneer and simmer 5 minutes.

name: Chana Dal Tadka
blurb: Split chickpea lentils cooked soft, finished with a sizzling ghee tempering of cumin, garlic and chilli.
method: Boil the dal with the turmeric until soft, about 40 minutes.
Fry the onions, ginger-garlic and tomatoes to a masala and stir into the dal.
Heat the oil, sizzle the cumin, sliced garlic and chillies, and pour over the dal.

name: Goan Pork Vindaloo
blurb: Pork marinated in a fiery, tangy vinegar-and-chilli paste and slow-cooked until unctuous.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp black pepper, 6 cloves
method: Blend the soaked chillies, vinegar, spices, garlic and ginger to a paste and marinate the pork for a few hours.
Fry the onions until golden, add the pork and its marinade.
Add a little water and simmer 1.5 hours until the sauce is thick and clinging.

name: Chicken Chettinad
blurb: A dark, peppery South Indian curry with roasted spices, coconut and curry leaves.
method: Dry-roast the coconut, pepper, coriander, fennel and chillies, then grind.
Fry the onions, ginger-garlic and tomatoes, add the ground masala.
Add the chicken and a splash of water and simmer 30 minutes; finish with fried curry leaves.

name: Prawn Malai Curry
blurb: Bengali prawns in a gentle, sweet coconut-milk gravy scented with cardamom and cinnamon.
method: Toss the prawns in turmeric and salt and fry briefly, remove.
Fry the whole spices, add the onion paste and ginger-garlic and cook until golden.
Add the coconut milk and sugar, simmer, then return the prawns for 4 minutes.

name: Punjabi Dhaba Chicken Curry
blurb: A rustic bone-in chicken curry in a robust onion-tomato masala, the kind roadside dhabas serve.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric
method: Fry the onions in the oil until deep brown, add the ginger-garlic and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a thick, oily masala.
Add the chicken and a cup of water and simmer 30 minutes; finish with garam masala.

name: Baingan Bharta
blurb: Aubergines charred over the flame, mashed and cooked with onion, tomato, ginger and peas.
method: Char the aubergines directly on the flame or under the grill until collapsed, then peel and mash.
Fry the cumin, onions, ginger-garlic and chilli, add the tomatoes and cook down.
Add the aubergine and peas and cook 10 minutes; finish with coriander.

name: Kerala Fish Molee
blurb: White fish poached in a pale, fragrant coconut curry with ginger, green chilli and curry leaves.
method: Soften the onions, ginger and chilli without colouring, add the turmeric and curry leaves.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Slide in the fish and tomato and poach 6-8 minutes.

name: Aloo Gobi
blurb: Potato and cauliflower cooked dry with turmeric, cumin, ginger and tomato until tender at the edges.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander
method: Fry the cumin, onions and ginger-garlic, add the ground spices.
Add the potato, cauliflower and tomatoes, cover and cook 25 minutes, stirring gently.
Uncover to dry out and finish with fresh coriander.

name: Chicken Dopiaza
blurb: Chicken with a double hit of onions — some cooked into the sauce, some added in chunks at the end.
method: Fry the sliced onions until brown, add the ginger-garlic, spices and tomatoes.
Add the chicken and a splash of water and simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in the onion chunks for the last 8 minutes so they keep some bite.

name: Mattar Paneer
blurb: Paneer and peas in a mild, tomatoey cashew-thickened gravy. A gentle, family-friendly curry.
method: Blend the onions, tomatoes and cashews.
Fry the cumin, add the paste and spices and cook until thick and glossy.
Add the peas, paneer and cream and simmer 8 minutes.

name: Beef Madras
blurb: A fierce, tangy South Indian-style beef curry with plenty of chilli and a hit of tamarind.
method: Brown the beef, fry the onions and ginger-garlic, add the spices.
Add the tomatoes and tamarind and return the beef.
Cover and simmer 1.5 hours until the beef is tender and the sauce is deep red.

name: Tarka Dal
blurb: Yellow split lentils cooked to a soft porridge, finished with a ghee tempering of garlic, cumin and chilli.
method: Boil the dal with the turmeric and tomato until collapsing, about 30 minutes; whisk smooth.
Heat the ghee and sizzle the cumin, garlic, chilli and asafoetida until golden.
Pour the tarka over the dal and stir through with coriander.

name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
blurb: Tandoori-style chicken in a smooth, buttery tomato-cream sauce with fenugreek and honey.
method: Marinate and grill the chicken until charred.
Fry the ginger-garlic in the butter, add the passata and simmer 20 minutes, then blend smooth.
Add the cream, fenugreek, honey and chicken and warm gently.

name: Vegetable Korma
blurb: Mixed vegetables in a mild, creamy almond-and-coconut sauce scented with cardamom.
method: Fry the whole spices and onions until soft, add the korma paste.
Add the firmer veg with a splash of water and cook 10 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk, almonds, remaining veg and yoghurt and simmer to tender.

name: Lamb Nihari
blurb: A slow, deeply spiced lamb shank stew thickened with wheat flour, finished with ginger and lime.
ingredients: julienned ginger, green chilli and lime to serve
method: Brown the shanks, add the fried onions, ginger-garlic and nihari masala.
Add the water and simmer very gently for 3 hours until the meat is falling off.
Slake the flour in water, stir in and cook 20 minutes to thicken; serve with the garnishes.

name: South Indian Egg Kurma
blurb: Boiled eggs in a coconut and poppy-seed gravy with fennel and curry leaves, for rice or dosa.
method: Grind the coconut, poppy seeds and cashews with a little water to a paste.
Fry the fennel, onions, ginger-garlic and tomatoes, add the paste and cook.
Add water to a gravy, slip in the halved eggs and simmer 8 minutes.

name: Chicken Jalfrezi
blurb: A hot, dry-ish stir-fried curry with peppers, onions, green chilli and a punchy tomato base.
method: Sear the chicken hard, remove.
Stir-fry the onions and peppers, add the ginger-garlic, chillies, spices and tomatoes.
Return the chicken and cook fast until the sauce clings and everything is glossy.

name: Rajma (Kidney Bean Curry)
blurb: Red kidney beans simmered in a thick, spiced onion-tomato gravy. Punjabi comfort with rice.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the onions until deep brown, add the ginger-garlic and ground spices.
Add the blended tomatoes and cook to a thick masala.
Add the beans and a cup of water, mash some to thicken, simmer 20 minutes.

name: Methi Chicken
blurb: Chicken cooked with fresh and dried fenugreek for a slightly bitter, deeply savoury curry.
ingredients: 200g fresh methi (fenugreek) leaves, or 3 tbsp dried
method: Fry the onions and ginger-garlic, add the spices and tomatoes.
Add the chicken and yoghurt and cook 20 minutes.
Stir in the methi and cook 10 minutes more until the oil separates.

name: Prawn & Pepper Balti
