blurb: Quick-cooked prawns and peppers in a bright, tomatoey balti sauce, served straight from the pan.
method: Fry the onions and peppers, add the ginger-garlic, balti paste and cumin.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a thick sauce.
Stir in the prawns and cook 4 minutes; finish with coriander and lemon.

name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
blurb: Baby potatoes fried and simmered in a spiced yoghurt gravy rich with fennel and Kashmiri chilli.
method: Parboil, peel and prick the potatoes, then fry until golden.
Whisk the yoghurt with the spices; warm the oil with the asafoetida.
Add the yoghurt mix carefully, then the potatoes and a little water, and simmer 20 minutes.

name: Chicken Xacuti
blurb: A Goan curry of chicken in a dark, complex roasted-coconut and spice paste with nutmeg and star anise.
ingredients: 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin, 6 cloves, 1 star anise, pinch nutmeg
method: Dry-roast the coconut and whole spices, then grind with a little water.
Fry the onions and ginger-garlic until brown, add the paste and cook out.
Add the chicken, tamarind and water and simmer 35 minutes.

name: Palak Dal (Spinach Lentils)
blurb: Yellow lentils cooked with spinach, garlic and cumin — light, green and quietly nourishing.
method: Boil the dal with the turmeric and tomato until soft.
Stir the chopped spinach through and cook 5 minutes.
Temper the cumin, garlic and chilli in the oil and pour over.

name: Lamb Bhuna
blurb: Lamb slow-fried in its own spiced masala until the sauce reduces to a thick, glossy coating.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric
method: Fry the onions until brown, add the ginger-garlic and ground spices.
Add the lamb and tomatoes and cook, stirring often, adding splashes of water.
Keep 'bhuna-ing' for an hour until the lamb is tender and the sauce is dark and thick.

name: Vegetable Jalfrezi
blurb: A dry, spicy stir-fried curry of peppers, onion, cauliflower and green beans in a punchy tomato base.
method: Stir-fry the onions and peppers hard, add the ginger-garlic, chilli and spices.
Add the cauliflower and beans with a splash of water and cook 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and fry until the sauce is thick and clinging.

name: Mangalorean Fish Curry
blurb: White fish in a bright red, tangy curry of roasted coconut, Kashmiri chilli and tamarind.
method: Grind the coconut, chillies, coriander, cumin and tamarind with water to a smooth paste.
Fry the onions and ginger-garlic, add the paste and cook out, then loosen with water.
Simmer 10 minutes, slide in the fish and cook 6-8 minutes.

name: Chole (Amritsari Chickpeas)
blurb: Chickpeas simmered dark with tea, pomegranate seeds and a robust blend of ground spices.
method: Simmer the chickpeas with the tea bag and a little bicarb for 20 minutes, then discard the bag.
Fry the onions dark, add the ginger-garlic, spices and tomatoes and cook to a thick masala.
Add the chickpeas with their liquid and simmer 20 minutes, mashing some to thicken.

name: Shahi Chicken Korma
blurb: A rich, pale Mughlai korma with cashews, cream, saffron and cardamom — a wedding-feast curry.
method: Fry the whole spices, add the ginger-garlic and the fried-onion paste.
Add the chicken and yoghurt a spoon at a time, then the cashew paste and a little water.
Simmer 25 minutes, then finish with the cream and saffron.

name: Bhindi Masala
blurb: Okra cooked dry with onion, tomato and amchur so it stays firm and not slimy. A great side-turned-main.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1/2 tsp turmeric
method: Fry the okra in hot oil for 8 minutes until it stops being sticky, remove.
Fry the onions, ginger-garlic, spices and tomatoes to a masala.
Return the okra, add the amchur and cook 5 minutes uncovered.

name: Lamb Keema Matar
blurb: Spiced minced lamb cooked down with peas and tomato until rich. Great with naan or over rice.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the onions and ginger-garlic, add the spices and lamb and brown hard.
Add the tomatoes and a splash of water and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in the peas and cook 8 minutes; finish with garam masala.

name: Paneer Tikka Masala
blurb: Charred marinated paneer in the same creamy tomato gravy as the chicken version. Fully vegetarian.
method: Marinate the paneer and peppers in the yoghurt and tikka spice and grill until charred.
Fry the onions and ginger-garlic, add the passata and garam masala and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the cream, paneer and peppers and warm through.

name: Grilled Fish Tikka Curry
blurb: Chunks of marinated grilled fish added to a light, spiced tomato-onion gravy at the end.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Marinate the fish in the yoghurt and tandoori spice, then grill until lightly charred.
Fry the onions, ginger-garlic, spices and tomatoes to a thin gravy.
Fold the grilled fish in gently and simmer 3 minutes.

name: Vegetable Makhani
blurb: Mixed vegetables and paneer in the buttery, silky tomato-cream makhani sauce.
method: Fry the ginger-garlic in the butter, add the passata and simmer 20 minutes, then blend.
Steam or boil the veg until just tender.
Combine with the sauce, paneer, cream, fenugreek and honey and simmer 5 minutes.

name: Chicken Saag
blurb: Chicken simmered in a spiced spinach purée with ginger and garlic. Iron-rich and comforting.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the onions and ginger-garlic, add the spices and tomatoes.
Add the chicken and cook 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach purée and simmer 15 minutes more.

name: Restaurant-Style Yellow Dal
blurb: A rich dal built on a fried onion-tomato masala with butter, cream and a double tempering.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, 4 garlic cloves, 2 dried chillies for the tarka
method: Boil the dal with turmeric until soft and whisk smooth.
Fry the onions, ginger-garlic and tomatoes in butter to a glossy masala and stir into the dal with the cream.
Finish with a hot tarka of cumin, garlic and chilli, and a pinch of crushed kasuri methi.

name: Lamb Dhansak
blurb: A Parsi curry of lamb and lentils, sweet-sour with pumpkin, tamarind and a hint of jaggery.
method: Simmer the lamb until nearly tender, about 1 hour.
Cook the lentils and pumpkin separately until soft, then blend.
Fry the onions, ginger-garlic and dhansak masala, add the lamb, lentil purée, tamarind and jaggery and simmer 30 minutes.

name: Aloo Matar
blurb: Potatoes and peas in a simple, homely tomato-onion gravy. A weeknight vegetarian curry.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp coriander, 1/2 tsp turmeric
method: Fry the cumin, onions and ginger-garlic, add the ground spices and tomatoes.
Add the potatoes and a cup of water, cover and cook 15 minutes.
Add the peas and cook 8 minutes more; finish with garam masala.

name: Chicken Kolhapuri
blurb: A fiery Maharashtrian curry with a dark roasted-coconut and sesame masala. Not for the faint-hearted.
ingredients: 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin, 6 cloves, 1 tsp black pepper
method: Dry-roast the coconut, sesame, whole spices and chillies, then grind to a paste.
Fry the onions and ginger-garlic until brown, add the paste and cook out.
Add the chicken and water and simmer 30 minutes.

name: Vegetable Kootu
blurb: A gentle South Indian lentil and vegetable stew with coconut, cumin and curry leaves.
method: Cook the dal with the turmeric until soft, add the chopped veg and cook until tender.
Grind the coconut, cumin and chilli with water and stir in, simmer 5 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil and pour over.

name: Slow Goat Curry
blurb: Bone-in goat simmered for hours in a robust onion-tomato masala until it slips off the bone.
method: Brown the goat, fry the onions dark, add the ginger-garlic, whole and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and yoghurt and cook to a thick masala.
Add the goat and water and simmer, covered, for 2.5 hours until falling apart.

name: Coconut Red Lentil Curry
blurb: Red lentils simmered with coconut milk, tomato, ginger and lime — a soothing bowl in half an hour.
ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the onions and ginger with the spices.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and 300ml water and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in a few handfuls of spinach and finish with lime.

name: Chicken Cafreal
blurb: Goan chicken marinated in a vivid green paste of coriander, chilli, ginger and spice, then pan-fried.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 6 cloves, 1 tsp peppercorns, 1 cinnamon stick
method: Blend the coriander, chilli, ginger, garlic, spices, vinegar and sugar to a green paste.
Marinate the chicken for a few hours.
Pan-fry gently in a covered pan for 25 minutes, turning, until cooked and the paste has caramelised.

name: Peas Pulao with Quick Curry
blurb: Fragrant whole-spice rice with peas, alongside a fast tomato-onion vegetable curry.
method: Fry the whole spices, add the rice and peas, then hot water, cover and steam 12 minutes.
For the curry, fry the onions, ginger-garlic and curry powder, add the tomatoes and yoghurt.
Add the veg and a splash of water and simmer until tender; serve with the pulao.

name: Kadai Chicken
blurb: Chicken tossed with peppers and onions in a coarse, freshly ground coriander-and-chilli masala.
ingredients: 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 4 dried chillies, coarsely ground
method: Fry the ginger-garlic and the coarse coriander-chilli grind, add the tomatoes and cook down.
Add the chicken and cook 15 minutes, then the peppers and onion chunks.
Cook fast until the sauce clings; finish with kasuri methi and garam masala.

name: Vegetable Sambar
blurb: A tangy, soupy South Indian lentil and vegetable stew with tamarind and roasted sambar powder.
method: Cook the dal with the turmeric until soft, mash smooth.
Simmer the vegetables with the tamarind, tomato and sambar powder until tender, then add the dal and loosen with water.
Temper mustard seeds, chillies and curry leaves in oil and pour over.

name: Coconut Prawn & Spinach Curry
blurb: Quick prawns and spinach in a lightly spiced coconut curry with lime and coriander. Thirty minutes.
method: Fry the onions and ginger, add the curry paste and cook out.
Add the coconut milk and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the prawns and spinach, cook 4 minutes, finish with lime and coriander.

name: Steak for Two with Peppercorn Sauce
blurb: A shared sirloin rested and sliced, with a brandy-cream peppercorn sauce and skinny fries.
ingredients: oven fries and watercress to serve
method: Fry the seasoned steak to your liking, rest under foil.
Soften the shallot in the pan, add the brandy and flame off, then the crushed peppercorns, cream and Dijon.
Slice the steak, pour over the sauce, serve with fries and watercress.

name: Seared Scallops with Black Pudding
blurb: Plump scallops and crumbled black pudding on pea purée — a restaurant starter, at home.
method: Blitz cooked peas with butter, mint and a splash of water to a purée; keep warm.
Fry the black pudding until crisp, remove.
Sear the dry scallops 90 seconds a side in the same pan, finish with lemon and plate on the purée with the pudding.

name: Wild Mushroom & Truffle Risotto
blurb: A slow, glossy risotto of mixed mushrooms finished with Parmesan and a little truffle oil.
method: Fry the fresh mushrooms until golden, set aside; soften the shallot, toast the rice, add the wine.
Add stock a ladle at a time with the chopped porcini and its liquid, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Beat in the butter, Parmesan and mushrooms, rest, and finish each plate with a few drops of truffle oil.

name: Pan-Roasted Duck Breast with Cherry Sauce
blurb: Crisp-skinned duck breast, rested pink, sliced into a port and cherry sauce.
method: Start the duck skin-side down in a cold pan, render 8 minutes, flip 3, then roast at 200C for 6; rest.
Pour off the fat, add the port and reduce, then the stock, cherries, vinegar and honey and simmer to a syrup.
Slice the duck and serve in the sauce.

name: Lobster Linguine for Two
blurb: A whole lobster picked into a garlic, chilli, tomato and white-wine sauce with linguine.
method: Pick all the lobster meat and chop; keep the shells to infuse the oil briefly over low heat.
Fry the garlic and chilli in the strained oil, add the tomatoes and wine and reduce.
Toss the cooked linguine and lobster through with parsley, lemon and a little pasta water.

name: Roast Châteaubriand with Béarnaise
blurb: A thick centre-cut fillet roasted to blushing pink, carved for two, with a proper béarnaise.
method: Sear the fillet on all sides, roast at 200C for 12-15 minutes to 50C, rest 10.
Reduce the vinegar with the shallot and tarragon stalks, strain, whisk into the yolks over a bain-marie, then trickle in the butter.
Fold chopped tarragon into the sauce; carve the beef thickly.

name: Sizzling Garlic Chilli Prawns to Share
blurb: Prawns cooked hot in garlic, chilli and sherry, brought to the table still spitting, with bread to mop.
method: Warm the oil with the garlic, chilli and paprika until fragrant.
Add the prawns and fry 2 minutes, add the sherry and bubble 1 minute.
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread.

name: Rib-Eye with Café de Paris Butter
blurb: A well-marbled rib-eye rested and sliced under a melting herb-and-anchovy butter.
method: Mash the butter with the finely chopped anchovies, capers, herbs, Dijon and curry powder; chill in a log.
Fry the steak to your liking and rest 8 minutes.
Slice, top with coins of the butter, serve with fries and a sharp salad.

name: Coquilles Saint-Jacques
blurb: Scallops in a creamy white-wine sauce, piped with potato and glazed golden under the grill.
method: Poach the scallops briefly in the wine and stock, remove; make a sauce with the butter, flour, poaching liquid and cream.
Divide scallops between shells or dishes, coat in sauce, pipe a border of mash.
Scatter with Gruyère and grill until bubbling and browned.

name: Veal Escalopes Marsala
blurb: Thin veal escalopes pan-fried and finished in a glossy Marsala and mushroom sauce.
method: Dust the veal and fry 90 seconds a side, remove.
Fry the mushrooms in the same pan, add the Marsala and reduce, then the stock.
Swirl in the butter, return the veal to warm through, finish with parsley.

name: Cheese Fondue for Two
blurb: Gruyère and Emmental melted with white wine and kirsch, for dipping bread, potatoes and cornichons.
ingredients: baguette, boiled baby potatoes and cornichons to dip
method: Rub the pot with garlic, warm the wine, then melt in the cheese a handful at a time.
Stir in the cornflour slaked with the kirsch until glossy and thick.
Keep warm over a low flame and dip everything.

name: Squid Ink Risotto with Prawns
blurb: A dramatic black risotto with sweet prawns and a squeeze of lemon. Serves two, impresses greatly.
method: Soften the shallot, toast the rice, add the wine.
Add stock gradually with the squid ink, stirring, for 18 minutes.
Stir in the prawns for the last 3 minutes, beat in the butter, finish with lemon and parsley.

name: Beef Bourguignon
blurb: Beef braised in red wine with bacon, baby onions and mushrooms until spoonably tender. Deeply romantic.
method: Brown the beef in batches, fry the lardons, shallots and mushrooms and set aside.
Deglaze with the wine, add the stock, purée and bouquet garni, return the beef.
Braise at 150C for 2.5 hours, add the garnish back for the last 30 minutes; serve on mash.

name: Roast Halibut with Beurre Blanc
blurb: A meaty halibut steak roasted and served with a sharp, buttery white-wine sauce and samphire.
method: Reduce the vinegar, wine and shallot to a couple of spoonfuls, then whisk in the cold butter piece by piece off the heat.
Sear the halibut, then roast at 200C for 6-8 minutes.
Blanch the samphire, plate the fish with the potatoes and pour over the beurre blanc.

name: Porcini Tagliatelle
blurb: Fresh tagliatelle in a cream sauce heavy with soaked porcini and Parmesan. Twenty-five minutes to swoon.
ingredients: 25g dried porcini, soaked in 200ml hot water
method: Fry the shallot in the butter, add the chopped porcini and 100ml of the strained soaking liquid.
Add the cream and reduce for 5 minutes.
Toss the cooked pasta through with the Parmesan and parsley, loosening with pasta water.

name: Moules Frites for Two
blurb: A big pot of mussels steamed in white wine, garlic and cream, with a bowl of hot fries and mayo.
ingredients: oven fries and mayonnaise to serve
method: Sweat the shallots and garlic in the butter, add the wine and bring to the boil.
Tip in the mussels, cover and steam 4 minutes until open, discard any that stay shut.
Stir in the cream and parsley and serve with the fries.

name: Homemade Chicken Kiev
blurb: Chicken breast wrapped around garlic-parsley butter, crumbed and fried so it bursts when cut.
ingredients: buttered greens and mash to serve
method: Beat the butter with the garlic and parsley, shape into two logs and freeze firm.
Cut a pocket in each breast, insert the butter, seal and chill; coat in flour, egg then panko twice.
Shallow-fry until golden, then finish in the oven at 190C for 12 minutes.

name: Grilled Lamb Cutlets with Salsa Verde
blurb: Quick-grilled cutlets with a punchy herb, caper and anchovy salsa verde and crushed potatoes.
ingredients: big handful parsley, mint and basil
method: Blitz the herbs, capers, anchovy, garlic, Dijon, oil and vinegar to a loose salsa verde.
Griddle the seasoned cutlets 2-3 minutes a side, rest.
Crush the boiled potatoes with oil and serve with the cutlets and plenty of salsa verde.

name: Crab Linguine
blurb: White and brown crab meat tossed through linguine with chilli, lemon and parsley. Light but luxe.
method: Gently warm the garlic and chilli in the oil, stir in the brown crab meat and a splash of pasta water.
Toss the cooked linguine through, then fold in the white crab, lemon and parsley off the heat.
Serve at once, no cheese.

name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Pork Fillet with Marsala
blurb: Pork fillet wrapped in prosciutto and sage, roasted and sliced into a Marsala pan sauce.
ingredients: roast potatoes and greens to serve
method: Wrap the seasoned pork in prosciutto with sage tucked under, tie loosely.
Sear all over, then roast at 200C for 15 minutes; rest.
Deglaze with the Marsala, add the stock, reduce, swirl in butter and slice the pork into it.

name: Sole Meunière
blurb: A whole Dover sole floured and fried in foaming butter, finished with lemon and parsley. Minimal, perfect.
method: Dust the sole in seasoned flour.
Fry in a little butter 3-4 minutes a side until golden, plate up.
Add the rest of the butter to the pan, cook to nut-brown, add lemon juice and parsley and pour over.

name: Gnocchi with Gorgonzola & Walnut
blurb: Soft gnocchi in a quick Gorgonzola cream with toasted walnuts and a little sage. Rich and ready fast.
method: Boil the gnocchi until they float, drain.
Melt the Gorgonzola into the cream with the sage, season with pepper.
Toss the gnocchi through and scatter with walnuts and a little butter-fried sage.

name: Tuna Tataki with Ponzu
blurb: Sesame-crusted tuna seared rare, sliced thin, with a ponzu dressing and pickled ginger. A cool, sharp starter-as-main.
method: Press the tuna into the sesame seeds, sear 20 seconds on each side in a very hot pan.
Rest 2 minutes, then slice thinly.
Fan over rice, spoon over the ponzu and sesame oil and top with ginger and spring onion.

name: Chicken Supreme with Tarragon Cream
blurb: A skin-on chicken breast pan-roasted crisp, in a white-wine, tarragon and crème fraîche sauce.
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down, then roast at 200C for 12 minutes; rest.
Soften the shallot in the pan, add the wine and reduce, then the crème fraîche and tarragon.
Slice the chicken and serve in the sauce.

name: Saffron Risotto Milanese
blurb: A luminous yellow risotto rich with bone marrow, saffron and Parmesan. The classic partner to osso buco, lovely alone.
method: Steep the saffron in a little warm stock.
Soften the shallot, toast the rice, add the wine, then stock a ladle at a time for 18 minutes, adding the saffron stock halfway.
Beat in the butter and Parmesan hard, rest 2 minutes, serve loose.

name: Baked Camembert & Charcuterie for Two
blurb: A molten studded Camembert with cured meats, cornichons, grapes and warm bread. A grazing dinner.
method: Score the cheese, stud with garlic and rosemary, drizzle with honey.
Bake in its box at 180C for 18 minutes until molten.
Serve in the centre of a board with the meats, pickles, grapes and warm bread.

name: Tournedos Rossini
blurb: Fillet steaks on croutons, topped with pâté and a Madeira sauce — decadent and unapologetic.
ingredients: 2 slices brioche, cut into rounds and fried
method: Fry the steaks to rare-medium, rest.
Deglaze with the Madeira, add the stock and reduce to a glaze, mount with butter.
Sit each steak on a fried brioche round, top with a slice of pâté and spoon over the sauce.

name: King Prawn & Lemon Risotto
blurb: A bright, elegant risotto with sweet prawns, lemon zest and a knob of chilli butter to finish.
method: Soften the shallot, toast the rice, add the wine, then stock gradually for 18 minutes.
Stir in the prawns for the last 3 minutes with most of the lemon.
Beat in butter mashed with the chilli and remaining zest, finish with parsley.

name: Tomato & Shallot Tarte Tatin
blurb: Caramelised shallots and cherry tomatoes baked under puff pastry, flipped out glistening. A showy veggie main.
ingredients: goat's cheese and salad to serve
method: Caramelise the shallots cut-side down in the butter and sugar in an oven-proof pan, add the tomatoes, balsamic and thyme.
Lay the pastry over, tucking in the edges, and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, invert onto a plate, crumble over goat's cheese.

name: Pan-Roast Lamb Loin with Dauphinoise
blurb: A quick-cooking lamb loin fillet, sliced pink, with a small dish of creamy garlic potatoes.
method: Layer the potatoes with the cream, milk and garlic in a dish and bake at 170C for 1 hour until soft and golden.
Sear the seasoned lamb 3-4 minutes a side, rest 8 minutes.
Slice the lamb, serve with the dauphinoise and a spoon of redcurrant jelly.

name: Surf & Turf: Steak with Garlic Butter Prawns
blurb: A rested sirloin sliced alongside prawns fried in garlic-parsley butter. The classic date-night splurge.
method: Fry the seasoned steak to your liking, rest under foil.
In the same pan melt the butter with the garlic, add the prawns and fry 2 minutes, finish with parsley and lemon.
Slice the steak, pile on the prawns, serve with chips.

name: Individual Mushroom Wellingtons
blurb: Two neat puff-pastry parcels of garlic mushrooms, spinach and blue cheese. A vegetarian date-night main.
method: Fry the shallot, garlic and mushrooms until dry, wilt in the spinach, cool, then fold in the blue cheese.
Divide between two pastry squares, fold into parcels, seal, glaze and score.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until deep golden.

name: Linguine alle Vongole
blurb: Clams opened in garlic, white wine and chilli, tossed through linguine with parsley. Fast and special.
method: Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli, add the clams and wine, cover and steam 3-4 minutes until open.
Add the just-undercooked linguine and a little pasta water and toss until coated.
Finish with parsley; discard any unopened clams.

name: Chicken in a Champagne Cream Sauce
blurb: Chicken breasts in a sparkling-wine, shallot and cream sauce with grapes. Quietly celebratory.
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down, then roast at 200C for 12 minutes; rest.
Soften the shallots in the pan, add the wine and reduce by half, then the cream and grapes.
Finish with tarragon and serve the sliced chicken in the sauce.

name: Twice-Baked Cheese Soufflés
blurb: Light cheese soufflés baked, turned out, then baked again in cream so they can be made ahead for two.
method: Make a thick sauce with the butter, cornflour and milk, beat in the cheese, yolks, Dijon and cayenne.
Fold in whisked whites, bake in buttered ramekins in a bain-marie at 190C for 15 minutes, then cool and turn out.
Sit in a dish, pour over the cream, scatter more cheese and bake again at 200C for 12-15 minutes; serve with leaves.

name: Pan-Roast Venison with Blackberry Sauce
blurb: Lean venison loin seared and rested rare, in a sharp red-wine and blackberry sauce with celeriac mash.
method: Sear the seasoned venison 2 minutes a side, rest 8 minutes (it wants to stay rare).
Deglaze with the wine, add the stock, jelly, balsamic and half the blackberries and reduce to a syrup.
Whisk in butter and the rest of the berries, slice the venison into the sauce.

name: Truffle Mac & Cheese for Two
blurb: A small, decadent dish of macaroni in a Gruyère and mascarpone sauce with truffle, baked with a crumb.
method: Cook the macaroni. Make a roux, whisk in the milk, melt in the Gruyère, mascarpone and truffle paste.
Fold in the pasta, tip into two dishes, top with panko and Parmesan.
Bake at 200C for 18 minutes until bubbling and golden.

name: Crispy-Skin Sea Bream with Brown Shrimp Butter
blurb: Sea bream fillets fried skin-side crisp, finished with a nutty brown-shrimp butter over crushed potatoes.
method: Fry the bream skin-side down, pressing, for 3 minutes, flip for 1, plate on the crushed potatoes.
Wipe the pan, cook the butter to nut-brown, add the shrimps, capers, lemon and parsley.
Spoon the shrimp butter over the fish.

name: Chicken Liver Parfait with Toast & Chutney
blurb: A silky, boozy parfait set under butter, spread thick on hot toast with fruit chutney. A rich light supper.
method: Reduce the brandy, port and shallot to a glaze, cool.
Blend the livers, eggs, glaze and warm melted butter until smooth, sieve, pour into a terrine.
Bake in a bain-marie at 140C for 40 minutes until just set, chill, seal with clarified butter and serve with toast and chutney.

name: Pan-Fried Gnocchi, Brown Butter, Sage & Amaretti
blurb: Crisp gnocchi in nut-brown butter with sage and a crushed amaretti rubble over squash purée.
ingredients: 300g roasted squash, blended with a little stock
method: Warm the squash purée and spread on plates.
Fry the gnocchi in a little oil until crisp, add the butter and sage and cook to nut-brown.
Pile the gnocchi on the purée, spoon over the butter, scatter with amaretti and Parmesan.

name: Fillet Steak with Blue Cheese Sauce
blurb: Two petite fillet steaks rested and sauced with a quick Stilton cream, alongside triple-cooked chips.
method: Fry the seasoned fillets to your liking, rest 8 minutes.
Soften the shallot in the pan, add the wine and reduce, then the cream and crumbled Stilton.
Pour the sauce over the steaks and serve with chips and rocket.

name: Spring Vegetable Risotto
blurb: A delicate risotto of asparagus, peas and broad beans finished with lemon, mint and mascarpone.
method: Soften the shallot, toast the rice, add the wine, then stock gradually for 16 minutes.
Add the asparagus, peas and beans for the last 4 minutes.
Beat in the mascarpone, Parmesan, lemon and mint and serve loose.

name: Pork Schnitzel with Lemon & Caper Butter
blurb: Thin, golden crumbed pork with a sharp caper-butter sauce and a lightly dressed potato salad.
method: Coat the pork in flour, egg then crumbs.
Shallow-fry 2-3 minutes a side until deep golden, drain.
Brown the butter, add the capers, lemon and parsley and pour over the schnitzels.

name: Roast Lamb Rump with Anchovy & Rosemary
blurb: A lamb rump studded with anchovy and rosemary, roasted pink and sliced over white bean purée.
method: Make small cuts in the lamb and push in slivers of anchovy, garlic and rosemary; sear fat-side down.
Roast at 200C for 12-15 minutes to pink, rest 8 minutes.
Warm the beans with garlic, lemon and oil and blitz to a purée; slice the lamb over it and add pan juices.

name: Prawn Tempura with Dipping Sauce
blurb: Feather-light battered prawns and vegetables with a warm soy-dashi dipping sauce. A crisp, sharing starter-main.
ingredients: 100ml dashi, 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp mirin for the sauce
method: Whisk the yolk, water and flour just to a lumpy batter; heat the oil to 180C.
Dip the prawns and veg and fry in batches until pale gold and crisp, drain.
Warm the dashi, soy and mirin, add grated daikon and serve for dipping.

name: Chicken Diane
blurb: Flattened chicken in a retro pan sauce of mushrooms, mustard, brandy, Worcestershire and cream.
method: Fry the seasoned chicken 3-4 minutes a side, remove.
Fry the shallot and mushrooms in the butter, add the brandy and flame off.
Stir in the Dijon, Worcestershire and cream, return the chicken to coat, serve on mash.

name: Oysters Rockefeller
blurb: Oysters baked under a buttery spinach, herb and Parmesan crust — a hot, briny opener for two.
ingredients: 12 oysters, shucked, on the half shell
method: Soften the shallot in the butter, add the spinach and herbs, then the Pernod, cook to a paste.
Sit the oysters on rock salt, spoon over the mixture and dust with Parmesan.
Bake at 220C for 8-10 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned.

name: Filet Mignon with Wild Mushroom Sauce
blurb: Two small fillet steaks in a Madeira and wild mushroom cream, with buttered spinach and pommes purée.
ingredients: smooth mash and spinach to serve
method: Sear the fillets to rare-medium, rest.
Fry the mushrooms and shallot in the butter, add the Madeira and reduce, then the stock and cream.
Return any resting juices, spoon the sauce over the steaks with mash and spinach.

name: Chicken Katsu Curry
blurb: Crisp panko chicken with a mild, glossy Japanese curry sauce and rice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp plain flour
Oil for shallow frying, rice to serve
method: Soften the onion and carrot in oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and spices for 2 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then whisk in the stock, soy and honey. Simmer 15 minutes, then blitz smooth.
Coat the chicken in flour, egg and panko. Shallow fry for 3-4 minutes each side until golden and cooked.
Slice the chicken, pour the sauce alongside and serve with rice.

name: Thai Green Chicken Curry
blurb: Fragrant coconut curry with green paste, aubergine and Thai basil.
ingredients: 2 tsp fish sauce, 1 tsp palm or brown sugar
method: Fry the curry paste in a little of the thick coconut cream for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat, then pour in the rest of the coconut milk.
Add the aubergine and simmer 8 minutes, then the beans for 4 more.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and lime, stir through the basil and serve with rice.

name: Pad Thai
blurb: Stir-fried rice noodles with tamarind, egg, prawns, peanuts and lime.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1.5 tbsp palm sugar
Lime wedges and chilli flakes to serve
method: Mix the tamarind, fish sauce and sugar into a sauce.
Stir-fry the tofu in hot oil until golden, add the prawns until pink, then push aside and scramble the egg.
Add the drained noodles and sauce, tossing over high heat until coated and tender.
Toss through the beansprouts and spring onions, then serve with peanuts, lime and chilli.

name: Beef in Black Bean Sauce
blurb: Quick wok stir-fry of beef strips, peppers and fermented black beans.
ingredients: 500g rump or sirloin steak, thinly sliced
2 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp sugar
method: Toss the beef with a little soy and cornflour. Sear in a very hot wok in batches, then set aside.
Stir-fry the onion and peppers for 2 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and black beans.
Return the beef, add the wine, soy, sugar and the cornflour water.
Toss until glossy and thickened, about 1 minute, and serve with rice.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
blurb: Sichuan stir-fry with dried chillies, peanuts and a tingly sauce.
ingredients: 10 dried red chillies, 1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns
Sauce: 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 2 tsp sugar, 1 tsp cornflour
method: Marinate the chicken in a little soy and cornflour for 10 minutes, then sear in a hot wok until nearly cooked. Remove.
Fry the dried chillies and Sichuan pepper in oil for 20 seconds, then add the garlic and ginger.
Return the chicken, add the sauce and toss until glossy.
Stir in the peanuts and spring onions and serve with rice.

name: Miso-Glazed Salmon
blurb: Salmon fillets baked under a sweet-savoury miso glaze, with greens and rice.
ingredients: 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey
Rice and sesame seeds to serve
method: Mix the miso, mirin, soy, honey and ginger.
Sit the salmon on a lined tray, spoon over most of the glaze and add the greens alongside with a little oil.
Grill or bake at 200C fan for 8-10 minutes until the salmon is just cooked and the glaze is caramelised.
Serve with rice, the remaining glaze and a scatter of sesame.

name: Chicken Chow Mein
blurb: Egg noodles tossed with chicken, cabbage and beansprouts in a savoury sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar
method: Cook the noodles, drain and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry the chicken in a hot wok until nearly done, then add the garlic and cabbage.
Add the noodles, beansprouts, spring onions and sauce, tossing over high heat for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately.

name: Crispy Tofu & Broccoli Stir-Fry
blurb: Cornflour-crisped tofu with broccoli in a garlicky soy-ginger sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp cornflour, 100ml water
method: Toss the tofu in cornflour and salt, then fry in shallow oil until crisp on all sides. Drain.
Stir-fry the broccoli with a splash of water until bright and just tender, then add the garlic and ginger.
Add the sauce and let it thicken, then return the tofu and toss to coat.
Serve over rice with sesame seeds.

name: Beef Bibimbap
blurb: Rice bowl topped with seasoned vegetables, bulgogi beef and a fried egg.
ingredients: Bulgogi marinade: 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp grated pear
Gochujang, sesame seeds and sesame oil to serve
method: Marinate the beef for 20 minutes.
Blanch and lightly season the spinach and beansprouts separately; quickly saute the carrot and mushrooms.
Sear the beef in a hot pan until caramelised.
Fry the eggs. Build bowls with rice, the vegetables arranged around, beef and a fried egg.
Serve with gochujang and sesame oil to stir through.

name: Teriyaki Chicken Donburi
blurb: Pan-fried chicken thighs in a sticky teriyaki glaze over rice.
ingredients: Sauce: 5 tbsp soy, 4 tbsp mirin, 3 tbsp sake, 2 tbsp sugar
Spring onions and sesame seeds to garnish
method: Fry the chicken skin-side down until deeply golden, then flip and cook through. Pour off excess fat.
Add the sauce ingredients and let them bubble and reduce, spooning over the chicken until sticky and glossy.
Slice the chicken and serve over rice with the sauce, spring onions and sesame.

name: Singapore Noodles
blurb: Thin rice vermicelli stir-fried with curry powder, prawns and char siu.
ingredients: 150g cooked prawns, 150g char siu or cooked pork, sliced
method: Scramble the egg in a hot wok and set aside.
Stir-fry the pepper and carrot for 2 minutes, then add the curry powder for 30 seconds.
Add the drained noodles, prawns, pork, soy and sugar, tossing until coated and hot.
Fold through the beansprouts, spring onions and egg, and serve.

name: Chicken Pho
blurb: Clear aromatic chicken broth with rice noodles and a pile of fresh herbs.
ingredients: 3 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves, 1 tsp coriander seeds
To serve: beansprouts, Thai basil, coriander, lime, sliced chilli
method: Char the onion and ginger under the grill until blackened in spots.
Simmer the stock with the charred aromatics and toasted spices for 30 minutes, then strain.
Season the broth with fish sauce and sugar.
Cook the noodles and divide between bowls with the chicken. Ladle over the hot broth.
Serve with the herb and lime plate to add at the table.

name: Sweet & Sour Pork
blurb: Crisp pork pieces with pineapple and peppers in a tangy red sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 4 tbsp ketchup, 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp soy, 150ml water, 1 tsp cornflour
Oil for frying, rice to serve
method: Coat the pork in egg then cornflour and deep or shallow fry until golden and crisp. Drain.
Stir-fry the onion and pepper for 2 minutes, then add the pineapple.
Pour in the mixed sauce and simmer until thick and glossy.
Toss the pork through at the last second to keep it crisp, and serve with rice.

name: Egg Fried Rice
blurb: The Sunday-night classic: day-old rice, egg, peas and spring onion.
ingredients: 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil
method: Scramble the eggs in a very hot oiled wok until just set, then remove.
Fry the garlic and peas briefly, then add the rice and press it into the pan to heat through.
Return the egg, add the soy, sesame oil and white pepper, and toss.
Finish with the spring onions and serve.

name: Japanese Beef Curry Rice
blurb: Comforting, mildly sweet curry with tender beef, carrot and potato.
ingredients: 1 tbsp grated apple, 1 tbsp grated ginger
method: Brown the beef, then soften the onions until caramelised.
Add the carrot, potato, apple, ginger and stock, and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Turn off the heat, dissolve in the roux blocks, then simmer 10 minutes more until thickened.
Serve over rice.

name: Larb Gai (Thai Chicken Salad)
blurb: Zingy minced chicken salad with lime, fish sauce, chilli and toasted rice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp uncooked rice, toasted and ground
Juice of 3 limes, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar
4 spring onions, handful each mint and coriander
method: Cook the chicken mince in a dry hot pan with a splash of water, breaking it small, until just done.
Off the heat, add the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and chilli.
Stir through the shallots, spring onions, herbs and toasted rice powder.
Serve warm or at room temperature with lettuce leaves for wrapping.

name: Char Siu Pork with Rice
blurb: Sticky roast pork with a five-spice honey glaze, sliced over rice and greens.
ingredients: 700g pork shoulder or fillet, in long strips
3 tbsp hoisin, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine
1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp five-spice, 2 garlic cloves crushed
1 tsp red fermented bean curd or a little tomato puree (for colour)
Rice and pak choi to serve
method: Mix the marinade and coat the pork. Leave for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.
Heat oven to 200C fan. Roast the pork on a rack over a tray of water for 25-30 minutes, basting with reserved marinade twice.
Grill for the last 3-4 minutes to caramelise, then rest for 10 minutes.
Slice and serve over rice with steamed pak choi and any pan juices.

name: Chicken Katsu Curry (Fakeaway)
blurb: Crisp panko chicken with a mild, glossy Japanese curry sauce and rice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp flour, 1 tbsp garam masala, 1 tsp turmeric
500ml chicken stock, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp honey
Oil for frying, rice to serve
method: Soften the onion and carrot, add garlic, ginger and spices, then the flour.
Whisk in the stock, soy and honey; simmer 15 minutes, then blitz smooth.
Coat the chicken in flour, egg and panko; shallow fry 3-4 minutes each side.
Slice and serve over rice with the sauce poured alongside.

name: Salt & Pepper Chicken
blurb: Crispy chicken tossed with fried onion, pepper, chilli and five-spice.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 green pepper, 2 red chillies, sliced
1 tsp Chinese five-spice, 1 tsp white pepper, 1 tsp flaky salt
Oil for shallow frying, rice to serve
method: Toss the chicken in the egg white then cornflour and fry in shallow oil until deep golden and crisp. Drain.
Stir-fry the onion, pepper and chillies in a little oil until charred at the edges.
Add the garlic, five-spice, white pepper and salt.
Return the crispy chicken and toss for 30 seconds; serve with rice.

name: Crispy Chilli Beef
blurb: Deep-fried shredded beef in a sticky sweet, sharp chilli sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 4 tbsp ketchup, 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 3 tbsp sweet chilli sauce, 2 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp sugar, 1-2 tsp chilli flakes
Oil for deep frying, rice to serve
method: Toss the beef in the cornflour and shake off the excess.
Deep fry in batches at 180C until dark and crisp; drain.
Stir-fry the carrot and pepper briefly, add the garlic, then the mixed sauce and bubble until sticky.
Toss the beef through at the last second and finish with spring onions; serve with rice.

name: Homemade Doner Kebab
blurb: Spiced blitzed lamb baked into a loaf, sliced thin and crisped, in flatbread.
ingredients: 2 tsp each cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, oregano, 1 tsp cayenne
Flatbreads, shredded lettuce, tomato, red onion, chilli sauce and garlic sauce to serve
method: Blitz the lamb with the onion, garlic, spices and salt to a smooth, tacky paste.
Press firmly into a loaf tin and bake at 180C fan for 35-40 minutes. Rest, then chill briefly to firm up.
Slice very thinly and crisp the slices in a hot dry pan.
Stuff into warm flatbreads with salad and both sauces.

name: Sweet & Sour Pork
blurb: Crisp pork with pineapple and peppers in a tangy red sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 4 tbsp ketchup, 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp soy, 150ml water, 1 tsp cornflour
Oil for frying, rice to serve
method: Coat the pork in egg then cornflour and shallow fry until golden and crisp; drain.
Stir-fry the onion and pepper, then add the pineapple.
Pour in the mixed sauce and simmer until thick and glossy.
Toss the pork through at the last second; serve with rice.

name: Chicken Chow Mein
blurb: Egg noodles tossed with chicken, cabbage and beansprouts in a savoury sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 3 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar
method: Cook the noodles, drain and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry the chicken in a hot wok until nearly done, add the garlic and cabbage.
Add the noodles, beansprouts, spring onions and sauce; toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately.

name: Chip Shop Chips & Curry Sauce
blurb: Proper chunky oven chips smothered in a mild, glossy chip-shop curry sauce.
ingredients: 1kg Maris Piper potatoes, cut into thick chips
2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp five-spice
1 tbsp cornflour, 1 tbsp sugar, 500ml vegetable stock, 1 tbsp soy
method: Parboil the chips for 6 minutes, drain and steam-dry, then roast in hot oil at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes.
Fry the onion until soft, add the curry powder, turmeric and five-spice for 1 minute.
Stir in the cornflour and sugar, then whisk in the stock and soy.
Simmer 5 minutes to a glossy sauce and pour over the chips.

name: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
blurb: Marinated in buttermilk, double-dredged and fried shatteringly crisp.
ingredients: 500ml buttermilk, 1 tbsp hot sauce, 1 tsp salt
300g flour, 2 tbsp cornflour, 1 tbsp each smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, 1 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp black pepper
method: Marinate the chicken in the seasoned buttermilk for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Mix the flour with the cornflour and spices. Dredge each piece, pressing the coating on firmly.
Fry at 165C for 12-15 minutes, turning, until deep golden and 75C inside.
Rest on a rack for 5 minutes so it stays crisp.

name: Teriyaki Chicken Donburi
blurb: Pan-fried chicken thighs in a sticky teriyaki glaze over rice.
ingredients: Sauce: 5 tbsp soy, 4 tbsp mirin, 3 tbsp sake, 2 tbsp sugar
Spring onions and sesame seeds to garnish
method: Fry the chicken skin-side down until deeply golden, flip and cook through; pour off excess fat.
Add the sauce and let it bubble and reduce, spooning over the chicken until sticky.
Slice and serve over rice with the sauce, spring onions and sesame.

name: Chicken Pakora Wraps
blurb: Spiced gram-flour-battered chicken in a wrap with mint yoghurt and salad.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, turmeric, chilli powder, 3 garlic cloves and 2cm ginger crushed
Cold sparkling water to a batter
Wraps, shredded lettuce and red onion
Mint yoghurt: 150g yoghurt, handful of mint, squeeze of lemon
method: Whisk the gram flour, baking powder, spices, garlic, ginger and enough water to a thick batter.
Coat the chicken and deep or shallow fry at 175C for 4-5 minutes until golden and cooked.
Mix the mint yoghurt.
Fill warm wraps with salad, pakora chicken and a good drizzle of mint yoghurt.

name: Lamb Bhuna
blurb: Lamb cooked down hard in a thick, dark, deeply spiced onion-tomato masala.
ingredients: 3 tomatoes, chopped, plus 2 tbsp tomato purée
2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp coriander, 2 tsp chilli powder
method: Fry the onions in oil until deep golden, about 15 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and ground spices, then the lamb, and brown well.
Add the tomatoes, purée and a splash of water; cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Uncover and cook hard, stirring, until the sauce is thick and clinging. Finish with garam masala and coriander.

name: Diner-Style Quarter Pounder
blurb: A fat beef patty, American cheese, pickles and burger sauce in a soft bun.
ingredients: 600g beef mince (20% fat), shaped into 4 thick patties
Burger sauce: 4 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp mustard, 1 tbsp chopped gherkin, pinch of paprika
Sliced pickles, shredded lettuce, sliced tomato
method: Season the patties well and fry in a hot pan for 3-4 minutes each side, adding cheese for the last minute.
Toast the buns cut-side down in the pan.
Spread both bun halves with burger sauce.
Build with lettuce, tomato, the cheesy patty and pickles.

name: Tonkatsu (Pork Katsu)
blurb: Panko pork loin fried crisp, sliced, with tonkatsu sauce, rice and cabbage.
ingredients: Tonkatsu sauce (shop-bought, or ketchup + Worcestershire + soy + sugar)
Oil for shallow frying, rice to serve
method: Coat the pork in flour, egg then panko, pressing on firmly.
Shallow fry for 3 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked; drain and rest 2 minutes.
Slice into thick fingers.
Serve with rice, a heap of raw cabbage and plenty of tonkatsu sauce.

name: Chicken Shawarma Plate
blurb: Spiced roast chicken thighs with rice, salad, pickles and garlic sauce.
ingredients: 150g yoghurt, juice of 1 lemon, 3 tbsp oil
2 tsp each cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, 1 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 4 garlic cloves
Rice, chopped salad, pickled chillies and garlic sauce to serve
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt, lemon, oil, spices and garlic for 1 hour.
Spread on a tray with the onions and roast at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes until charred.
Rest, then slice.
Serve over rice with salad, pickles and garlic sauce.

name: Firecracker Prawn Noodles
blurb: Prawns in a hot, sweet, sticky chilli sauce tossed with noodles.
ingredients: Sauce: 3 tbsp sweet chilli, 2 tbsp sriracha, 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sugar
3 garlic cloves, 3 spring onions, sesame seeds
method: Cook the noodles and toss with a little oil.
Stir-fry the pepper and onion for 2 minutes, add the garlic, then the prawns until pink.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble and coat.
Toss through the noodles and spring onions; finish with sesame.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
blurb: Wok-fried day-old rice with chicken, egg, peas and soy.
ingredients: 2.5 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, white pepper
method: Stir-fry the chicken in a hot wok until cooked, then push aside and scramble the egg.
Add the garlic and peas briefly, then the rice, pressing it into the pan.
Add the soy, sesame oil and white pepper and toss until hot through.
Fold through the spring onions and serve.

name: Poached Cod with Parsley Sauce
blurb: Cod gently poached in milk, served under an old-fashioned parsley sauce with buttered new potatoes.
method: Poach the cod in the milk with the bay for 6-8 minutes, then lift out and keep the milk.
Make a roux, whisk in the poaching milk to a smooth sauce, stir in the parsley.
Serve the cod with the sauce and buttered potatoes.

name: Salmon Fishcakes
blurb: Flaked salmon and mash bound with dill and mustard, crumbed and fried crisp. Serve with lemon mayo.
method: Mix the salmon, mash, mustard and dill and shape into 8 cakes; chill.
Coat in flour, egg then breadcrumbs.
Fry until golden both sides and serve with lemon mayo and salad.

name: Tuna Melt
blurb: Tuna mayo with sweetcorn and spring onion piled on sourdough under bubbling cheese. A quick dinner.
method: Mix the tuna with the mayo, corn and spring onion.
Pile onto the bread, top with cheese.
Grill until the cheese is molten and bubbling.

name: Garlic & Chilli Prawn Linguine
blurb: Prawns fried in garlic-chilli oil with white wine and lemon, tossed with linguine and parsley.
method: Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli, add the prawns and fry 2 minutes.
Add the wine and bubble, then the drained linguine and pasta water.
Toss with lemon and parsley.

name: Miso-Glazed Baked Salmon
blurb: Salmon marinated in miso, mirin and sugar, then grilled until caramelised. With rice and greens.
ingredients: rice and pak choi to serve
method: Mix the miso, mirin, sugar and soy and coat the salmon, ideally for 30 minutes.
Grill or bake at 200C for 8-10 minutes, basting, until glazed and just cooked.
Serve with rice and steamed pak choi.

name: Baja Fish Tacos
blurb: Beer-battered white fish in warm tortillas with cabbage slaw, chipotle crema and lime.
method: Whisk the flour, lager and baking powder to a batter; heat the oil to 180C.
Dip the fish and fry until golden and crisp, drain.
Fill tortillas with slaw, fish and chipotle crema, squeeze over lime.

name: Smoked Haddock Kedgeree
blurb: Curried rice with flaked smoked haddock, soft-boiled eggs, peas and parsley. Anglo-Indian comfort.
method: Poach the haddock in milk or water, then flake, discarding skin and bones.
Soften the onion in the butter with the curry powder, stir in the rice and stock and cook 12 minutes.
Fold in the haddock, peas and quartered soft-boiled eggs; finish with parsley and lemon.

name: Mussels in Cider & Cream
blurb: Mussels steamed with cider, leek, bacon and a splash of cream, with bread for the broth.
method: Fry the lardons, add the leek and butter and soften.
Add the cider and bring to the boil, tip in the mussels, cover and steam 4 minutes.
Stir in the cream and parsley; discard any closed shells.

name: Pan-Fried Sea Bass with Salsa Verde
blurb: Crisp-skinned sea bass fillets over crushed potatoes with a sharp caper-and-herb salsa verde.
ingredients: big handful parsley, mint and basil
method: Boil and lightly crush the potatoes with oil.
Blitz the herbs, capers, garlic, vinegar and oil to a salsa verde.
Fry the bass skin-side down until crisp, flip briefly, and serve over the potatoes with the salsa.

name: Quick Fish Pie
blurb: A fish pie mix in a speedy crème fraîche and dill sauce under a piped mash lid, baked golden.
ingredients: 600g fish pie mix (white fish, salmon, smoked fish)
method: Mix the raw fish and prawns with the crème fraîche, mustard and herbs and tip into a dish.
Top with mash and cheese.
Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.

name: 20-Minute Coconut Prawn Curry
blurb: Prawns simmered in a quick coconut, tomato and lime curry with spinach. Fast and fragrant.
method: Fry the onion, add the curry paste, then the passata and coconut milk.
Simmer 5 minutes, then add the prawns and spinach.
Cook 4 minutes, finish with lime and coriander; serve with rice.

name: Smoked Cod & Corn Chowder
blurb: A creamy chowder of smoked cod, potato, sweetcorn and bacon, thick enough to be dinner.
method: Fry the lardons, add the onion, celery and potato.
Add the stock and simmer 12 minutes, then the milk and corn.
Add the cod and cook 5 minutes until it flakes; finish with parsley.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Poke-Style Bowl
blurb: Flaked teriyaki salmon over rice with avocado, edamame, cucumber and sesame. A cooked take on poke.
ingredients: 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp honey
method: Pan-fry the salmon, add the soy, mirin and honey and glaze, then flake.
Divide the rice between bowls.
Top with salmon, avocado, edamame and cucumber, drizzle with sriracha mayo and sesame.

name: Plaice with Brown Butter & Capers
blurb: Delicate plaice fillets floured and fried, finished with nut-brown butter, capers and lemon.
ingredients: boiled potatoes and greens to serve
method: Dust the plaice and fry 2 minutes a side in a little butter, plate up.
Add the rest of the butter and cook to nut-brown.
Add the capers, lemon and parsley and spoon over the fish.

name: Hake with Chorizo & White Beans
blurb: Hake fillets pan-roasted and set on smoky chorizo, butter beans and cherry tomatoes.
method: Fry the chorizo until the oil runs, add the shallot, beans and tomatoes and cook 8 minutes.
Nestle in the seasoned hake, cover and cook 6-8 minutes until it flakes.
Finish with lemon and parsley.

name: Homemade Fish Goujons & Chips
blurb: Panko-crumbed strips of white fish, baked crisp, with oven chips, peas and tartare. A family Friday.
ingredients: tartare sauce and lemon to serve
method: Coat the fish in flour, egg then panko.
Bake with the chips at 220C for 15-18 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Serve with minted peas, tartare and lemon.

name: Salmon en Papillote
blurb: Salmon steamed in a paper parcel with lemon, dill, courgette ribbons and white wine. No washing up.
method: Lay each fillet on courgette ribbons on a square of parchment.
Top with lemon, dill, wine and butter and fold into sealed parcels.
Bake at 200C for 12-14 minutes; open at the table.

name: The Fish Finger Sandwich
blurb: Crisp fish fingers in soft white bread with tartare, lettuce and a squeeze of lemon. Unbeatable.
method: Bake or grill the fish fingers until deep golden and crisp.
Butter the bread and spread with tartare.
Layer in the fish fingers and lettuce, squeeze over lemon, close and press.

name: Thai Fish Cakes
blurb: Bouncy fish cakes with red curry paste, green beans and lime leaf, with a sweet chilli-cucumber dip.
ingredients: sweet chilli sauce and cucumber to serve
method: Blitz the fish with the curry paste, fish sauce and egg to a paste.
Fold in the beans and lime leaf and shape into small patties.
Shallow-fry until golden and springy; serve with sweet chilli and diced cucumber.

name: Roast Cod with Romesco
blurb: A thick cod loin roasted and served on a smoky roast-pepper and almond romesco with charred greens.
method: Blitz the peppers, almonds, garlic, vinegar, paprika and oil to a romesco.
Roast the seasoned cod at 200C for 10 minutes; char the tenderstem in a hot pan.
Spread the romesco on plates and sit the cod and greens on top.

name: Prawn Toast & Sesame Noodles
blurb: Crisp sesame prawn toasts alongside a bowl of quick garlic-sesame noodles. A takeaway favourite, at home.
ingredients: 1 egg white, 1 tsp cornflour, 1 tsp sesame oil
2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, 1 garlic clove
method: Blitz the prawns with the egg white, cornflour and sesame oil, spread on the bread, press into sesame seeds.
Shallow-fry seed-side down until golden, then flip; cut into triangles.
Toss the cooked noodles in the soy, vinegar, sugar and garlic and serve with the toasts.

name: Trout with Almonds
blurb: Whole trout floured and fried, finished with butter, flaked almonds and lemon. A ten-minute classic.
ingredients: boiled potatoes and green beans to serve
method: Dust the trout and fry 4 minutes a side until the skin crisps, plate up.
Add the butter and almonds to the pan and cook until golden.
Add lemon and parsley and pour over the fish.

name: Grilled Mackerel with Gooseberry Sauce
blurb: Oily mackerel fillets grilled crisp, cut by a sharp gooseberry compote. A very British pairing.
ingredients: boiled new potatoes and watercress to serve
method: Simmer the gooseberries with the sugar and vinegar until collapsed, then beat in the butter.
Slash and grill the mackerel skin-side up for 4-5 minutes until crisp.
Serve with the sauce, potatoes and watercress.

name: Cod & Leek Gratin
blurb: Cod and softened leeks in a mustard cheese sauce, topped with breadcrumbs and baked. Comfort with fish.
method: Make a cheese sauce with the butter, flour, milk, cheddar and mustard.
Fold in the leeks and raw cod and tip into a dish.
Top with breadcrumbs and bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Salmon & Miso Noodle Soup
blurb: Salmon poached in a gingery miso broth with udon, greens and a jammy egg. Twenty-five minutes.
method: Simmer the ginger in the stock, whisk in the miso off the boil.
Add the salmon and pak choi and poach 4 minutes.
Divide cooked udon between bowls, ladle over the soup and add halved eggs and spring onion.

name: Fritto Misto
blurb: A light-battered fry-up of squid, prawns and whitebait with lemon and garlic aioli. A sharing supper.
method: Whisk the flours with cold sparkling water to a thin batter; heat the oil to 180C.
Dip the seafood and fry in small batches until pale gold and crisp, drain on paper.
Season with salt and serve at once with lemon and aioli.

name: Tandoori Salmon Traybake
blurb: Salmon in a yoghurt-tandoori marinade roasted over spiced potatoes and green beans.
method: Marinate the salmon in the yoghurt, tandoori spice and lemon.
Roast the potatoes with the cumin and oil at 200C for 20 minutes, add the beans.
Sit the salmon on top and roast 12 minutes; scatter with coriander.

name: Cullen Skink
blurb: A thick Scottish soup of smoked haddock, potato, onion and milk. Simple, warming, complete.
method: Poach the haddock in the milk and water, then lift out and flake.
Soften the onion in the butter, add the potato and the poaching liquid and simmer until soft.
Roughly mash some potato to thicken, return the haddock, warm through and add the herbs.

name: Crispy-Skin Salmon on Lentils
blurb: Salmon fried skin-side crisp, set on warm puy lentils with bacon, spinach and a mustard dressing.
method: Fry the lardons and diced veg, add the lentils and stock and simmer 25 minutes.
Fry the salmon skin-side down, pressing, until crisp, then flip for 1 minute.
Wilt the spinach into the lentils, dress with mustard and vinegar, and top with the salmon.

name: Prawn & Cheddar Grits
blurb: Creamy cheese grits topped with garlicky prawns, bacon and a little hot sauce. Southern comfort.
method: Cook the grits in the milk and water until thick, beat in the cheddar.
Fry the lardons, then the prawns and garlic for 2-3 minutes.
Spoon the prawns and bacon over the grits with spring onion and hot sauce.

name: Herb-Crusted Pollock with Mushy Peas
blurb: Sustainable pollock under a lemon-parsley crumb with proper mushy peas and buttery potatoes.
method: Mix the crumbs, parsley, zest and melted butter and press onto the fish; bake at 200C for 12 minutes.
Simmer the peas until soft and crush with butter, mint and seasoning.
Serve with buttered potatoes.

name: Salt & Pepper Squid with Lime Mayo
blurb: Cornflour-dusted squid fried crisp and tossed with fried chilli, garlic and five-spice.
ingredients: 1 tsp five-spice, 1 tsp white pepper, 1 tsp salt
1 red chilli, 3 garlic cloves, 2 spring onions
method: Toss the squid in the seasoned cornflour.
Deep-fry in batches at 190C for 90 seconds until pale and crisp, drain.
Flash-fry the chilli, garlic and spring onion, toss the squid through, serve with lime mayo.

name: Fish Korma
blurb: Chunks of white fish poached in a gentle, creamy almond-and-coconut korma. Mild enough for everyone.
method: Fry the onions and cardamom until soft, add the korma paste.
Add the coconut milk, almonds and yoghurt and simmer 8 minutes.
Slide in the fish and poach gently for 6 minutes; finish with coriander.

name: Grilled Hake with Anchovy Butter
blurb: Meaty hake fillets grilled and topped with a melting anchovy-parsley butter, over crushed peas.
ingredients: 20g butter and a little mint for the peas
method: Beat the butter with the anchovy, parsley and lemon.
Grill the hake for 6-8 minutes until it flakes, then top with the butter.
Serve on peas crushed with butter and mint.

name: Seared Tuna with Warm Niçoise
blurb: Tuna steaks seared rare over a warm salad of new potatoes, green beans, olives and soft egg.
ingredients: 1 tbsp Dijon, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 4 tbsp olive oil
method: Boil the potatoes and beans; whisk the mustard, vinegar and oil to a dressing.
Toss the warm potatoes, beans and olives in the dressing.
Sear the tuna 1 minute a side, slice, and serve over the salad with the halved eggs.

name: Clam & Bacon Linguine
blurb: Fresh clams steamed open with bacon, garlic, white wine and parsley, tossed with linguine.
method: Fry the lardons, add the garlic and wine and bring to the boil.
Tip in the clams, cover and steam 3-4 minutes until open.
Toss the just-cooked linguine and parsley through with a little pasta water.

name: Baked Cod Puttanesca
blurb: Cod baked in a gutsy sauce of tomatoes, olives, capers and anchovy, with bread or potatoes.
method: Melt the anchovies with the garlic and chilli, add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer 10 minutes.
Nestle in the cod, cover and bake at 200C for 12 minutes until it flakes.
Finish with parsley and serve with bread.

name: Teriyaki Salmon Noodles
blurb: Glazed salmon flaked through stir-fried noodles with tenderstem, sesame and spring onion.
ingredients: 3 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp honey
method: Pan-fry the salmon, glaze with the soy, mirin and honey, then flake.
Stir-fry the garlic and tenderstem, add the cooked noodles and a splash of the glaze.
Fold the salmon back in and finish with sesame oil, seeds and spring onion.

name: Tomato & Saffron Fish Stew
blurb: A quick bouillabaisse-style stew of white fish, mussels and prawns in a saffron-fennel-tomato broth.
method: Soften the fennel, onion and garlic, add the saffron, tomatoes, stock and orange zest and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the fish and cook 4 minutes, then the mussels and prawns until the shells open.
Serve with rouille-topped toasts.

name: Individual Salmon & Prawn Pies
blurb: Little pots of salmon and prawns in dill sauce under mash, baked golden. Two neat portions.
method: Mix the raw salmon and prawns with the crème fraîche, mustard and dill and divide between two dishes.
Top with mash and cheese.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until bubbling and browned.

name: Maryland Crab Cakes
blurb: Crab bound with just enough mayo and crumb, fried golden, with a lemon-caper remoulade.
method: Gently mix the crab with the mayo, egg, crumbs, mustard and spice, keeping it lumpy.
Shape into 4 cakes and chill 20 minutes.
Fry 3 minutes a side until golden; serve with remoulade and lemon.

name: Grilled Swordfish with Caponata
blurb: A firm swordfish steak grilled and served with sweet-sour Sicilian aubergine caponata.
ingredients: 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar
method: Fry the aubergine golden, remove; soften the onion and celery, add the passata, olives, capers and raisins.
Return the aubergine, add the vinegar and sugar and simmer 15 minutes.
Griddle the swordfish 2-3 minutes a side and serve on the caponata.

name: Smoked Fish & Spinach Pie
blurb: Smoked haddock and spinach in a nutmeg cream sauce under mash, with a hidden layer of soft egg.
method: Poach the haddock in the milk, flake, and use the milk for a béchamel with the butter and flour.
Wilt the spinach, fold into the sauce with the fish and nutmeg, tip into a dish and tuck in halved eggs.
Top with mash and cheese and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

name: Prawn Saganaki
blurb: Prawns baked in a tomato and ouzo sauce with feta, straight from the pan with bread.
method: Soften the onion and garlic, add the ouzo and cook off, then the tomatoes and chilli.
Simmer 10 minutes, add the prawns and crumble over the feta.
Bake at 200C for 10 minutes; scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

name: Basque Hake in Green Sauce (Merluza en Salsa Verde)
blurb: Hake fillets and clams in a glossy garlic, parsley and white-wine sauce thickened just with the fish.
method: Gently fry the garlic in oil, stir in the flour, then the wine and stock, swirling the pan to emulsify.
Add the hake and clams, cover and cook 6-8 minutes, shaking the pan often.
Stir in the parsley and serve with potatoes and peas.

name: Crispy Fish Goujon Wraps
blurb: Panko fish goujons in soft tortillas with shredded lettuce, tartare and pickled onion. A quick handheld dinner.
method: Coat the fish in flour, egg then panko and bake at 220C for 15 minutes until crisp.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill with lettuce, goujons, tartare, pickled onion and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Zuppa Toscana
blurb: A creamy Tuscan-style soup of Italian sausage, potato and kale with a hit of chilli and bacon.
ingredients: 200g kale or cavolo nero, stripped and torn
method: Fry the sausagemeat in a large pot, breaking it into chunks, until browned. Add the bacon and cook until its fat runs.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, then the garlic and chilli flakes for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 12-15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer 3-4 minutes until wilted but still green.
Off the heat, stir in the cream and season well. Serve with Parmesan.

name: Italian Wedding Soup
blurb: Tiny herby meatballs and pasta in a clear parmesan broth with plenty of greens.
ingredients: 300g beef mince (or half beef, half pork)
30g breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 30g grated Parmesan, 2 garlic cloves, small bunch parsley
1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks, finely diced
method: Mix the mince with the breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, crushed garlic and chopped parsley and season. Roll into small marble-sized balls.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in a little oil in a large pot for 8 minutes.
Add the stock and Parmesan rind and bring to a gentle simmer. Drop in the meatballs and poach for 8 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente.
Stir in the spinach until just wilted, remove the rind, season, and serve with more Parmesan.

name: Marry Me Chicken
blurb: Pan-fried chicken in a rich sun-dried tomato, parmesan and basil cream sauce.
ingredients: 1 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp dried oregano
Pasta, mash or bread, to serve
method: Season the chicken and fry in the oil and butter for 4-5 minutes each side until golden and just cooked. Lift out.
Add the garlic, chilli flakes, oregano and sun-dried tomatoes to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock, scrape the base, and reduce by half, then add the cream and simmer for 3-4 minutes to thicken.
Stir in the Parmesan until smooth, then return the chicken and any juices to warm through.
Scatter with basil and serve with pasta, mash or bread to mop the sauce.

name: Chicken Piccata
blurb: Lightly floured chicken escalopes in a sharp lemon, caper and butter pan sauce.
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts, halved horizontally and beaten thin
2 lemons (juice of both, plus a few thin slices)
Small bunch parsley, chopped; spaghetti or new potatoes, to serve
method: Dust the chicken in the seasoned flour. Fry in the oil and half the butter for 2-3 minutes each side until golden. Lift out and keep warm.
Soften the shallot in the pan for 1 minute, then add the wine and lemon slices and reduce by half.
Add the stock and lemon juice and simmer for 2 minutes.
Whisk in the rest of the butter and stir in the capers.
Return the chicken briefly to coat, scatter with parsley, and serve with spaghetti or potatoes.

name: White Chicken Chili
blurb: A creamy, mild chilli of chicken, white beans and green chillies with lime and coriander.
ingredients: 500g chicken thighs, diced (or use shredded cooked chicken)
2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp cayenne
2 x 400g tins cannellini or butter beans, drained
1 small tin (200g) chopped green chillies (or 2 fresh jalapeños)
50g grated Monterey Jack or mild cheddar
Lime, coriander, sliced jalapeño and tortilla chips, to serve
method: Brown the chicken in a little oil in a pot, then add the onion for 5 minutes and the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add one tin of beans (mashed), the second tin whole, the green chillies and the stock.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the chilli has thickened slightly.
Off the heat, stir in the soured cream and cheese until melted and creamy. Season and sharpen with lime.
Serve topped with coriander, sliced jalapeño and a handful of crushed tortilla chips.

name: Beef Tips & Gravy
blurb: Chunks of seared beef braised low in a rich onion-and-mushroom gravy, served over rice or mash.
ingredients: 700g braising steak or beef sirloin tips, in 3cm cubes
1 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp Dijon
Steamed rice, mashed potato or buttered egg noodles, to serve
method: Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown in batches in a heavy pan; set aside.
Fry the onions for 8 minutes until soft and golden, add the mushrooms for 5 minutes, then the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Return the beef, add the stock, Worcestershire, Dijon, bay and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 (or 150C oven) until the beef is very tender and the gravy is glossy.
Season, discard the bay and thyme, and serve over rice, mash or noodles.

name: Scalloped Potatoes & Ham
blurb: Thinly sliced potato and ham baked in a garlicky cheese sauce until bubbling and golden.
ingredients: 400g cooked ham or gammon, torn into pieces
50g butter and 40g flour (or cornflour for GF)
3 garlic cloves, crushed; grating of nutmeg
Green salad or peas, to serve
method: Heat the oven to 180C fan. Melt the butter, cook the garlic for 30 seconds, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk and cream to a smooth sauce. Add the nutmeg and three-quarters of the cheese; season.
Layer half the potatoes in a buttered dish, then the onion and ham, then the rest of the potatoes.
Pour over the cheese sauce, pressing the potatoes down so they are submerged, and scatter with the rest of the cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes, then uncover for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the top is deep golden.
Rest for 10 minutes so it sets, then serve with a salad or peas.

name: Courgette Lasagne
blurb: A lighter lasagne — ribbons of griddled courgette in place of pasta, layered with beef ragù and ricotta.
ingredients: 4 large courgettes, sliced lengthways into 4mm ribbons
1 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 carrot, finely chopped
400g chopped tomatoes, 2 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tsp oregano
250g ricotta mixed with 1 egg and 30g grated Parmesan
method: Salt the courgette ribbons and leave 15 minutes, then pat very dry and griddle (or bake) in batches until softened and lightly charred — they must not be watery.
Brown the mince, add the onion, carrot and garlic for 6 minutes, then the tomatoes, purée and oregano. Simmer 20 minutes to a thick ragù; season.
In a baking dish, layer: ragù, courgette ribbons, dollops of the ricotta mix. Repeat, finishing with ragù and the torn mozzarella.
Bake at 190C fan for 30 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Rest for 10-15 minutes (important, or it slides) before cutting. Serve with a salad.

name: Chicken Divan
blurb: A retro American bake of chicken and broccoli in a sherry-spiked creamy cheese sauce with a crisp crumb.
ingredients: 40g panko tossed with 20g melted butter and 20g Parmesan, for the top
method: Heat the oven to 190C fan. Melt the butter, whisk in the flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in the stock and cream and simmer to a smooth sauce.
Stir in the sherry, Dijon, lemon and most of the cheddar; season.
Spread the blanched broccoli in a baking dish, top with the chicken, and pour over the sauce.
Scatter with the rest of the cheddar and the Parmesan-panko crumb.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and the top is golden and crisp. Serve with rice.

name: Chicken Lazone
blurb: New Orleans-style chicken strips in a quick Cajun-spiced butter and cream sauce, over pasta.
ingredients: 600g chicken breast, cut into thick strips
2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar
method: Mix all the spices with the salt and sugar and toss the chicken strips in the mixture.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6-8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Add the rest of the butter and let it melt, then pour in the cream.
Simmer for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens and turns a warm orange.
Toss through cooked pasta with a splash of its water, scatter with parsley, and serve.

name: King Ranch Chicken
blurb: A Texan casserole of shredded chicken, tortillas, peppers and a spiced creamy sauce, baked under cheese.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 green and 1 red pepper, diced
1 x 400g tin chopped tomatoes with green chillies (or tomatoes + 1 chopped jalapeño)
2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp chilli powder
method: Fry the onion and peppers in a little oil for 8 minutes until soft.

Add the butter, melt it, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock. Add the tomatoes with chillies and the spices and simmer 5 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the soured cream and season.
Fold the shredded chicken and torn tortillas into the sauce.
Tip half into a baking dish, scatter with half the cheese, then the rest of the mixture and the remaining cheese.
Bake at 190C fan for 25-30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

name: Boeuf Bourguignon
blurb: Beef braised slowly in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and baby onions.
ingredients: 250g button mushrooms, 200g peeled shallots or baby onions
method: Fry the lardons until crisp, then brown the floured beef in batches in a casserole.
Stir in the tomato puree, add the wine and stock, and tuck in the bouquet garni.
Cover and cook at 150C fan for 2.5 hours until the beef is very tender.
Fry the mushrooms and shallots in butter until golden and stir them in.
Simmer 20 minutes more to thicken, then serve with mash.

name: Coq au Vin
blurb: Chicken braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and shallots.
ingredients: 2 tbsp flour, 2 garlic cloves, bouquet garni
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down in a casserole, then set aside. Fry the lardons, mushrooms and shallots until golden and remove.
Stir the flour and garlic into the fat, then add the wine and stock.
Return the chicken and bouquet garni, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the lardons, mushrooms and shallots for the last 15 minutes.
Swirl in the butter, finish with parsley and serve with bread or mash.

name: Ratatouille
blurb: Slow-cooked Provencal stew of aubergine, courgette, pepper and tomato.
ingredients: Bunch of basil, 1 tsp thyme, 1 bay leaf
method: Fry the aubergine, then the courgette, then the peppers separately in oil until browned, setting each aside.
Soften the onion and garlic, add the puree, tomatoes, thyme and bay, and simmer 15 minutes.
Return all the vegetables and simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until soft and glossy.
Stir through torn basil and a final drizzle of oil; serve with bread, rice or a fried egg.

name: Croque Monsieur
blurb: Grilled ham and cheese sandwich blanketed in bechamel and gruyere.
ingredients: 1 tsp Dijon mustard, pinch of nutmeg
method: Make a thick bechamel with the butter, flour and milk; stir in the mustard, nutmeg and a third of the cheese.
Butter the bread, build sandwiches with ham and some cheese, and toast in a pan until golden.
Transfer to a tray, spread the bechamel over the top, scatter with the rest of the cheese.
Grill for 3-4 minutes until bubbling and browned. Add a fried egg on top for a croque madame.

name: Moules Mariniere
blurb: Mussels steamed open in white wine, garlic, shallot and cream, with fries.
ingredients: Fries or crusty bread to serve
method: Discard any mussels that stay open when tapped.
Soften the shallots and garlic in the butter in a large lidded pan.
Add the wine, bring to the boil, then tip in the mussels and cover.
Steam for 3-4 minutes, shaking, until they open. Discard any that stay shut.
Stir in the cream and parsley and serve with fries or bread.

name: Steak Frites with Peppercorn Sauce
blurb: Pan-fried steak with crisp fries and a creamy green peppercorn sauce.
ingredients: Oil for frying, or 4 tbsp for oven fries
Sauce: 1 shallot, 2 tbsp brandy, 150ml beef stock, 100ml double cream, 1 tbsp green peppercorns, 1 tsp Dijon
method: Cook the fries: either double-fry in oil, or toss in oil and roast at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes until crisp.
Fry the seasoned steaks in a hot pan to your liking, basting with butter and thyme. Rest.
In the same pan soften the shallot, add the brandy and flambe or reduce, then the stock, cream, peppercorns and mustard.
Simmer to a coating sauce, add any resting juices, and serve with the steak and fries.

name: Quiche Lorraine
blurb: Buttery pastry case with a set custard of bacon, cream and gruyere.
method: Fry the lardons until lightly golden, then scatter over the pastry base with the cheese.
Whisk the eggs, yolks, cream, milk, nutmeg and a little salt and pepper.
Pour into the case and bake at 160C fan for 35-40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Cool for 15 minutes before slicing; serve with a green salad.

name: French Onion Soup
blurb: Deeply caramelised onions in beef broth under a gruyere crouton.
ingredients: 1.2 litres good beef or vegetable stock
method: Cook the onions in the butter and oil over low-medium heat for 40-45 minutes, stirring, until deep brown and sweet. Add the sugar near the end.
Stir in the flour, then the wine and let it reduce.
Add the stock, bay and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes. Season.
Ladle into bowls, float a baguette slice on each, pile with gruyere and grill until molten and bubbling.

name: Salmon en Papillote
blurb: Salmon steamed in a parcel with white wine, lemon, dill and vegetables.
ingredients: 1 courgette and 1 fennel bulb, thinly sliced
2 tbsp white wine, 1 tbsp olive oil
method: Heat oven to 200C fan. Cut two large squares of baking paper.
Divide the courgette and fennel between them, sit the salmon on top and season.
Add the wine, oil, lemon slices, dill and a little butter, then fold into sealed parcels.
Bake for 12-14 minutes until the fish is just cooked. Open at the table, with new potatoes.

name: Omelette aux Fines Herbes
blurb: A soft, barely-set French omelette with chives, parsley, tarragon and chervil.
ingredients: 1 tbsp chopped mixed soft herbs (chives, parsley, tarragon)
method: Beat the eggs with the herbs, salt and pepper until just combined.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat until foaming.
Pour in the eggs and stir briskly with a fork while shaking the pan, for about 20 seconds.
Stop stirring, let the base set for a few seconds, then fold and roll out onto a plate while still creamy inside.

name: Beef Bibimbap
blurb: A hot rice bowl of seasoned vegetables, marinated beef, a fried egg and gochujang to stir through.
ingredients: 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil
method: Marinate the beef in the soy, sugar and sesame oil.
Blanch and season each vegetable separately with a little salt and sesame oil.
Sear the beef hard; build bowls with rice, veg, beef and a fried egg, with gochujang alongside.

name: Chicken Katsu Curry Bowl
blurb: Crisp panko chicken sliced over rice, blanketed in a mild, sweet Japanese curry sauce.
method: Soften the onion and carrot, stir in the curry powder and flour, add the stock and honey and simmer 15 minutes, then blend.
Crumb and shallow-fry the chicken until golden.
Slice over rice and pour the sauce alongside.

name: Salmon Poke Bowl
blurb: Diced raw salmon in a soy-sesame marinade over sushi rice with avocado, edamame and cucumber.
method: Toss the salmon with the soy, sesame oil and vinegar and chill 10 minutes.
Divide the rice between bowls.
Top with salmon, avocado, edamame and cucumber and scatter with sesame.

name: Teriyaki Tofu Donburi
blurb: Sticky glazed tofu over rice with quick-pickled cucumber and spring onion. Vegan comfort in a bowl.
method: Toss the tofu in cornflour and fry until crisp on all sides.
