Add the soy, mirin and maple and let it bubble to a glaze.
Serve over rice with vinegar-tossed cucumber and spring onion.

name: Nasi Goreng
blurb: Indonesian fried rice with kecap manis, prawns and chicken, topped with a fried egg and prawn crackers.
method: Fry the shallots, garlic and chicken, add the prawns.
Add the rice, kecap manis and sambal and fry hard for 4 minutes.
Top each bowl with a fried egg and prawn crackers.

name: Gyudon (Japanese Beef Bowl)
blurb: Thin beef and onion simmered in a sweet dashi-soy broth, spooned over rice with pickled ginger.
method: Simmer the onion in the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar for 5 minutes.
Add the beef and cook 3-4 minutes until just done.
Spoon over rice with the broth and top with ginger and spring onion.

name: Chicken Burrito Bowl
blurb: Chipotle chicken, coriander-lime rice, black beans, corn salsa and guacamole in a bowl.
method: Toss the chicken in the chipotle and fry until cooked.
Stir lime and coriander through the warm rice; warm the beans.
Build bowls with rice, beans, chicken, corn, guac and soured cream.

name: Loco Moco
blurb: A Hawaiian diner bowl: a beef patty and fried egg on rice, smothered in mushroom gravy.
method: Shape and fry two seasoned patties, remove.
Fry the mushrooms, stir in the flour, then the stock and Worcestershire to a gravy.
Serve the patties on rice with a fried egg and the gravy poured over.

name: Mapo Tofu Rice Bowl
blurb: Silken tofu and pork mince in a numbing, spicy Sichuan sauce over rice.
method: Fry the pork until crisp, add the doubanjiang, garlic, ginger and Sichuan pepper.
Add the stock and soy, slide in the tofu and simmer 4 minutes, then thicken with the cornflour slurry.
Scatter with spring onion and serve over rice.

name: Jollof Rice with Chicken
blurb: West African one-pot rice cooked in a smoky pepper-tomato base with roast chicken thighs.
ingredients: 2 red peppers, 2 tomatoes, 1 onion, 1 scotch bonnet, blended
method: Season and roast the chicken thighs until crisp.
Fry the purée, add the blended pepper base and curry powder and cook down for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice and stock, cover and steam 20 minutes, then sit the chicken on top.

name: Arroz con Pollo
blurb: Chicken and rice cooked together with peppers, peas, saffron and green olives. A Latin one-pot.
method: Brown the chicken, soften the onion, peppers and garlic with the cumin.
Stir in the rice, saffron and stock, sit the chicken back on top.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes, stir in the peas and olives, rest 5 minutes.

name: Chicken Yakisoba
blurb: Wok-fried noodles with chicken, cabbage and carrot in a tangy yakisoba sauce, topped with pickled ginger.
method: Stir-fry the chicken, add the cabbage and carrot for 2 minutes.
Add the cooked noodles and the sauces and toss over high heat.
Top with pickled ginger and a sprinkle of aonori or sesame.

name: Pad See Ew
blurb: Wide rice noodles charred in the wok with dark soy, egg, chicken and Chinese broccoli.
method: Fry the garlic and chicken, push aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the noodles, sauces and sugar and fry hard, letting the noodles catch.
Add the greens and toss until just wilted.

name: Bun Cha Bowl
blurb: Grilled lemongrass pork over rice vermicelli with herbs, pickled veg and a nuoc cham dressing.
ingredients: 1 stalk lemongrass, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp sugar
nuoc cham: fish sauce, lime, sugar, chilli, garlic
method: Mix the pork with the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce and sugar, form small patties and grill until charred.
Soak the vermicelli, drain, and pile into bowls with herbs and pickled carrot.
Add the pork and spoon over the nuoc cham.

name: Chirashi-Style Rice Bowl
blurb: Seasoned sushi rice scattered with sashimi, tamago, avocado and pickles. A no-roll sushi dinner.
ingredients: 2 portions sushi rice, seasoned with rice vinegar and sugar
method: Spread the seasoned rice in bowls.
Arrange the fish, avocado and tamago on top.
Finish with roe, ginger and wasabi, and serve soy alongside.

name: Halloumi & Grain Bowl
blurb: Griddled halloumi over lemony mixed grains with roasted veg, herbs and a tahini drizzle.
method: Roast the sliced veg at 210C for 20 minutes.
Griddle the halloumi until marked.
Toss the grains with lemon, oil and herbs, top with veg and halloumi, drizzle with loosened tahini.

name: Ropa Vieja Rice Bowl
blurb: Cuban shredded beef braised with peppers, olives and cumin, piled on rice with black beans.
ingredients: rice and black beans to serve
method: Simmer the beef in the stock with half the aromatics for 1.5 hours until it shreds.
Fry the peppers and onion, add the tomatoes, olives, cumin and oregano.
Fold in the shredded beef and reduce, serve on rice with beans.

name: Kimchi Jjigae
blurb: A bubbling Korean stew of aged kimchi, pork belly and tofu, served with a bowl of rice.
method: Fry the pork belly, add the kimchi and gochugaru and cook 5 minutes.
Add the stock, gochujang and sugar and simmer 15 minutes.
Slide in the tofu, warm through, top with spring onion; serve with rice.

name: Oyakodon
blurb: Chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy-dashi broth, set with loose egg and slid onto rice.
method: Simmer the onion in the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the egg, cover and cook 1 minute until just set, slide over rice.

name: Chicken Shawarma Bowl
blurb: Spiced chicken over turmeric rice with garlic sauce, pickled cabbage, tomato and parsley.
method: Toss the chicken in the spice and fry until charred at the edges.
Cook the rice with the turmeric.
Build bowls with rice, chicken, garlic sauce, pickled cabbage, tomato and parsley.

name: Thai Crab Fried Rice
blurb: Delicate wok-fried rice with white crab meat, egg, spring onion and a wedge of lime.
method: Scramble the eggs in a hot wok, add the rice and fry hard.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, fold in the crab and spring onion gently.
Serve with lime and cucumber.

name: Roasted Veg Buddha Bowl
blurb: Quinoa with roast sweet potato, chickpeas, kale and avocado under a lemon-tahini dressing.
method: Roast the sweet potato and drained chickpeas with oil and spice at 220C for 25 minutes.
Cook the quinoa; massage the kale with a little oil.
Build bowls and drizzle with tahini loosened with lemon, maple and water.

name: Chicken Chow Mein
blurb: Egg noodles stir-fried with chicken, beansprouts, cabbage and a soy-oyster sauce.
method: Stir-fry the chicken until nearly done, add the cabbage and spring onion.
Add the noodles and beansprouts and the sauces.
Toss over high heat for 2 minutes and finish with sesame oil.

name: Dakgalbi (Spicy Korean Chicken)
blurb: Chicken stir-fried with cabbage, sweet potato and rice cakes in a fiery gochujang sauce.
method: Marinate the chicken in the gochujang, gochugaru, soy and honey.
Stir-fry with the sweet potato until nearly cooked, add the cabbage and rice cakes.
Cook until the sauce is thick and glossy; serve with rice.

name: Ginger Veg Fried Rice
blurb: A bright, gingery vegetable fried rice with egg, edamame and sesame. Fifteen minutes, one wok.
method: Scramble the eggs, set aside.
Stir-fry the ginger, garlic, carrot and edamame, add the rice and fry hard.
Season with soy and sesame oil and fold in the egg and spring onion.

name: Pork Larb Rice Bowl
blurb: Zingy Thai minced pork with lime, fish sauce, toasted rice powder and herbs over steamed rice.
method: Fry the pork mince until cooked, breaking it up, then take off the heat.
Toss with the fish sauce, lime, ground rice, shallots and chilli.
Fold in the herbs and serve over rice.

name: Miso Vegetable Noodle Soup
blurb: A quick miso broth with udon, greens, mushrooms and a soft-boiled egg. Twenty minutes of comfort.
method: Simmer the mushrooms in the stock 5 minutes, then whisk in the miso off the boil.
Cook the udon separately and divide between bowls with the pak choi.
Ladle over the broth, add halved eggs, spring onion and sesame oil.

name: Sichuan Chilli Beef Noodles
blurb: Crispy shredded beef in a sweet-hot chilli sauce over noodles with pickled cucumber.
method: Toss the beef in cornflour and shallow-fry until crisp, drain.
Simmer the soy, vinegar, sugar, chilli bean paste and Sichuan pepper to a syrup and toss the beef through.
Serve over noodles with pickled cucumber.

name: Vegetable Bibimbap
blurb: A meat-free bibimbap loaded with seasoned spinach, carrot, courgette, mushrooms and a fried egg.
ingredients: sesame oil and salt for each vegetable
method: Cook each vegetable separately and season with sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Fry the eggs.
Arrange the vegetables over rice in sections, add an egg and serve with gochujang and kimchi.

name: Pineapple Fried Rice
blurb: Jasmine rice fried with prawns, cashews, egg and pineapple, seasoned with curry powder and fish sauce.
method: Scramble the eggs, set aside; toast the cashews.
Stir-fry the prawns, add the rice and curry powder and fry hard.
Season with fish sauce, fold in the pineapple, egg, cashews and spring onion.

name: Salmon & Avocado Donburi
blurb: Warm rice topped with soy-glazed salmon flakes, avocado, nori strips and sesame.
method: Pan-fry the salmon, add the soy, mirin and honey and glaze, then flake.
Divide the rice between bowls.
Top with salmon, sliced avocado, nori and sesame.

name: Massaman Chicken Rice Bowl
blurb: Mild, sweet-spiced massaman chicken with potato and peanuts, spooned over jasmine rice.
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream, add the chicken and coat.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, potatoes, fish sauce and sugar and simmer 30 minutes.
Stir in the peanuts and serve over rice.

name: Sweet Potato Katsu Curry
blurb: Panko-crumbed sweet potato slabs over rice with a mild vegan Japanese curry sauce.
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato, cut into 1cm slabs and par-boiled
method: Make the sauce: soften the onion and carrot, stir in the curry powder and flour, add the stock, simmer and blend.
Coat the sweet potato in flour, plant-milk batter, then panko and shallow-fry until golden.
Serve over rice with the sauce.

name: Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup
blurb: Braised beef shin in a spiced, soy-rich broth over wheat noodles with pickled mustard greens.
method: Blanch the beef, fry the aromatics and chilli bean paste, add the tomatoes.
Add the beef, soy, spices and stock and simmer 2 hours until tender.
Cook the noodles, ladle over the beef and broth, top with greens.

name: Huevos Rancheros
blurb: Fried eggs on tortillas with a smoky tomato-chilli salsa, black beans, avocado and coriander.
method: Fry the onion and garlic, add the tomatoes and chipotle and simmer to a salsa; warm the beans.
Fry the eggs and lightly char the tortillas.
Build plates with tortillas, beans, salsa, eggs and avocado.

name: Vegetable Pad Thai
blurb: Rice noodles tossed in a tamarind-palm sugar sauce with tofu, egg, beansprouts and peanuts.
method: Soak the noodles; fry the tofu until golden, push aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the drained noodles and the tamarind, sugar and soy and toss.
Fold in the beansprouts and spring onion, top with crushed peanuts and lime.

name: Jerk Chicken Rice & Peas Bowl
blurb: Marinated jerk chicken over coconut rice and kidney beans with charred pineapple salsa.
method: Marinate and grill the chicken until charred and cooked.
Cook the rice with the coconut milk, beans, spring onion and thyme.
Make a quick salsa with the pineapple, red onion and lime; build the bowls.

name: Miso Mushroom Donburi
blurb: Meaty mushrooms glazed in miso and butter over rice with a jammy egg and spring onion.
method: Fry the mushrooms hard until deep golden.
Add the miso, butter, mirin and soy and toss to glaze.
Serve over rice with a halved egg and spring onion.

name: Koshari
blurb: Egypt's national dish: layered rice, lentils and macaroni with spiced tomato sauce and crisp onions.
method: Cook the rice, lentils and macaroni separately.
Simmer the tomatoes with the vinegar, cumin and chilli to a sharp sauce.
Layer lentils, rice and macaroni, top with chickpeas, sauce and a big handful of crisp onions.

name: Chicken Adobo Rice Bowl
blurb: Filipino chicken braised in soy, vinegar, garlic and bay until glossy, over rice.
method: Marinate the chicken in the soy, vinegar, garlic, bay and pepper for 30 minutes.
Simmer everything gently for 30 minutes, then remove the chicken and reduce the sauce with the sugar.
Return the chicken to glaze and serve over rice.

name: Smoky Bean Jambalaya Bowl
blurb: Cajun-spiced rice with peppers, celery, kidney beans and smoked paprika. Vegan, hearty, one pot.
method: Fry the veg with the Cajun spice and paprika.
Stir in the rice, tomatoes, beans and stock.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes, rest 5, fluff.

name: Tonkatsu Rice Bowl
blurb: Crisp breaded pork loin sliced over rice and shredded cabbage with tonkatsu sauce and sesame.
method: Flatten the pork slightly, coat in flour, egg then panko.
Shallow-fry 3-4 minutes a side until deep golden, rest, then slice.
Serve over rice and cabbage with tonkatsu sauce and sesame.

name: Tofu Poke Bowl
blurb: Marinated tofu over sushi rice with mango, edamame, avocado, pickled ginger and sesame.
method: Toss the tofu with the soy, sesame oil and sriracha and leave 15 minutes.
Divide the rice between bowls.
Top with tofu, mango, avocado, edamame, ginger and sesame.

name: 20-Minute Chilli Garlic Noodles
blurb: Noodles tossed in a hot sizzling-oil dressing of garlic, chilli flakes, soy and black vinegar.
method: Pile the garlic, chilli flakes and white spring onion in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the oil until smoking and pour over to sizzle, then stir in the soy, vinegar and sugar.
Toss the cooked noodles through and top with green spring onion.

name: Thai Basil Beef Rice Bowl
blurb: Stir-fried minced beef with chilli, garlic and holy basil over jasmine rice with a crispy fried egg.
method: Pound the chilli and garlic, fry briefly, add the mince and brown hard.
Season with the oyster sauce, soy and sugar, then stir in the basil.
Serve over rice with a crisp fried egg.

name: Gochujang Glazed Tofu Bowl
blurb: Crispy tofu in a sticky gochujang glaze over rice with quick sesame greens and pickled radish.
method: Toss the tofu in cornflour and fry until crisp.
Add the gochujang, soy, maple and vinegar and toss to a sticky glaze.
Serve over rice with sesame-tossed tenderstem and pickled radish.

name: Bengali Egg Curry
blurb: Boiled eggs fried until blistered, then simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy. Serve over rice.
ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Rub the eggs with turmeric and salt and fry until golden and blistered, remove.
Fry the onions until deep brown, add the ginger-garlic, spices and tomatoes and cook to a thick gravy.
Return the eggs with a splash of water, simmer 5 minutes, serve over rice.

name: Margherita Pizza
blurb: A blistered, chewy base with a bright uncooked tomato sauce, torn mozzarella and basil.
ingredients: For the dough (makes 2): 300g strong white bread flour, 1/2 tsp instant yeast, 1 tsp salt, 200ml warm water, 1 tbsp olive oil
1 x 400g tin good plum tomatoes, hand-crushed and drained a little
1 garlic clove, grated; pinch of salt and sugar; drizzle of olive oil
2 balls mozzarella (about 250g), torn and patted dry
Fine semolina or flour, for dusting
method: Mix the dough ingredients into a rough ball, knead 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, then leave covered for 1-2 hours until doubled (or overnight in the fridge). Divide in two and shape into tight balls; rest 30 minutes.
Put a heavy oven tray or pizza steel on the top shelf and heat the oven as high as it goes (250C+) for 30 minutes.
Season the crushed tomatoes with the garlic, salt, sugar and oil.
Stretch one dough ball on a semolina-dusted board to a thin 28cm round, leaving a puffier rim. Spread with a thin layer of sauce and scatter over half the mozzarella.
Slide onto the hot tray and bake 6-9 minutes until the crust is charred in spots and the cheese is molten. Finish with basil and a little olive oil. Repeat for the second.

name: Pepperoni Pizza
blurb: The classic: crisp-rimmed base, tomato, mozzarella and cupped, spicy pepperoni crisping at the edges.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (as Margherita), divided into 2 balls
1 x 400g tin plum tomatoes, crushed and seasoned with garlic, salt, sugar and oil
2 balls mozzarella (250g), torn and patted dry
100g pepperoni or spicy salami, thinly sliced
Chilli flakes and a little honey, to finish (optional)
method: Make and prove the dough as for the Margherita. Heat the oven with a heavy tray inside at maximum for 30 minutes.
Stretch a dough ball thin on a floured board, leaving a raised rim.
Spread with a thin layer of tomato, scatter over half the mozzarella, then lay on half the pepperoni and a pinch of oregano.
Bake on the hot tray for 6-9 minutes until the crust is blistered and the pepperoni has curled and crisped.
Finish with chilli flakes and a thread of honey if you like. Repeat for the second pizza.

name: Garden Vegetable Pizza
blurb: Tomato base loaded with courgette, pepper and red onion, finished with rocket and lemon.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (as Margherita), divided into 2 balls
1 x 400g tin plum tomatoes, crushed and seasoned
Handful of rocket, lemon and olive oil, to finish
method: Make and prove the dough; heat the oven with a heavy tray at maximum for 30 minutes.
Toss the courgette, pepper and onion with a little oil and salt.
Stretch a dough ball thin, spread with tomato and scatter over half the mozzarella and half the vegetables.
Bake on the hot tray for 7-9 minutes until the crust is charred and the vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Top with rocket dressed in lemon and oil. Repeat for the second.

name: Nduja & Hot Honey Pizza
blurb: Fiery nduja melting into the cheese, cut through with a sharp drizzle of chilli honey.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (as Margherita), divided into 2 balls
1 x 400g tin plum tomatoes, crushed and seasoned
3 tbsp runny honey warmed with 1/2 tsp chilli flakes
Fresh basil or oregano, to finish
method: Make and prove the dough; heat the oven with a heavy tray at maximum for 30 minutes.
Stretch a dough ball thin, spread with a thin layer of tomato and scatter over half the mozzarella.
Dot half the nduja over the top so it can melt and spread as it bakes.
Bake on the hot tray for 6-9 minutes until blistered and bubbling.
Drizzle with the warm chilli honey, add herbs, and repeat for the second.

name: Beer-Battered Fish & Chips
blurb: Crisp, lacy beer batter around flaky white fish, with proper chunky chips and mushy peas.
ingredients: 4 skinless cod, haddock or pollock fillets (about 150g each)
1.2kg floury potatoes (Maris Piper), cut into 1.5cm chips
200g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
330ml very cold beer or sparkling water
300g frozen peas, 20g butter, sprig of mint (for mushy peas)
Lemon wedges and malt vinegar, to serve
method: Rinse the chips, dry very well, and fry at 140C for 6-7 minutes until soft but not coloured. Lift out and cool.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then whisk in the cold beer to a batter just thicker than double cream. Keep it cold.
Heat the oil to 180C. Dust the fish in flour, dip in batter, let the excess drip, and fry two pieces at a time for 5-6 minutes until deep gold and crisp. Drain on a rack in a low oven.
Turn the oil up to 190C and fry the chips again for 3-4 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain and salt.
Simmer the peas with a splash of water, drain, crush with the butter and mint. Serve everything hot with lemon and vinegar.

name: Jamaican Oxtail Stew
blurb: Oxtail browned and slow-braised with allspice, thyme, scotch bonnet and butter beans until falling off the bone.
ingredients: 2 tbsp browning or 1 tbsp dark soy + 1 tsp treacle
4 spring onions, 6 garlic cloves, 1 thumb ginger
2 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
method: Toss the oxtail with the browning and plenty of salt and pepper. Brown very well in batches in a heavy pot — take your time, this is the flavour.
Soften the onions, carrot, spring onions, garlic and ginger in the fat for 8 minutes. Stir in the allspice, thyme and tomato purée for 1 minute.

Return the oxtail, add the Worcestershire, whole scotch bonnet and stock to just cover. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook at 150C (or lowest hob) for 3 hours, turning once, until the meat is yielding.
Lift out the scotch bonnet. Add the butter beans and simmer uncovered for 20-30 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and the oxtail is falling apart.
Skim the fat, rest 15 minutes, and serve with rice and peas.

name: Brown Stew Chicken
blurb: Jamaican chicken marinated in green seasoning, seared dark and simmered in a rich onion-pepper gravy.
ingredients: 4 spring onions, 4 garlic cloves, 1 thumb ginger, small bunch thyme — blitzed to a paste with 1 tbsp oil
1 tbsp browning or 1 tbsp dark soy
Rice and peas or plain rice, to serve
method: Rub the chicken with the green seasoning paste and browning and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Scrape off most of the marinade (reserve it) and sear the chicken hard in a little oil until very dark on all sides. Lift out.
Fry the onions and peppers in the pan for 8 minutes, add the reserved marinade, ketchup and allspice for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken with the whole scotch bonnet, carrot and stock. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, then uncover for 10 more to thicken the gravy.
Remove the scotch bonnet before it bursts, check the seasoning, and serve over rice.

name: Escovitch Fish
blurb: Crisp-fried snapper or sea bream doused in a hot, sweet-sour vinegar dressing of peppers and onion.
ingredients: 4 whole small snapper or sea bream, scaled and slashed (or 4 firm white fillets)
1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp salt (to season the fish)
1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp allspice berries, a few pepper leaves or bay
Rice and peas or festival, to serve
method: Pat the fish very dry and season with allspice and salt. Shallow fry in hot oil for 4-5 minutes each side until crisp and golden. Drain and lay in a deep dish.
In a clean pan, warm 3 tbsp oil and soften the onions, peppers, carrot and scotch bonnet for 4-5 minutes so they still have crunch.
Add the vinegar, sugar, allspice berries and bay and bring to a quick boil.
Pour the hot pickle and all its liquid over the fish.
Leave at least 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge) for the flavours to soak in, then serve at room temperature with rice.

name: Trinidad Chicken Pelau
blurb: One-pot rice cooked in burnt-sugar caramel with chicken, pigeon peas and coconut.
ingredients: 3 tbsp green seasoning (blitzed spring onion, garlic, thyme, coriander, culantro)
1 x 400g tin pigeon peas (or kidney beans), drained
1 scotch bonnet whole, 2 tbsp ketchup, thyme
method: Marinate the chicken in the green seasoning for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot, add the sugar and let it caramelise to a dark bubbling amber.
Add the chicken and stir hard so it coats in the caramel and browns, 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the rice, peas, carrot, pepper, ketchup and thyme, then pour in the coconut milk and stock. Add the whole scotch bonnet and season.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 20-25 minutes until the rice is tender and a little sticky. Rest 10 minutes, remove the scotch bonnet, and fluff.

name: Chicken Yassa
blurb: Senegalese chicken braised in a mountain of slow-cooked onions sharp with lemon, mustard and chilli.
ingredients: 1 Scotch bonnet or 2 tbsp mustard, whole
method: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic and half the sliced onions with salt and pepper. Add the chicken and marinate for at least 1 hour (ideally overnight).
Lift the chicken out and sear it in the oil until deeply browned; set aside.
Add all the onions (marinade included) to the pan and cook down over medium heat for 20-25 minutes until soft, jammy and lightly caramelised.
Return the chicken with the bay, whole Scotch bonnet and 200ml water. Cover and simmer 25 minutes until tender, then uncover to reduce to a thick onion sauce.
Fish out the Scotch bonnet, stir in the olives, and serve over rice.

name: Doro Wat
blurb: Ethiopia's national dish: chicken slow-simmered in a deep, fiery berbere and caramelised-onion sauce with whole eggs.
ingredients: 60g niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) or 60g butter/oil
4 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, grated
4 hard-boiled eggs, peeled and lightly scored
method: Toss the chicken with the lemon juice and a little salt; set aside.
Cook the onions in a dry heavy pan over low heat, stirring often, for 20 minutes until collapsed and golden — no oil yet.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic and ginger and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the berbere and tomato purée and fry gently for 3-4 minutes until darkened and glossy.
Add the chicken, turn to coat, then pour in the stock. Cover and simmer very gently for 35-40 minutes until the sauce is thick and clinging.
Nestle in the boiled eggs for the last 10 minutes to take on colour. Serve with injera to scoop.

name: Bobotie
blurb: South African spiced beef mince baked under a savoury egg custard, with bay leaves and chutney.
ingredients: 2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp ground cumin
2 slices white bread soaked in 200ml milk
3 tbsp fruit chutney, 2 tbsp sultanas, 30g flaked almonds
Yellow rice (rice cooked with turmeric and a cinnamon stick), to serve
method: Fry the onions until soft, add the mince and brown well, then stir in the curry powder, turmeric and cumin for 2 minutes.
Squeeze the milk from the bread (keep the milk) and mash the bread into the meat with the chutney, sultanas, almonds and lemon juice. Season well.
Beat 1 egg and mix it through, then pack the mixture into a baking dish and smooth the top.
Beat the remaining 2 eggs with the reserved milk and pour over. Tuck in the bay leaves.
Bake at 180C for 30-35 minutes until the custard is just set and golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with yellow rice.

name: Chicken & Dumplings
blurb: Southern-style: shredded chicken in a creamy broth with pillowy dropped dumplings and peas.
ingredients: For the dumplings: 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 60g cold butter, small bunch parsley, about 120ml milk
method: Poach the chicken in the stock with a bay leaf for 20 minutes, then lift out, shred and set aside. Keep the stock.
Melt the butter, soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, then stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in the reserved stock and simmer to a light gravy. Add the cream, nutmeg and shredded chicken.
Rub the butter into the dumpling flour and baking powder, stir in the parsley and enough milk for a soft dough. Drop tablespoons on top of the gently bubbling stew.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes without peeking until the dumplings are risen and cooked through. Stir in the peas and serve.

name: Red Beans & Rice
blurb: New Orleans Monday supper: red beans slow-simmered creamy with the trinity and smoked sausage.
ingredients: 500g dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight (or 3 tins, drained — reduce simmer to 30 min)
1 onion, 1 green pepper, 2 celery sticks, diced
2 bay leaves, 1 tbsp Cajun seasoning, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp dried thyme
1 smoked ham hock or 100g smoked bacon (optional)
Steamed long-grain rice and sliced spring onion, to serve
method: Brown the sausage in a heavy pot and set aside. Soften the onion, pepper and celery in the fat for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the drained beans, bay, ham hock if using, and stock to cover by 4cm.
Simmer gently, part-covered, for about 1 hour 15 until the beans are very soft, stirring now and then.
Mash a ladle of beans against the side and stir back in to thicken the pot to a creamy gravy. Return the sausage, shred any ham hock meat back in, and add the vinegar.
Season and serve spooned over rice with spring onions.

name: Shrimp Étouffée
blurb: Prawns smothered in a blond-roux Cajun sauce with the holy trinity, over fluffy rice.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 green pepper, 2 celery sticks, finely diced
500ml shellfish or chicken stock (simmer the shells in it for 15 min, then strain)
1 tbsp Cajun seasoning, 1/2 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp smoked paprika
2 spring onions and small bunch parsley, chopped
method: Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 6-8 minutes to a peanut-coloured roux.
Add the onion, pepper and celery and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock and simmer for 12-15 minutes to a smooth, gravy-thick sauce.
Stir in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes just until pink and firm.
Fold through the spring onions and parsley, check the seasoning, and serve over rice.

name: Yankee Pot Roast
blurb: A whole braising joint slow-cooked with root vegetables until sliceable-soft, in its own rich gravy.
ingredients: 1.5kg beef brisket or chuck, in one piece
4 carrots and 3 celery sticks, in chunks
3 bay leaves, sprig of rosemary and thyme
method: Season the beef all over and brown it hard on every side in a heavy casserole. Lift out.
Brown the onions, carrots and celery in the fat for 8 minutes, stir in the tomato purée for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and let it bubble.
Return the beef, add the stock and herbs to come halfway up, cover and cook at 150C for 2 hours 30, turning once.
Add the potatoes and cook, still covered, for a further 45 minutes until everything is very tender.
Rest the beef 15 minutes, skim the fat, thicken the gravy with a little slaked cornflour if you like, then slice the beef against the grain and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

name: Beef Bulgogi
blurb: Thin beef marinated in soy, pear and sesame, seared fast and served over rice with kimchi.
ingredients: 600g sirloin or rump steak, sliced as thinly as you can (freeze for 30 min first)
Steamed rice and kimchi, to serve
method: Mix the grated pear, soy, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and gochugaru in a bowl. Add the beef and turn to coat. Leave 20 minutes at room temperature (or up to a day in the fridge).
Get a large frying pan or wok very hot with a little neutral oil.
Lift the beef from the marinade, letting excess drip off, and sear in two batches for 2 minutes each so it browns rather than stews. Return all the beef to the pan.
Add the marinade and the spring onions and toss for 1 minute until the sauce is sticky and glossy.
Scatter with sesame seeds and serve over rice with kimchi.

name: Japchae (Korean Glass Noodles)
blurb: Sweet-potato glass noodles tossed with sesame, soy and a rainbow of quick-fried vegetables.
ingredients: 2 tbsp toasted sesame oil, plus extra
method: Boil the noodles for 6 minutes until slippery and just tender, drain, rinse under cold water and snip a few times with scissors. Toss with 1 tbsp each soy and sesame oil.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, refresh, squeeze dry and season with a little sesame oil and salt.
Fry each vegetable separately in a hot pan with a drop of oil, seasoning lightly, so each keeps its colour: onion and pepper 2 minutes, carrot 1 minute, mushrooms 3 minutes with the garlic.
Combine remaining soy, sugar and sesame oil in a large bowl. Add the noodles, spinach and all the vegetables and toss thoroughly with your hands so everything is glossed.
Warm through in the pan for a minute, then finish with sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
blurb: Chewy rice cakes simmered in a fiery, slightly sweet gochujang sauce with fish cake and spring onion.
ingredients: 500g fresh or vacuum-packed Korean rice cakes (tteok)
150g Korean fish cakes or firm tofu, sliced
method: If your rice cakes are firm or from the fridge, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes so they soften.
Whisk the gochujang, gochugaru, soy, sugar and garlic into the water in a wide pan and bring to a simmer.
Add the rice cakes and fish cakes and cook, stirring often so nothing sticks, for 8-10 minutes until the sauce is thick and clings and the rice cakes are chewy.
Stir in the spring onions and cook 1 minute more. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens too much.
Top with halved boiled eggs and sesame seeds and eat hot.

name: Korean Fried Chicken
blurb: Double-fried for shatter-crisp skin, then tossed in a sticky sweet-spicy gochujang glaze.
ingredients: 1kg chicken wings or boneless thighs, cut into 4cm pieces
1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp white pepper, 1 tbsp grated ginger
2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar
3 garlic cloves crushed, 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
method: Toss the chicken with the salt, pepper and ginger. Whisk the cornflour, flour and baking powder, then whisk in the sparkling water to a thin batter.
Heat 6cm of oil to 160C. Dip the chicken in batter, let the excess run off and fry in batches for 6 minutes. Lift out and rest on a rack.
Turn the heat up to 190C and fry each batch a second time for 3-4 minutes until deep gold and very crisp. Drain.
Warm the gochujang, honey, soy, vinegar and garlic in a wide pan until glossy and just bubbling.
Off the heat, add the chicken and toss to coat every piece. Finish with sesame seeds and serve at once.

name: Doenjang Jjigae
blurb: A quick, deeply savoury Korean soybean-paste stew with tofu, courgette and mushrooms.
method: Whisk the doenjang and gochugaru into the water in a pot and bring to a simmer.
Add the potato and onion and cook for 8 minutes until the potato is nearly tender.
Add the courgette, mushrooms and garlic and simmer 5 minutes.
Slip in the tofu and warm through for 3-4 minutes without stirring too hard so it stays whole.
Scatter with spring onions and serve bubbling hot with a bowl of rice on the side.

name: Jjajangmyeon (Korean Black Bean Noodles)
blurb: Chewy noodles under a glossy, savoury-sweet black bean sauce loaded with pork and diced vegetables.
ingredients: 300g pork shoulder or belly, cut into 1cm dice
method: Fry the chunjang gently in the oil for 3-4 minutes to take off its raw edge, then scrape into a bowl.
In the same pan, brown the pork over high heat. Add the onion, potato and courgette and fry for 6-8 minutes until softening.
Return the fried paste with the sugar and garlic, add 300ml water and simmer for 10 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook 1 minute to a glossy, thick sauce.
Cook the noodles, drain and divide between bowls. Ladle over the sauce and top with cucumber.

name: Weeknight Shoyu Ramen
blurb: A soy-based chicken broth with springy noodles, jammy egg, greens and quick-glazed chicken.
ingredients: 1 thumb ginger sliced, 4 garlic cloves smashed
4 nests ramen or medium egg noodles
4 spring onions sliced, 1 sheet nori, chilli oil to serve
method: Bring the stock, 2 tbsp soy, ginger, garlic and dried shiitake to a gentle simmer while you cook everything else. Strain before serving.
Boil the eggs for 6.5 minutes, cool in iced water and peel.

Sear the chicken thighs skin-side down in a dry pan for 6 minutes until golden, flip and cook 4 minutes more. Add the remaining soy, the mirin and sugar and bubble to a sticky glaze. Rest, then slice.
Cook the noodles to packet time; blanch the pak choi in the same water for the last minute.
Divide noodles between deep bowls, pour over the hot broth, and top with sliced chicken, a halved egg, pak choi, spring onions, torn nori and chilli oil.

name: Pan-Fried Pork Gyoza
blurb: Juicy pork and cabbage dumplings, crisped on one side and steamed on the other, with a sharp dipping sauce.
ingredients: 200g white cabbage, very finely chopped and salted for 10 min, then squeezed
2 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, grated
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
For dipping: 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp chilli oil
method: Mix the pork, squeezed cabbage, spring onions, garlic, ginger, soy, sesame oil and sugar until sticky.
Put a heaped teaspoon on each wrapper, wet the edge, fold into a half-moon and pleat one side to seal. Sit each on its base.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large lidded frying pan. Add a batch of gyoza flat-side down and fry for 2 minutes until golden underneath.
Pour in 80ml water, cover immediately and steam for 4-5 minutes until the water has gone and the wrappers are translucent. Uncover and fry 1 minute more to re-crisp the base.
Serve crisp-side up with the dipping sauce.

name: Okonomiyaki
blurb: A thick Osaka-style cabbage pancake topped with sauce, mayo, bonito and a snow of seaweed.
ingredients: 8 rashers streaky bacon or thin pork belly slices
For topping: okonomiyaki or brown sauce, Kewpie or regular mayo
Bonito flakes and aonori (seaweed flakes), to finish
method: Whisk the flour, dashi and eggs to a smooth batter. Fold in the cabbage and spring onions — it will look mostly cabbage, that's right.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium. Spoon in half the mixture and pat into a 2cm-thick round.
Lay half the bacon over the top, cook 5 minutes until set underneath, then flip carefully and cook 5 minutes more so the bacon crisps.
Flip once more, bacon-side up. Slide onto a plate.
Zigzag with sauce and mayo, then shower with bonito flakes and aonori. Repeat for the second pancake.

name: Chicken Karaage
blurb: Ginger-and-soy marinated chicken thighs in a light potato-starch crust, fried shatteringly crisp.
ingredients: 700g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 4cm pieces
Lemon wedges, Kewpie mayo and steamed rice, to serve
method: Mix the soy, sake, ginger, garlic, sugar and pepper. Add the chicken and marinate for 20 minutes.
Beat in the egg, then add the potato starch and toss so each piece wears a loose, craggy coating.
Heat 4cm of oil to 170C. Fry the chicken in batches for 4 minutes, lift out and rest for 3 minutes.
Return each batch to the oil for a second 1-2 minute fry at 185C until deep gold and crisp. Drain on a rack.
Serve hot with lemon wedges to squeeze over, a blob of mayo and plenty of rice.

name: Nikujaga
blurb: Japanese comfort food: thin beef and potatoes simmered in a sweet soy-dashi broth until meltingly soft.
ingredients: 300g thinly sliced beef (sukiyaki cut) or rump, sliced thin
100g mangetout or green beans, to finish
method: Sear the beef in a little oil in a wide pan just until it changes colour, then push to one side.
Add the onions and carrots and fry for 3 minutes, then add the potatoes.
Pour in the dashi, soy, mirin, sake and sugar. Bring to a simmer and lay a round of baking paper directly on the surface as a lid.
Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are very tender and the liquid has reduced by half.
Add the mangetout for the last 3 minutes. Let it sit off the heat for 10 minutes before serving — it tastes better warm than piping hot.

name: Lemongrass Pork Banh Mi
blurb: Griddled lemongrass pork in a crisp baguette with quick pickles, cucumber, chilli and herbs.
ingredients: 600g pork loin or shoulder steaks, thinly sliced
3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar
1 carrot and 1/2 daikon (or extra carrot), shredded
3 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, pinch salt (for the pickle)
4 short baguettes or 1 large, cut into 4
1/2 cucumber sliced, 1 red chilli sliced, coriander and mint sprigs
method: Mix the lemongrass, fish sauce, sugar, garlic and oil, add the pork and leave 20 minutes.
Toss the shredded carrot and daikon with the vinegar, sugar and salt and set aside to pickle.
Get a griddle or frying pan smoking hot and cook the pork in a single layer for 2 minutes each side until caramelised at the edges.
Split the baguettes, pull out a little crumb, and spread with mayo (and pate if using).
Fill with pork, drained pickle, cucumber, chilli and a good handful of herbs. Press shut and eat.

name: Caramel Black Pepper Pork
blurb: Vietnamese-style pork simmered in a dark palm-sugar caramel sharp with fish sauce and lots of pepper.
ingredients: 4 tbsp palm sugar or light brown sugar
3 spring onions and 1 red chilli, sliced, to finish
method: Melt the sugar in a dry heavy pan over medium heat until it turns a deep amber caramel — watch it closely.
Carefully add 2 tbsp water (it will spit), then the fish sauce, soy and black pepper.
Add the pork, shallots, garlic and ginger and turn to coat in the caramel.
Pour in the coconut water, bring to a simmer, half-cover and cook gently for 35-40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is tender and the sauce is syrupy and clings.
Scatter with spring onions and chilli and serve with rice.

name: Mee Goreng
blurb: Bold Malaysian fried noodles with chicken, egg and greens in a sweet, spicy, savoury sauce.
ingredients: 400g fresh yellow egg noodles (or 250g dried, cooked)
2 tbsp sambal oelek or chilli paste
150g choi sum or pak choi, chopped
100g beansprouts, fried shallots and lime, to serve
method: Mix the kecap manis, soy, sambal and ketchup in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 3 minutes until nearly cooked. Push aside, pour in the egg and scramble.
Add the garlic, tomato and greens and toss for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss constantly for 2 minutes until everything is coated and slightly caramelised at the edges.
Stir through the beansprouts, then serve topped with fried shallots and lime wedges.

name: Chicken Khao Soi
blurb: Northern Thai curry noodle soup: coconut broth over soft noodles, crowned with a tangle of crisp ones.
ingredients: 6 chicken thighs, bone-in if you can
3 tbsp khao soi or massaman curry paste, plus 1 tsp curry powder and 1 tsp turmeric
Oil, for frying a handful of the noodles until crisp
To serve: lime wedges, sliced shallots, pickled mustard greens, coriander, chilli oil
method: Fry the curry paste, curry powder and turmeric in 2 tbsp oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the thick cream from the top of one tin of coconut milk and cook until the oil splits, then add the chicken and turn to coat.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the stock, add fish sauce and sugar, and simmer gently for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Meanwhile, fry a small handful of raw noodles in hot oil until puffed and golden; drain. Boil the rest of the noodles and divide between deep bowls.
Ladle the curry and chicken over the noodles, top with the crisp noodles and serve the garnishes alongside for everyone to add.

name: Chicken Chasseur
blurb: Bistro braise of chicken with mushrooms, shallots, white wine, tomato and tarragon.
ingredients: Small bunch tarragon and parsley, chopped
Mashed or boiled potatoes, to serve
method: Season the chicken well. Brown it skin-side down in the butter and oil in a wide pan for 6-7 minutes until deep gold, then turn and colour the other side. Lift out.
Add the shallots and mushrooms to the pan and cook for 6 minutes until browned. Add the garlic and tomato purée and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, scrape the base and let it reduce by half.
Add the stock and chopped tomatoes, return the chicken skin-side up, and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the chicken is tender.
Stir in most of the herbs, check the seasoning, and serve with potatoes, scattered with the rest.

name: Chicken Paprikash
blurb: Hungarian braise heavy with sweet paprika, finished with soured cream, over buttered egg noodles.
ingredients: 8 bone-in chicken thighs or 1 jointed chicken
300g egg noodles or nokedli, cooked and buttered
method: Brown the chicken in the lard in a heavy pan, then set aside.
Cook the onions in the fat over low heat for 12-15 minutes until soft and golden — this sweetness is the base of the dish.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika (it burns easily), then the peppers and tomatoes.
Return the chicken, add the stock, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until tender.
Whisk the flour into the soured cream, stir in a ladle of hot sauce to temper it, then stir it all back into the pan and warm through without boiling. Serve over buttered noodles.

name: Tartiflette
blurb: Alpine gratin of potatoes, bacon and onions blanketed in melting Reblochon.
method: Boil the potatoes whole until just tender, cool a little, then peel and slice 1cm thick.
Fry the lardons until crisp, add the onions and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Rub a baking dish with the cut garlic. Layer in half the potatoes, season, spoon over the bacon-onion mix and half the crème fraîche, then the rest of the potatoes and crème fraîche, with nutmeg.
Cut the Reblochon in half through its middle and lay it rind-side up on top.
Bake at 190C for 25-30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 5 minutes and serve with a sharp green salad.

name: Blanquette de Veau
blurb: A gentle white braise of veal (or chicken) with mushrooms and baby onions in a silky cream sauce.
ingredients: 900g veal shoulder or blade (or use chicken thighs), in large chunks
1 onion studded with 2 cloves, 1 carrot, 1 leek, 1 bay leaf
Chopped parsley and steamed rice, to serve
method: Put the veal in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil and skim off the foam. Add the studded onion, carrot, leek and bay, and simmer very gently for 1 hour 15 until tender. Strain, keeping 700ml of the broth.
Simmer the baby onions and mushrooms in a little of the broth for 10 minutes; set aside.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes without colouring. Whisk in the reserved broth and simmer to a smooth, coating sauce.
Whisk the cream and yolk together, add a ladle of hot sauce, then return to the pan off the heat and warm through without boiling. Sharpen with lemon.
Fold in the veal, onions and mushrooms, scatter with parsley and serve with rice.

name: Poulet Basquaise
blurb: Chicken braised with peppers, tomatoes, onions and a little chorizo, Basque-style, over rice.
ingredients: 1 tsp piment d'Espelette or mild chilli
method: Brown the chicken all over in a wide pan, then set aside. Fry the chorizo for 2 minutes and lift out too.
Cook the onions and peppers in the coloured fat for 12 minutes until soft and sweet. Add the garlic and piment d'Espelette for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, bay and thyme.
Return the chicken and chorizo, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, then uncover for 10 more to thicken.
Check the seasoning and serve over rice.

name: Beef Daube Provençal
blurb: Beef slow-braised in red wine with orange peel, olives and herbs until it collapses.
ingredients: 1.2kg beef shin or chuck, in large chunks
2 bay leaves, sprig of rosemary and thyme
Mashed or boiled potatoes, to serve
method: The night before, marinate the beef in the wine with the onions, carrots, garlic, orange peel and herbs.
Next day, strain, keeping the wine and vegetables separate. Pat the beef dry and brown it hard in a casserole, then set aside.
Fry the lardons and the marinated vegetables until coloured, stir in the tomato purée, then pour in the wine and let it bubble for 5 minutes.
Return the beef with the orange peel and herbs, top up with water to almost cover, cover and cook at 150C for 3 hours until fork-tender.
Stir in the olives, rest for 20 minutes, skim the fat, and serve with potatoes to mop the sauce.

name: Pollo al Ajillo (Spanish Garlic Chicken)
blurb: Chicken pieces fried golden with a whole head of garlic, sherry and bay — a tapas bar classic scaled up.
ingredients: 1 chicken, jointed into small pieces (or 8 thighs, halved)
1 whole head of garlic, cloves peeled and lightly crushed
Fried or crushed potatoes and crusty bread, to serve
method: Season the chicken generously. Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the chicken in a single layer, turning, for 12-15 minutes until deep golden and nearly cooked.
Add the garlic cloves and bay and fry gently for 3-4 minutes until the garlic is soft and nutty, not burnt.
Stir in the paprika and chilli flakes, then pour in the sherry and let it bubble and reduce to a glossy pan juice.
Cover and cook 5 minutes more until the chicken is cooked through.
Shower with parsley and serve with potatoes and bread for the garlicky oil.

name: Fabada Asturiana
blurb: A rich Asturian bean stew with chorizo, morcilla and smoked pork, barely spiced, deeply savoury.
ingredients: 500g dried large white beans (fabes or butter beans), soaked overnight
200g smoked pork belly or gammon, in one piece
method: Drain the beans and put them in a wide pot with the chorizo, morcilla, pork belly, onion, garlic and bay. Cover with cold water by 4cm.
Bring slowly to a simmer, skimming off any foam. Add the paprika and saffron.
Cook very gently, barely bubbling, for about 1 hour 15, adding a splash of cold water now and then to 'scare' the beans and keep them whole, until they are creamy and tender.
Lift out the meats, slice them, and return to the pot. Discard the onion and bay.
Let it settle off the heat for 15 minutes so the broth thickens, then serve in deep bowls with bread.

name: Bacalhau à Brás
blurb: Portuguese comfort food: flaked salt cod, straw potatoes and onions bound in soft scrambled egg.
ingredients: 500g salt cod, soaked 24-36 hours with water changes (or 500g fresh cod, lightly salted for 1 hour)
600g potatoes, cut into fine matchsticks (or 300g ready-made straw potatoes)
method: Poach the cod in barely simmering water for 8 minutes, drain, and flake into large pieces, discarding skin and bones.
Fry the potato matchsticks in batches in hot oil until crisp and golden; drain on paper. (Skip if using ready-made.)
Soften the onions and garlic in 3 tbsp olive oil over low heat for 12 minutes until sweet.
Add the flaked cod and warm through, then the crisp potatoes, tossing gently.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir over low heat for a minute until just softly set — it should be creamy, not dry. Off the heat, fold through olives and parsley and serve at once.

name: Albóndigas en Salsa
blurb: Spanish pork-and-beef meatballs simmered in a smoky tomato and almond sauce.
ingredients: 50g breadcrumbs soaked in 4 tbsp milk (or water)
1 egg, 3 garlic cloves crushed, small bunch parsley
method: Mix both minces with the soaked breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, half the parsley, paprika and cumin. Roll into 24 walnut-sized balls.
Brown the meatballs all over in a little oil, then lift out.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 8 minutes, add the rest of the garlic and the extra paprika for 1 minute.
Add the wine and reduce, then the tomatoes and ground almonds, and simmer 5 minutes.
Return the meatballs, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through and the sauce is thick. Finish with parsley and serve with bread.

name: Pisto with Fried Eggs
blurb: Spain's answer to ratatouille — soft stewed peppers, courgette and tomato — topped with a runny egg.
method: Soften the onions in the oil over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the peppers and cook 10 minutes until floppy, then the courgettes and garlic for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the tomatoes, paprika and sugar, season, and simmer gently for 15 minutes until jammy and most of the liquid has gone.
Make wells in the pisto and crack in the eggs, or fry them separately. Cover and cook 3-4 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks runny.
Serve straight from the pan with plenty of bread.

name: Currywurst mit Pommes
blurb: Berlin street food: sliced bratwurst under a spiced curry-ketchup sauce, with a pile of chips.
ingredients: 1 tbsp mild curry powder, plus extra to finish
method: Get the chips cooking.
Simmer the ketchup, passata, vinegar, Worcestershire, curry powder, paprika, cayenne and sugar in a small pan for 8-10 minutes until glossy and thick. Taste and adjust the heat.
Grill or fry the sausages until browned and cooked through, then slice into 2cm pieces.
Pile the sausage onto plates, spoon over the warm sauce and dust with more curry powder.
Serve with the chips and extra sauce for dunking.

name: Käsespätzle
blurb: Soft hand-scraped egg noodles baked with mountain cheese and a heap of sticky fried onions.
method: Whisk the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg into a thick, sticky batter and rest 15 minutes.
Fry the onions slowly in the butter for 20 minutes until deep golden and jammy.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Press the batter through a colander or spätzle grater into the water in batches; when the noodles float, give them 1 minute, then scoop out.
Layer the spätzle with the grated cheese in a baking dish, finishing with cheese.
Bake at 200C for 10 minutes until molten, top with the fried onions and chives, and serve with a sharp salad.

name: Steak & Kidney Pudding
blurb: A proper steamed suet pudding with a dark, gravy-rich filling of beef and kidney.
ingredients: 150g ox or lamb kidney, trimmed and diced
For the pastry: 300g self-raising flour, 150g shredded suet, pinch of salt, about 180ml cold water
method: Toss the steak and kidney in seasoned flour. Brown in batches, then add the onion for 5 minutes. Add the stock and Worcestershire, bring to a simmer, then cool completely (the filling goes in raw-ish; the steaming cooks it).
Rub the suet into the flour and salt, add enough water to make a soft dough. Roll out three-quarters and line a buttered 1.2-litre pudding basin.
Spoon in the filling and its gravy. Roll the rest of the dough into a lid, dampen the edges and seal.
Cover with pleated baking paper and foil, tie with string, and steam in a covered pan of simmering water (halfway up the basin) for 3 hours 30, topping up the water as needed.
Turn out, or serve from the basin wrapped in a napkin, with mash and greens.

name: Cornish Pasty
blurb: Shortcrust filled with beef skirt, potato, swede and onion, crimped and baked golden.
ingredients: For the pastry: 500g strong white flour, 120g cold butter, 120g lard, 1 tsp salt, about 175ml cold water
350g beef skirt or chuck, cut into 1cm dice
Plenty of salt and white pepper
method: Rub the fats into the flour and salt until crumbly, add the water and bring together to a firm dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, potato, swede and onion and season very generously — this is the key.
Divide the pastry into 4 and roll each into a 20cm circle. Pile a quarter of the filling on one half, add a knob of butter, and leave a border.
Brush the edge with egg, fold over and crimp the seam into a rope along the top. Cut a small steam hole.
Glaze with egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes, then 165C for 45 minutes until deep golden. Cool for 15 minutes before eating.

name: Bubble & Squeak with a Fried Egg
blurb: Leftover potato and greens fried into a crisp, craggy cake and topped with a runny egg.
ingredients: 500g cooked potato (leftover mash or boiled and crushed)
250g cooked greens — cabbage, sprouts, kale or leftover roast veg — chopped
Brown sauce or ketchup, to serve
method: Fry the onion in half the butter until soft. Mix into the potato and greens and season well.
Heat the rest of the butter and the oil in a non-stick frying pan. Press the mixture in to a thick cake and cook, undisturbed, for 6-7 minutes until a deep crust forms underneath.
Break it up roughly with a spatula, turn the pieces, press down again and cook another 5-6 minutes so plenty of edges catch and crisp.
Fry the eggs to your liking in a second pan.
Serve the bubble and squeak topped with the eggs and a squeeze of brown sauce.

name: Cheese & Onion Pie
blurb: A double-crust pie of sweet softened onions and mature cheddar, a proper Northern tea.
ingredients: Baked beans or peas, to serve
method: Cook the onions in the butter over low heat for 20-25 minutes until very soft and pale gold. Cool completely.
Mix the cooled onions with the cheese, crème fraîche, mustard, thyme and plenty of black pepper.
Line a 22cm pie dish with two-thirds of the pastry. Add the filling and level it.
Roll the rest for a lid, seal and crimp the edges, cut a couple of vents, and glaze with egg.
Bake at 200C for 30-35 minutes until deep golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with beans or peas.

name: Steak & Kidney Pie
blurb: A shortcrust or puff-topped pie with a dark, slow-cooked filling of beef and kidney in rich gravy.
ingredients: 200g ox or lamb kidney, cored and diced
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp tomato purée
method: Toss the steak and kidney in seasoned flour. Brown in batches in a little oil in a heavy pan, then set aside.
Soften the onions for 8 minutes, add the mushrooms for 4, then stir in the tomato purée.
Return the meat, add the stock, Worcestershire, bay and thyme. Cover and simmer very gently for 1 hour 30 until the beef is tender and the gravy thick. Cool completely.
Tip into a pie dish. Roll the pastry, lay it over, trim and crimp the edge, and cut a steam vent. Glaze with egg.
Bake at 200C for 30-35 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Serve with mash and greens.

name: Homity Pie
blurb: An open West Country pie of potato, leek and onion bound with cheese in a crisp shortcrust.
method: Line a 22cm tart tin with the pastry, prick the base, line with paper and beans, and blind bake at 190C for 15 minutes, then 5 minutes uncovered.
Boil the potatoes until just tender; drain.
Soften the leeks and onions in the butter over low heat for 15 minutes until sweet, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Fold the potatoes, leek mixture, most of the cheese, the cream and parsley together and season well. Pile into the pastry case.
Scatter with the rest of the cheese and bake at 190C for 25 minutes until golden. Serve warm with a sharp salad.

name: Pan Haggerty
blurb: A Northumbrian skillet cake of sliced potato, onion and cheese, fried and grilled until crisp and molten.
ingredients: 200g mature cheddar or Northumberland cheese, grated
Salt and plenty of black pepper
Green salad or baked beans, to serve
method: Melt the butter in a heavy 24cm frying pan. Layer in a third of the potatoes, then a third of the onions, season and add a third of the cheese. Repeat twice, pressing down.
Cover and cook over low heat for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the base is deep golden.
Uncover, scatter any remaining cheese on top and slide under a hot grill for 5 minutes until blistered and brown.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into wedges.
Serve straight from the pan with a salad or beans.

name: Welsh Cawl
blurb: A clear, honest broth of lamb, leek, swede and potato, traditionally eaten with bread and cheese.
ingredients: 800g lamb neck or shoulder, on the bone if possible
3 leeks, sliced (keep the green tops separate)
2 bay leaves, small bunch thyme and parsley
Crusty bread and grated cheese, to serve
method: Put the lamb in a large pot with the onions, bay and herbs. Cover with the water, bring to a simmer, skim, and cook gently for 1 hour 30.
Lift out the lamb, pull the meat from the bones in chunks and return it to the pot; discard the bones.
Add the carrots and swede and simmer 20 minutes, then the potatoes and the white of the leeks for 15 minutes more.
Stir in the leek greens for the last 5 minutes so they stay bright. Season well.
It is even better the next day. Serve in deep bowls with bread and cheese on the side.

name: Beef Cobbler
blurb: A beef and ale casserole topped with cheesy scone rounds baked until golden.
ingredients: For the cobbler: 300g self-raising flour, 75g cold butter, 100g grated cheddar, 1 tsp mustard powder, about 180ml milk
method: Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown in batches; set aside. Soften the vegetables for 8 minutes, add the tomato purée for 1 minute.
Pour in the ale and reduce by half, then add the stock, beef and herbs. Cover and cook at 160C for 1 hour 45 until tender.
Rub the butter into the flour and mustard powder, stir in most of the cheese, then add enough milk for a soft dough. Pat out and cut 8 rounds.
Sit the rounds on top of the hot stew, glaze with egg and scatter with the rest of the cheese.
Bake uncovered at 200C for 20-25 minutes until the cobbles are risen and golden.

name: Palak Paneer
blurb: Cubes of paneer in a smooth, vivid green spinach sauce with garam masala and a swirl of cream.
ingredients: 3 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, grated
1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric
3 tbsp double cream or coconut cream
method: Blitz the blanched spinach with the chillies and a splash of water to a smooth purée.
Fry the paneer in 1 tbsp ghee until golden on all sides; set aside (soak in warm water if you like it soft).
Crackle the cumin seeds in the rest of the ghee, add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, then the ginger-garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook to a paste, then stir in the spinach purée and 100ml water and simmer 5 minutes.
Fold in the paneer and cream, warm through, and serve with rice or naan.

name: Pilau Rice
blurb: Fluffy basmati cooked with whole spices, onion and a little colour — the side that makes a curry night.
ingredients: 300g basmati rice, rinsed until the water runs clear and soaked 20 minutes
1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 4 green cardamom pods, 1 bay leaf
1/2 tsp turmeric (or a pinch of saffron)
method: Heat the oil and fry the onion for 8-10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the whole spices and cumin seeds and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the drained rice and turmeric so every grain is coated.
Pour in the boiling water, add the salt, bring back to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 10 minutes.
Rest, covered and undisturbed, for 10 minutes, then fork through gently and serve.

name: Vada Pav
blurb: Mumbai's potato-fritter burger — spiced mash fried in gram-flour batter, in a soft roll with chutneys.
ingredients: 1 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 10 curry leaves, pinch asafoetida
For the batter: 150g gram flour, 1/4 tsp turmeric, pinch bicarb, water to a thick coating batter
Green chutney (coriander, mint, chilli) and tamarind chutney
Dry garlic chutney (blitzed garlic, peanuts, chilli, salt)
method: Temper the mustard seeds, curry leaves and asafoetida in the oil, add the ginger-garlic-chilli paste and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Mix into the mash with the coriander and salt. Shape into 8 balls and flatten slightly.
Dip each in the gram-flour batter and deep fry at 175C for 3-4 minutes until golden. Drain.
Split the rolls, spread one side with green chutney and the other with tamarind, and sprinkle in dry garlic chutney.
Sit a hot vada in each and press. Eat immediately, with a fried green chilli on the side.

name: Chicken Seekh Kebabs
blurb: Spiced minced chicken moulded onto skewers and grilled until charred, with mint yoghurt and flatbread.
ingredients: 1 onion, very finely chopped and squeezed dry
1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1/2 tsp ground cumin
Small bunch coriander and mint, chopped
Flatbreads, sliced onion and lemon, to serve
Mint yoghurt (yoghurt, mint, garlic, lemon), to serve
method: Mix the mince with everything except the serving items and knead for a minute until sticky and paste-like. Chill 20 minutes.
With wet hands, mould the mixture around metal skewers into sausage shapes, or shape into kofta if you have no skewers.
Grill, griddle or barbecue over a high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Rest briefly, then slide off the skewers.
Serve in warm flatbreads with sliced onion, lemon and plenty of mint yoghurt.

name: Railway Mutton Curry
blurb: A gently sour, potato-thickened lamb curry from India's colonial-era dining cars.
ingredients: 800g lamb or mutton shoulder, in chunks
2 tbsp curry powder (Madras strength), 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder
3 tbsp oil, curry leaves, coriander to finish
method: Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 12-15 minutes until deep golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then the spices for another minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a thick masala, then add the lamb and turn to coat.
Pour in 500ml water, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, then add the potatoes and cook 25 minutes more until both are tender and the sauce clings.
Stir in the tamarind and sugar, balance to a mild sourness, and serve with rice, scattered with coriander.

name: Chicken Chop Suey
blurb: A quick, brothy stir-fry of chicken and lots of crunchy vegetables in a light savoury sauce.
ingredients: 1 tin water chestnuts or bamboo shoots, drained
For the sauce: 300ml chicken stock, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp cornflour
method: Whisk the sauce ingredients together.
Stir-fry the chicken in a hot wok with 1 tbsp oil for 3-4 minutes until nearly cooked; lift out.
Add the onion, celery and pepper and stir-fry 2 minutes, then the garlic, mangetout and water chestnuts for 1 minute.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce and bubble for 1-2 minutes until lightly thickened.
Toss through the beansprouts so they keep their crunch and serve over rice.

name: General Tso's Chicken
blurb: Crisp battered chicken in a glossy sweet-sour-spicy sauce with garlic, ginger and dried chilli.
ingredients: 1 egg, 5 tbsp cornflour, 2 tbsp plain flour (for the coating)
For the sauce: 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp rice vinegar, 3 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp hoisin, 200ml chicken stock, 1 tbsp cornflour
4 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, minced
3 spring onions, sliced; steamed rice and broccoli, to serve
method: Toss the chicken with the egg, then the cornflour and flour, to a craggy coating.
Deep fry at 180C in batches for 4-5 minutes until deep golden and crisp; drain.
Mix the sauce ingredients. In a wok with 1 tbsp oil, fry the dried chillies for a few seconds, then the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce and bubble until thick and glossy.
Toss the crisp chicken through to coat, scatter with spring onions, and serve with rice and steamed broccoli.

name: Crispy Shredded Chilli Chicken
blurb: Strips of chicken fried shatteringly crisp and tossed in a sticky sweet-chilli sauce with peppers and onion.
ingredients: 600g chicken breast, cut into thin strips
1 egg white, 6 tbsp cornflour, pinch of salt (for the coating)
For the sauce: 4 tbsp sweet chilli sauce, 2 tbsp ketchup, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tsp chilli flakes
Spring onions and sesame seeds, to finish; egg-fried or steamed rice, to serve
method: Toss the chicken strips with the egg white, then the cornflour and salt, coating well.
Deep fry at 180C in small batches for 3-4 minutes until very crisp and golden; drain on a rack.
Pour off most of the oil, stir-fry the onion and peppers for 2 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the mixed sauce and bubble to a syrup, then toss the crisp chicken through fast so it stays crunchy.
Scatter with spring onions and sesame seeds and serve over rice.

name: Gado Gado
blurb: Indonesian composed salad of blanched vegetables, potato, egg and tofu under a thick peanut sauce.
ingredients: 200g firm tofu, fried golden and cubed
For the sauce: 6 tbsp crunchy peanut butter, 1 tbsp kecap manis, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp tamarind, 1 tsp sambal, 1 garlic clove, water to loosen
Prawn crackers and crispy shallots, to serve
method: Whisk the peanut sauce ingredients with warm water until it is a thick, pourable dressing. Taste for salt, sweet and sour.
Blanch each vegetable separately so it keeps its colour and bite, then cool.
Arrange the potatoes, beans, cabbage, beansprouts, cucumber, tofu and eggs in sections on a big platter.
Spoon over plenty of the peanut sauce, or serve it alongside.
Top with crispy shallots and serve with prawn crackers.

name: Filipino Pork Adobo
blurb: Pork simmered then reduced in soy, vinegar, garlic, bay and peppercorns until dark and glazed.
ingredients: 800g pork shoulder or belly, in 4cm chunks
1 whole head of garlic, cloves crushed
method: Combine everything except the sugar in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer, part-covered, for 40 minutes until the pork is tender. Do not stir for the first 10 minutes so the vinegar cooks off its rawness.
Lift the pork out. Add the sugar to the liquid and reduce it hard for 8-10 minutes to a dark, syrupy sauce.
Meanwhile, sear the pork pieces in a dry hot pan until browned and a little crisp at the edges.
Return the pork to the reduced sauce and toss to glaze.
Serve over rice, spooning over plenty of sauce.

name: Pancit Bihon
blurb: Filipino rice vermicelli tossed with chicken, prawns and vegetables in a savoury, citrus-sharp sauce.
ingredients: 4 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp fish sauce
Lemon or calamansi wedges, to serve
method: Stir-fry the chicken in a wok with a little oil until nearly cooked, add the prawns and garlic for 1 minute, then lift out.
Add the carrot, pepper and cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock, soy and fish sauce and bring to a simmer.
Add the drained noodles and toss constantly for 3-4 minutes until they have drunk up most of the liquid.
Return the chicken and prawns with the spring onions, toss through, and serve with lemon wedges to squeeze over.

name: Chicken Yakitori
blurb: Skewers of chicken thigh and spring onion, grilled and repeatedly dipped in a sweet soy tare.
ingredients: 8 boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3cm pieces
4 thick spring onions or 2 leeks, cut into 3cm lengths
For the tare: 6 tbsp soy sauce, 4 tbsp mirin, 2 tbsp sake, 2 tbsp sugar
Shichimi togarashi and steamed rice, to serve
method: Simmer the tare ingredients in a small pan for 5-8 minutes until slightly syrupy. Pour half into a bowl for dipping.
Thread the chicken and spring onion alternately onto skewers. Brush with oil and season lightly.
Grill or griddle over a medium-high heat for 4 minutes, turning, then start basting with the pan of tare and cook 4-5 minutes more, glazing each turn.
Give a final dip in the reserved tare.
Serve over rice with a shake of shichimi togarashi.

name: Sukiyaki
blurb: A sweet-savoury hotpot of thin beef, tofu, mushrooms and greens cooked at the table and dipped in raw egg.
ingredients: 1/2 Chinese leaf, chopped; bunch of spinach or chrysanthemum greens
For the warishita: 100ml soy sauce, 100ml mirin, 3 tbsp sugar, 100ml dashi or water
method: Mix the warishita sauce ingredients.
Heat a wide, shallow pan (a cast-iron one is ideal). Sear a few slices of beef in a little oil, then pour in enough warishita to come 1cm up the pan.
Add the leeks, mushrooms, tofu and Chinese leaf in sections and simmer for a few minutes.
Add more beef, the greens and noodles in batches as you eat, topping up with sauce and a splash of water as it reduces.
Each person cracks an egg into a bowl and dips the hot beef and vegetables into it before eating.

name: Chicken Tamales
blurb: Soft masa dough spread on corn husks, filled with shredded chilli chicken, folded and steamed.
ingredients: 20-24 dried corn husks, soaked in hot water
For the dough: 400g masa harina, 120g lard or vegetable shortening, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp salt, about 500ml warm chicken stock
3 dried guajillo and 2 ancho chillies, soaked
2 garlic cloves, 1/2 onion, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano
method: Blitz the soaked chillies with the garlic, onion, cumin, oregano and stock. Simmer with the shredded chicken for 15 minutes to a thick, saucy filling.
Beat the lard until fluffy, then work in the masa harina, baking powder and salt, adding warm stock until you have a soft, spreadable dough (a teaspoon dropped in water should float).
Spread 2-3 tbsp dough onto the smooth side of each husk, leaving borders. Add a line of filling down the middle.
Fold the sides of the husk over the filling, then fold up the bottom. Stand upright, open end up, in a steamer.
Steam for 60-75 minutes until the dough peels cleanly away from the husk. Rest 10 minutes before unwrapping.

name: Chiles Rellenos
blurb: Roasted poblano chillies stuffed with cheese, in a light egg batter, served in a warm tomato broth.
ingredients: 300g cheese (Oaxaca, mozzarella or mild cheddar), in batons
2 tbsp plain flour, plus more for dusting
For the sauce: 400g chopped tomatoes, 1/2 onion, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp oregano, 300ml stock
Steamed rice and refried beans, to serve
method: Blister the poblanos over a flame until blackened, steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then rub off the skins. Cut a slit in each, remove the seeds, and stuff with cheese.
Simmer the blitzed tomato sauce ingredients for 15 minutes; season and keep warm.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then fold in the yolks and 2 tbsp flour.
Dust each stuffed chilli in flour, dip in the batter and shallow-fry in hot oil for 2-3 minutes each side until golden and puffed. Drain.
Serve the chiles in shallow bowls with the warm tomato sauce ladled around, and rice and beans alongside.

name: Sopa de Fideo
blurb: Toasted vermicelli simmered in a light tomato broth — Mexico's quick, comforting noodle soup.
ingredients: 200g fideo (thin vermicelli, broken) or angel-hair pasta
To serve: crumbled feta, diced avocado, lime, coriander
method: Blitz the tomatoes, onion, garlic and chipotle to a smooth purée.
Toast the dry fideo in the oil in a pot over medium heat, stirring, until golden brown — watch it closely.
Pour in the tomato purée (it will splutter) and cook for 3-4 minutes until darkened and thick.
Add the stock and cumin, bring to a simmer and cook for 6-8 minutes until the noodles are soft and the broth slightly thickened.
Serve in bowls with feta, avocado, coriander and a good squeeze of lime.

name: Picadillo
blurb: Latin American spiced beef mince with tomato, olives, raisins and potato — for rice, tacos or stuffing.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 bay leaf
1 tbsp cider vinegar; steamed rice and black beans, to serve
method: Brown the mince well in a wide pan, breaking it up, then push aside and soften the onion, pepper and potato for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, paprika and bay for 1 minute, then the tomato purée for another.
Add the chopped tomatoes and 150ml water and simmer for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the olives, raisins and vinegar and cook 5 minutes more until thick.
Serve over rice with black beans, or use to fill tacos or peppers.

name: Beef Milanesa
blurb: Thin crumbed steak fried crisp, Argentine-style, with lemon and a tomato-and-onion salad.
ingredients: 4 thin sirloin or topside steaks, beaten to 5mm
2 eggs beaten with 2 crushed garlic cloves and chopped parsley
Chips or crushed potatoes, to serve
Tomato, red onion and lettuce salad with oil and vinegar, to serve
method: Season the steaks. Coat each in flour, then the garlicky egg, then a firm press into the breadcrumbs.
Chill the crumbed steaks for 15 minutes so the coating sets.
Shallow-fry in 5mm of hot oil for 2 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked. Drain on a rack.
Serve each milanesa with chips, the sharp salad and lemon to squeeze over.
For milanesa napolitana, top with tomato sauce, ham and mozzarella and flash under the grill.

name: Beef Empanadas
blurb: Hand pies of spiced beef, onion, egg and olive in a short, flaky pastry, baked golden.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp oregano, pinch chilli
2 hard-boiled eggs, chopped; 40g green olives, chopped
12 empanada discs (or 500g shortcrust, cut into 12 rounds)
method: Fry the onions in a little oil until soft and golden, add the spices for 1 minute, then the mince and brown well.
Stir in the tomato purée and 4 tbsp water and cook to a moist but not wet filling. Season, cool, then fold in the chopped egg and olives.
Put a heaped tablespoon of filling on one half of each disc. Brush the edge with water, fold over and seal, then crimp or fork the edge.
Sit on a lined tray, glaze with egg, and cut a small vent.
Bake at 200C for 20-25 minutes until deep golden. Good hot or at room temperature.

name: Ají de Gallina
blurb: Peruvian shredded chicken in a creamy, gently spiced yellow-chilli and walnut sauce, over rice and potato.
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts, poached and shredded (keep 400ml of the stock)
2 onions and 4 garlic cloves, finely chopped
4 slices white bread, soaked in 200ml milk
Boiled potatoes, rice, halved boiled eggs and black olives, to serve
method: Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft, add the garlic and ají amarillo paste and cook 3 minutes until deepened.
Blitz the soaked bread (with its milk) and stir it into the pan with the reserved stock and turmeric. Simmer to a smooth, thick sauce.
Stir in the walnut-Parmesan mix and the shredded chicken and warm through, loosening with stock if needed.
Season — it should be creamy, nutty and only mildly hot.
Serve over rice with a boiled potato or two, halved egg and a few olives.

name: Beef Rouladen
blurb: Thin beef rolled around bacon, onion, mustard and gherkin, browned and braised in red wine gravy.
ingredients: 8 thin slices topside or silverside (about 700g), beaten flat
German or Dijon mustard, for spreading
2 onions (1 sliced for the rolls, 1 chopped for the gravy)
Mashed potato and red cabbage, to serve
method: Spread each beef slice with mustard, season, lay on a rasher of bacon, some sliced onion and a piece of gherkin. Roll up tightly and secure with a cocktail stick.
Brown the rolls all over in a heavy pan, then set aside. Fry the chopped onion for 6 minutes, stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the stock and bay.
Return the rolls, cover and braise gently (hob or 160C oven) for 1 hour 30, turning once, until very tender.
Remove the sticks, reduce the gravy if needed, and serve with mash and braised red cabbage.

name: Jägerschnitzel
blurb: Crisp pork schnitzel under a rich hunter's sauce of mushrooms, onion and cream.
ingredients: Chopped parsley; chips or spätzle, to serve
method: Coat the pork in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Shallow-fry in oil and a little butter for 3 minutes each side until golden. Keep warm.
In the same pan, fry the onion and mushrooms in butter for 8 minutes until browned.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then the stock, and reduce again.
Stir in the cream and simmer to a coating sauce; season well.
Serve the schnitzels with the hunter's sauce spooned over, parsley on top, and chips or spätzle alongside.

name: Gołąbki (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
blurb: Cabbage leaves wrapped around pork, beef and rice, baked in a light tomato sauce until tender.
ingredients: 1 egg, 1 tsp marjoram, salt and pepper
For the sauce: 700g passata, 400ml stock, 1 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tsp sugar, 1 bay leaf
method: Core the cabbage and simmer it whole for 8-10 minutes, peeling off leaves as they soften. Shave down the thick rib of each leaf.
Mix the minces, cooked rice, softened onion, egg and marjoram and season well.
Put a sausage of filling near the base of each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up. Pack seam-down into a baking dish.
Stir the sauce ingredients together and pour over so the rolls are nearly covered.
Cover with foil and bake at 180C for 1 hour, then uncover for 15 minutes. Serve with mash and plenty of sauce.

name: Bigos (Hunter's Stew)
blurb: Poland's long-simmered stew of sauerkraut, fresh cabbage, several meats and sausage, deep and smoky.
ingredients: 6 juniper berries, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp caraway, 1 tsp paprika
500ml stock; a splash of red wine
Rye bread or boiled potatoes, to serve
method: Brown the pork and bacon in a large pot, then set aside. Soften the onions in the fat for 8 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, fresh cabbage, drained mushrooms (chop them), tomato purée and spices and stir well.
Return the meats, add the sausage, stock and wine, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook very gently for 2 hours, stirring now and then, until everything is meltingly soft and the liquid has cooked down.
Bigos improves reheated over 2-3 days. Serve with rye bread or potatoes.

name: Chicken Fricassée
blurb: Chicken gently cooked in a velvety white sauce with mushrooms, baby onions and a lift of lemon.
ingredients: Juice of 1/2 lemon; parsley and rice, to serve
method: Colour the chicken lightly in half the butter (you want pale gold, not brown), then set aside.
Soften the onions and mushrooms in the rest of the butter for 6 minutes, then stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
