Add the wine, let it bubble, then whisk in the stock. Return the chicken and simmer, part-covered, for 25 minutes until tender.
Whisk the cream and yolk, add a ladle of hot sauce, then stir back into the pan off the heat and warm gently without boiling.
Sharpen with lemon, scatter with parsley, and serve over rice.

name: Choucroute Garnie
blurb: Alsatian sauerkraut braised in wine with juniper, piled with sausages, smoked pork and potatoes.
ingredients: 6 juniper berries, 4 cloves, 2 bay leaves, 10 peppercorns (tied in muslin)
400ml dry Riesling or other dry white wine
400g piece of smoked gammon or pork loin
800g small potatoes; Dijon mustard, to serve
method: Fry the lardons in a large casserole until the fat runs, add the onions and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, the spice bag, wine and stock. Bury the piece of gammon in the middle.
Cover and braise gently (hob or 160C oven) for 45 minutes.
Nestle in the sausages and the potatoes and cook, covered, for a further 30 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the sausages hot through.
Discard the spice bag. Pile the sauerkraut on a platter with the sliced meats and potatoes around it, and serve with plenty of mustard.

name: Sausages with Aligot
blurb: Toulouse sausages in red wine gravy with aligot — mashed potato beaten with garlic and stretchy cheese.
ingredients: For the aligot: 1kg floury potatoes, 100g butter, 150ml warm milk, 3 garlic cloves crushed, 250g mozzarella (or tomme fraîche), grated
method: Boil the potatoes until very soft, drain and mash smooth (or pass through a ricer). Beat in the butter, garlic and warm milk over low heat.
Add the mozzarella a handful at a time, beating hard with a wooden spoon, until the mash turns glossy and stretches in ribbons. Keep warm.
Brown the sausages, set aside, then soften the onions in the pan for 10 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce, then the stock and mustard, and simmer to a glossy gravy. Return the sausages to warm through.
Serve the sausages and gravy over a big spoon of stretchy aligot, with a sharp salad.

name: Pipérade with Baked Eggs
blurb: Basque stew of sweet peppers, onion and tomato spiced with piment d'Espelette, finished with eggs and ham.
ingredients: 1 tsp piment d'Espelette or mild chilli, 1 tsp smoked paprika
method: Soften the onions in the oil over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the peppers and cook for 12-15 minutes until completely soft, then the garlic, piment d'Espelette and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes until jammy. Season well.
Make wells and crack in the eggs (or lay the ham over first). Cover and cook 4-5 minutes until the whites are just set.
Serve from the pan with bread, the ham draped over if using.

name: Chicken-Fried Steak
blurb: Tenderised beef in a craggy crust, fried like fried chicken and smothered in black pepper cream gravy.
ingredients: 4 cube steaks or thin sirloin, tenderised
150g plain flour seasoned with 1 tsp each salt, pepper, paprika, garlic granules
For the gravy: 3 tbsp of the frying fat, 3 tbsp flour, 500ml whole milk, lots of black pepper
Mash and green beans, to serve
method: Dredge each steak in the seasoned flour, then the egg-buttermilk, then the flour again, pressing hard.
Shallow-fry in 1cm of hot oil for 3 minutes each side until deep golden and crisp. Drain on a rack and keep warm.
Pour off all but 3 tbsp of the fat. Whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then gradually whisk in the milk.
Simmer to a thick, pourable gravy and season with plenty of black pepper and salt.
Serve the steaks blanketed in gravy, with mash and beans.

name: Tuna Noodle Casserole
blurb: The classic bake — pasta, tuna, peas and mushrooms in a creamy sauce under a crunchy crumb.
ingredients: 60g panko tossed with 1 tbsp melted butter, for the top
method: Cook the pasta until just short of done; drain.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk and simmer to a smooth sauce. Stir in the cheese and mustard.
Fold in the pasta, fried mushrooms, tuna and peas and season well.
Tip into a baking dish and scatter with the buttered panko.
Bake at 200C for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and the top is golden and crunchy.

name: Tater Tot Hotdish
blurb: Midwest one-dish supper — seasoned beef and vegetables under a lid of crisp potato tots.
ingredients: 1 tsp onion granules, 1 tsp garlic granules, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
300g frozen mixed vegetables (green beans, corn, carrot)
method: Brown the mince with the onion, then drain off excess fat and season.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then the milk and stock, and simmer to a gravy. Add the granules, Worcestershire and half the cheese.
Stir the mince and frozen vegetables into the sauce and tip into a large baking dish.
Line the top completely with potato tots in neat rows and scatter with the rest of the cheese.
Bake at 200C for 35-40 minutes until the tots are deep golden and crisp and the filling bubbles at the edges.

name: Cubano (Cuban Sandwich)
blurb: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard pressed in a buttered roll until crisp and molten.
ingredients: 1 large soft baguette or 2 Cuban rolls
200g leftover roast pork or slow-cooked mojo pork, sliced
method: Split the bread. Spread the cut sides with mustard.
Layer on the ham, roast pork, cheese and a line of pickles, then close the sandwich.
Butter the outside of the bread generously.
Press in a hot dry pan or panini press with a weight on top (a second heavy pan) for 3-4 minutes each side until the bread is flat, crisp and golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut on a sharp diagonal and eat hot.

name: Guyanese Cook-Up Rice
blurb: A one-pot of rice cooked in coconut milk with black-eyed peas, chicken and thyme until sticky and rich.
ingredients: 2 tbsp green seasoning (blitzed spring onion, garlic, thyme, coriander)
1 onion, chopped; few sprigs thyme; 1 scotch bonnet, whole
2 tbsp oil; 1 tbsp browning or dark soy
method: Marinate the chicken in the green seasoning for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil, add the browning, then brown the chicken with the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the peas, rice, thyme and whole scotch bonnet and stir to coat.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, season, and bring to a boil. Cover and cook on low for 20-25 minutes until the rice is tender and a little sticky.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat, remove the scotch bonnet, and fork through.

name: Beef Maafe
blurb: West African groundnut stew — beef and root vegetables simmered in a deep peanut and tomato sauce.
ingredients: 1 sweet potato and 1 carrot, in chunks
method: Brown the beef well in a heavy pot, then set aside. Soften the onions and garlic for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato purée for 2 minutes, then the chopped tomatoes and the water, and bring to a simmer.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of the hot liquid until smooth, then stir it back in. Return the beef with the whole scotch bonnet and stock cube.
Simmer gently, part-covered, for 1 hour, then add the sweet potato and carrot and cook 40 minutes more until everything is tender and the sauce is thick and oil-flecked.
Remove the scotch bonnet and serve over rice.

name: Shiro Wat
blurb: A smooth, fast Ethiopian stew of spiced chickpea flour simmered with berbere and garlic.
ingredients: 150g shiro powder (spiced chickpea/broad bean flour) — or 150g gram flour + 1 extra tbsp berbere
method: Cook the onion in the oil over low heat for 10 minutes until very soft, adding the garlic for the last 2.
Stir in the berbere and tomato purée and fry gently for 2 minutes until darkened.
Add the water and bring to a simmer.
Rain in the shiro powder while whisking constantly to avoid lumps, then simmer gently for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until thick, smooth and no longer raw-tasting.
Loosen with a little water to a pourable stew and serve with injera to scoop, plus a tomato-onion salad.

name: Chakalaka with Pap
blurb: South African spiced vegetable relish — peppers, carrot, beans and curry spice — with soft maize porridge.
ingredients: 1 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp chilli
1 x 400g tin baked beans (yes, really) or cannellini
For the pap: 250g coarse maize meal, 1 litre water, 1 tsp salt, knob of butter (optional)
method: For the pap, bring the salted water to a boil, rain in the maize meal while whisking, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and smooth. Beat in butter if using.
Fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, peppers and spices for 2 minutes.
Add the grated carrot and cook 3 minutes until it softens.
Stir in the tomatoes and beans and simmer 10 minutes to a thick, glossy relish. Season.
Serve the chakalaka warm or at room temperature, spooned over a mound of hot pap.

name: KFC-Style Fakeaway Chicken
blurb: Buttermilk-brined chicken in a heavily seasoned crust, oven-baked or air-fried instead of deep-fried.
ingredients: 300ml buttermilk (or milk + 1 tbsp lemon juice), 1 tsp salt (to brine)
For the coating: 150g flour, 1 tbsp each smoked paprika, garlic granules, onion granules, 1 tsp each white pepper, black pepper, celery salt, dried oregano, dried thyme, ginger, mustard powder
Corn on the cob, chips or a bap, to serve
method: Brine the chicken in the salted buttermilk for at least 1 hour (or overnight).
Heat the oven to 200C fan and put a wire rack over a tray.
Mix all the coating spices into the flour. Lift each piece of chicken from the buttermilk, letting the excess drip, and press firmly into the flour for a thick, craggy crust.
Sit on the rack, spray generously all over with oil, and bake for 35-40 minutes (or air-fry at 190C for 25), turning once, until deep golden and cooked through (75C).
Rest 5 minutes and serve with corn and chips.

name: Big Mac-Style Burger
blurb: Two thin beef patties, melty cheese, shredded lettuce, pickles and a tangy special sauce in a sesame bun.
ingredients: 600g beef mince (15% fat), formed into 8 thin patties
4 sesame burger buns (plus 4 extra bun bases for the 'middle', optional)
Sliced dill pickles, 1/2 onion finely diced
For the sauce: 6 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp burger relish or finely chopped gherkin, 1 tbsp ketchup, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tsp white wine vinegar, 1/2 tsp paprika, pinch garlic and onion granules
method: Mix the special sauce and chill.
Season the patties and sear on a very hot flat pan or griddle for 1-2 minutes each side, adding a slice of cheese to melt on each.
Lightly toast the bun surfaces.
Build: base bun, sauce, onion, pickles, lettuce, a patty; then (if doing the triple-decker) a middle bun, more sauce and toppings and the second patty; then the lid.
Press gently and eat straight away.

name: Bang Bang Chicken
blurb: Crisp coated chicken pieces tossed in a creamy sweet-chilli and sriracha sauce, over rice or in a wrap.
ingredients: Low-cal spray oil (for oven/air-fryer) or oil for shallow frying
For the sauce: 4 tbsp light mayo, 3 tbsp sweet chilli sauce, 1 tbsp sriracha, 1 tsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp honey
Spring onions, sesame seeds; steamed rice and shredded lettuce, to serve
method: Coat the chicken in cornflour, then beaten egg, then panko.
Air-fry at 200C for 12-14 minutes (spray with oil, shake once), or oven-bake at 220C for 18 minutes, or shallow fry until golden and cooked through.
Whisk the sauce ingredients in a large bowl.
Tip the hot crisp chicken into the sauce and toss gently to coat.
Serve over rice with shredded lettuce, scattered with spring onions and sesame seeds.

name: Enchilada Lasagne
blurb: Layers of tortilla, spiced beef and beans, salsa and cheese, baked like a lasagne and cut into squares.
ingredients: 700g beef mince (or turkey mince for lighter)
3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp fajita or taco seasoning, 1 tsp smoked paprika
1 x 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 1 x 400g tin black beans, drained
1 x 400g tin kidney beans, drained; 200g sweetcorn
500g jar tomato salsa or enchilada sauce
250g grated cheese; soured cream, coriander, jalapeños, to serve
method: Brown the mince with the onion and pepper, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, beans and corn. Simmer 10 minutes to a thick chilli.
Spread a little salsa in a large baking dish. Layer: tortillas, a third of the mince, salsa, cheese. Repeat twice, finishing with tortillas, salsa and a thick layer of cheese.
Cover with foil and bake at 190C for 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until bubbling and golden.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut into squares and serve with soured cream, coriander and jalapeños.

name: Char Kway Teow
blurb: Smoky wok-fried flat rice noodles with prawns, egg, chinese sausage and beansprouts.
ingredients: 400g fresh wide flat rice noodles (ho fun), loosened
1 tbsp dark soy, 2 tbsp light soy, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar
method: Mix the soy sauces, oyster sauce, sugar and chilli paste in a small bowl.
Get a wok scorching hot with 1 tbsp oil. Fry the sausage for 1 minute, add the garlic and prawns and stir-fry until the prawns just turn pink.
Push everything aside, add a splash more oil and the eggs, and scramble roughly.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss hard for 2 minutes, letting the noodles catch a little for smokiness.
Throw in the beansprouts and spring onions, toss 30 seconds so they stay crunchy, and serve at once.

name: Nasi Lemak
blurb: Fragrant coconut rice with a fiery sambal, crunchy peanuts, cucumber and a fried egg.
ingredients: 3 pandan leaves knotted (optional), 1 slice ginger, 1/2 tsp salt
For the sambal: 6 dried chillies soaked, 2 shallots, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp shrimp paste (optional), 1 tbsp tamarind, 1 tbsp sugar
Crispy fried shallots and lime, to serve
method: Cook the rice with the coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt — bring to a boil, cover, lowest heat 12 minutes, then rest 10.

Blitz the sambal chillies, shallots, garlic and shrimp paste to a paste. Fry in 3 tbsp oil over medium-low for 10-12 minutes until dark and split, then stir in the tamarind and sugar and cook to a jammy relish.
Fry the eggs with crispy lacy edges.
Fluff the rice and mound onto plates.
Add a spoon of sambal, a pile of peanuts, cucumber slices, an egg and a scatter of fried shallots, with lime to squeeze.

name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
blurb: Silky poached chicken with rice cooked in the poaching stock, and three punchy dipping sauces.
ingredients: 1 thumb ginger sliced, 4 spring onions, 6 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp salt
1 tbsp chicken fat or oil, 2 garlic cloves and 2cm ginger minced (for the rice)
Chilli sauce: 4 red chillies, 2 garlic cloves, 2cm ginger, 1 tbsp lime, pinch sugar, 3 tbsp stock — blitzed
Ginger-scallion: 4 tbsp minced ginger and 6 spring onions with 4 tbsp hot oil and a pinch of salt
Cucumber slices and coriander, to serve
method: Put the chicken in a snug pot with the ginger, spring onions, garlic and salt. Cover with cold water, bring just to a bare simmer, then poach very gently for 35-40 minutes (barely a bubble). Lift out and plunge into iced water for 5 minutes, then rub with a little sesame oil. Keep the stock.
Fry the minced garlic and ginger in the chicken fat, add the rinsed rice and toast 2 minutes, then cook with 480ml of the hot poaching stock — boil, cover, lowest heat 12 minutes, rest 10.
Make the chilli sauce and the ginger-scallion sauce.
Carve the chicken into pieces.
Serve the chicken over or beside the rice with a bowl of hot clear stock, cucumber, and the three sauces plus dark soy.

name: Chinese Takeaway Chicken Curry
blurb: That glossy, mild, slightly sweet chip-shop curry sauce over chicken, peas and onions with rice.
ingredients: Steamed rice or chips, to serve
method: Fry the onions in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until very soft and pale gold.
Stir in the curry powder, five-spice, turmeric and ginger and cook 1 minute, then the flour for another minute.
Gradually whisk in the stock, add the soy and sugar, and simmer for 10 minutes until smooth and glossy. Blitz for the classic silky texture if you like.
Add the chicken and peas and simmer for 6-8 minutes until the chicken is cooked and the sauce coats a spoon.
Serve over rice or with chips.

name: Hot & Sour Soup
blurb: A peppery, vinegar-sharp broth thick with tofu, mushrooms, bamboo and ribbons of egg.
ingredients: 150g firm tofu, cut into thin batons
1 small tin bamboo shoots, drained and shredded
1 tbsp chilli oil or chilli bean paste
3 tbsp cornflour mixed with 5 tbsp water
2 eggs, beaten; 2 spring onions and 1 tsp sesame oil, to finish
method: Bring the stock to a simmer with the mushrooms and bamboo shoots and cook 5 minutes.
Add the tofu, soy sauce, vinegar, white pepper and chilli oil.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and simmer 2 minutes until the soup thickens to a light gravy.
Turn off the heat. Pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream while stirring gently so it sets in ribbons.
Taste and add more vinegar or pepper — it should make you sniff. Finish with spring onions and sesame oil.

name: Egg Foo Young
blurb: Fluffy Cantonese omelettes packed with prawns and vegetables under a glossy brown gravy.
ingredients: 150g cooked small prawns or shredded char siu
1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil (for the egg)
For the gravy: 300ml chicken stock, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp cornflour slaked in water
method: Simmer the gravy ingredients (except cornflour) for 2 minutes, then stir in the slaked cornflour and cook to a glossy sauce. Keep warm.
Mix the beaten eggs with the prawns, beansprouts, spring onions, water chestnuts, soy and sesame oil.
Heat a good slick of oil in a small frying pan over medium-high. Ladle in about a quarter of the mixture and fry for 2 minutes until golden underneath, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
Repeat for the rest, keeping the omelettes warm.
Serve on rice with the hot gravy poured over.

name: Beef Chow Fun
blurb: Wide rice noodles and marinated beef seared hard in a smoky, dark-soy wok toss with beansprouts.
ingredients: 250g rump or flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
1 tsp cornflour, 1 tsp soy, 1 tsp shaoxing wine (to marinate)
400g fresh wide flat rice noodles, loosened
1 tbsp dark soy, 1 tbsp light soy, 1 tsp sugar
method: Toss the beef with the cornflour, soy and wine and leave 10 minutes.
Get a wok smoking hot with 1 tbsp oil. Sear the beef in one layer for 1 minute without moving, then toss for 30 seconds and tip out.
Add a little more oil and the garlic, then the noodles. Add the dark and light soy and sugar and toss gently but firmly for 2 minutes, letting the noodles catch.
Return the beef with the beansprouts and spring onions and toss for 30 seconds.
Serve straight from the wok.

name: Pork Sinigang
blurb: A bright, sour Filipino tamarind broth with pork ribs, daikon, green beans and water spinach.
ingredients: 800g pork ribs or belly, in chunks
1 bunch water spinach or spinach, chopped
Fish sauce, to season; steamed rice, to serve
method: Put the pork, onion and tomatoes in a pot with the water. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 45 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the tamarind paste until dissolved and the broth turns properly sour — add more to taste.
Add the daikon and simmer 8 minutes, then the aubergine, beans and whole chillies for 5 minutes.
Stir in the greens and cook 1 minute until just wilted.
Season with fish sauce — it should be sour first, salty second. Serve in bowls with rice.

name: Kare-Kare
blurb: Filipino oxtail and vegetables in a thick, mild peanut and toasted-rice sauce, with salty shrimp paste on the side.
ingredients: 80g smooth peanut butter, plus 40g ground roasted peanuts
3 tbsp raw rice, toasted and ground to a powder
2 tbsp annatto seeds steeped in 4 tbsp hot oil (or 1 tsp paprika)
1 aubergine sliced, 150g green beans, 1 bundle pak choi or banana heart
method: Simmer the oxtail with the onion and garlic in water to cover for 2.5-3 hours until very tender. Keep 1 litre of the stock.
Strain the annatto oil into a wide pan and warm it. Whisk in the peanut butter, ground peanuts and toasted rice powder, then the reserved stock, and simmer to a thick, smooth gravy.
Add the oxtail and season with the fish sauce.
Blanch or fry the aubergine, beans and greens separately until just tender and add to the pot to warm through.
Serve with rice and a small dish of shrimp paste to stir in bite by bite.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Grilled Chicken
blurb: Chicken thighs marinated in lemongrass, garlic and fish sauce, charred and served with rice and pickles.
ingredients: Steamed rice, sliced cucumber and quick carrot pickle, to serve
Nuoc cham (fish sauce, lime, sugar, garlic, chilli, water), to drizzle
method: Blitz or pound the lemongrass, garlic, shallots, fish sauce, sugar, oil, soy and chilli to a loose paste.
Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 20 minutes (or overnight).
Grill, griddle or barbecue over a medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes each side until caramelised at the edges and cooked through.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Serve over rice with cucumber, carrot pickle and a good spoon of nuoc cham.

name: Chicken Cacciatore
blurb: Hunter's-style chicken braised with tomatoes, peppers, olives, rosemary and a splash of red wine.
ingredients: 80g black olives, sprig of rosemary, 1 bay leaf
Polenta, potatoes or crusty bread, to serve
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down in a wide pan until deep gold, turn briefly, then lift out.
Fry the onion and peppers in the fat for 8 minutes, add the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, stock, olives, rosemary and bay.
Return the chicken skin-side up and simmer uncovered for 30-35 minutes until the sauce is thick and the chicken tender.
Discard the rosemary and bay and serve with polenta or potatoes.

name: Chicken Milanese
blurb: Thin breaded chicken fried crisp and golden, served with a lemon-dressed rocket and tomato salad.
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts, butterflied and beaten to 5mm
150g fine dried breadcrumbs mixed with 30g grated Parmesan
Olive oil and 30g butter, for frying
Lemon, extra virgin olive oil, to dress
method: Season the chicken, then coat each piece in flour, then egg, then the Parmesan breadcrumbs, pressing them on firmly.
Heat a 3mm depth of olive oil with the butter in a large pan over medium-high.
Fry the escalopes for 3 minutes each side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack and salt lightly.
Toss the rocket, tomatoes and onion with lemon juice, olive oil and seasoning.
Serve each escalope topped with a handful of the salad and lemon wedges.

name: Pasta e Fagioli
blurb: A thick, humble Italian soup-stew of borlotti beans, small pasta, tomato and rosemary.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins borlotti or cannellini beans
1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, finely diced
1 sprig rosemary, 1 bay leaf, pinch chilli flakes
Parmesan rind (optional), plus grated Parmesan to serve
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in 3 tbsp olive oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato purée, rosemary, bay and chilli for 2 minutes.
Add one tin of beans with their liquid and roughly mash, then add the second tin drained, the stock and the Parmesan rind.
Simmer for 15 minutes, then add the pasta and cook until al dente, adding water if it gets too thick — it should be spoonable, not soupy.
Discard the rosemary, bay and rind. Season well.
Serve with a hard grating of Parmesan and a generous swirl of olive oil.

name: Ham & Ricotta Calzone
blurb: A folded, stuffed pizza — molten ricotta, mozzarella and ham inside a puffed, blistered crust.
ingredients: 1 batch pizza dough (300g strong flour, 1/2 tsp yeast, 1 tsp salt, 200ml warm water, 1 tbsp oil), proved and divided into 4
Handful of basil, grating of nutmeg
Simple tomato sauce (400g passata simmered with garlic and oregano), to serve
method: Heat the oven with a heavy tray inside to its maximum for 30 minutes.
Mix the ricotta, half the mozzarella, the Parmesan, nutmeg and seasoning.
Stretch each dough ball to a 22cm round. Spread the ricotta mix over one half, top with ham, the rest of the mozzarella and torn basil, leaving a border.
Fold over into a half-moon, press and crimp the edge firmly, and cut two small steam vents. Glaze with egg.
Bake on the hot tray for 10-12 minutes until deep golden and puffed. Serve with the warm tomato sauce for dipping.

name: Pasta alla Gricia
blurb: The ancestor of amatriciana without the tomato: crisp guanciale, pecorino and a storm of black pepper.
ingredients: 150g guanciale (or pancetta), cut into short lardons
method: Put the pasta on to cook in well-salted water.
Fry the guanciale in a cold dry pan, bringing it up to medium heat, until the fat has rendered and the pieces are golden and crisp. Take off the heat and keep the fat.
Toast the black pepper in the guanciale fat for a few seconds, then add a ladle of pasta water and swirl.
Drain the pasta a minute early and add it to the pan with the guanciale. Toss over low heat, adding pasta water bit by bit.
Off the heat, add the pecorino a handful at a time, tossing hard, until you have a creamy, clinging sauce. Serve at once with more pepper.

name: Chilaquiles Rojos with Fried Eggs
blurb: Tortilla chips simmered briefly in a smoky red salsa so they soften at the edges but keep some bite, topped with egg, crema and onion.
ingredients: 200g lightly salted tortilla chips (or fry 6 corn tortillas cut into triangles)
4 tomatoes and 2 dried chipotle or ancho chillies (soaked), or 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo
Crema or soured cream, sliced red onion, coriander
method: Blitz the tomatoes, chillies, onion and garlic to a smooth salsa.
Fry the salsa in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until darkened, then add the stock and simmer to a loose, pourable sauce. Season.
Fry the eggs to your liking in a separate pan.
Add the tortilla chips to the simmering sauce and fold gently for 1-2 minutes — you want them coated and softening but not turned to mush.
Tip onto plates, top with the eggs, then crema, cheese, red onion and coriander, with lime to squeeze.

name: Camarones a la Diabla
blurb: Prawns in a fiery, brick-red sauce of guajillo and chipotle chillies, garlic and tomato.
ingredients: 4 guajillo chillies and 2 chipotles (or 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo), stemmed and soaked
Lime, coriander and steamed rice, to serve
method: Blitz the soaked chillies, tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano, cumin and tomato purée with the stock to a smooth sauce.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the sauce for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens.
Season the prawns and add them to the sauce.
Cook for 3-4 minutes, turning, just until the prawns are pink and firm.
Finish with lime juice and coriander and serve with rice to soak up the sauce.

name: Rajas con Crema Tacos
blurb: Charred poblano strips softened with onion and sweetcorn in a light cream sauce, folded into warm tortillas.
method: Blister the poblanos directly over a flame or under a hot grill until blackened all over. Steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then rub off the skins, deseed and slice into strips (rajas).
Fry the onions in a little oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the pepper strips, sweetcorn and oregano and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the crema and milk and simmer 3-4 minutes to a loose sauce. Season and add most of the cheese.
Spoon into warm tortillas, top with the rest of the cheese and serve with lime.

name: Enchiladas Suizas
blurb: Chicken-filled tortillas under a tangy green tomatillo sauce and a blanket of melted cheese.
ingredients: 600g tomatillos (or 2 tins), or 500g green tomatoes + 2 tbsp lime
2 green chillies, 1/2 onion, 2 garlic cloves, small bunch coriander
200g grated cheese (Monterey Jack or mild cheddar)
Sliced onion and coriander, to serve
method: Simmer the tomatillos, chillies, onion and garlic in a little water for 8 minutes until soft, then blitz with the coriander, stock and cream to a smooth pourable sauce. Season.
Warm each tortilla briefly in a little oil so it is pliable.
Fill each with shredded chicken, roll up and pack seam-down into a baking dish.
Pour over all the sauce so the tortillas are covered, then scatter with the cheese.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden. Top with raw onion and coriander to serve.

name: Brazilian Feijoada
blurb: A deep, smoky black bean stew with several cuts of pork and beef, served with rice, greens and orange.
ingredients: For the couve: 1 bunch spring greens or kale, finely shredded, fried with garlic
Steamed rice, orange segments and hot sauce, to serve
method: Brown all the meats in a large pot in batches, then set aside. Soften the onions and garlic in the fat for 10 minutes with the cumin.
Return the meats, add the drained beans and bay, and cover with water by 5cm.
Simmer gently, part-covered, for about 2 hours until the beans are creamy and the meat is tender, topping up with water as needed.
Lift out the meats, slice, and stir the sliced sausage and larger pieces back in. Mash a ladle of beans against the side to thicken the pot.
Fry the shredded greens hard with garlic. Serve the feijoada with rice, the greens, a few orange segments and hot sauce.

name: Lomo Saltado
blurb: Peruvian stir-fry of beef, onion and tomato in soy and vinegar, piled with chips and served with rice.
ingredients: 600g sirloin or rump steak, cut into thick strips
1 aji amarillo or 1 yellow chilli, sliced
method: Season the beef well and sear it in two batches in a screaming-hot wok or heavy pan for 1-2 minutes so it browns but stays pink inside. Set aside.
Add the onions and chilli to the pan and stir-fry for 2 minutes so they keep some crunch, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and toss for 1 minute.
Return the beef, add the soy and vinegar and toss for 30 seconds, scraping up the pan.
Fold through the hot chips and the coriander and serve straight away, with rice on the side.

name: Moqueca
blurb: A vivid Brazilian fish stew in coconut milk, tomatoes and peppers, finished with lime and dendê oil.
ingredients: 700g firm white fish (cod, hake or monkfish), in large chunks
Juice of 2 limes, 3 garlic cloves crushed (to marinate)
2 tbsp palm (dendê) oil or olive oil
method: Toss the fish with the lime juice, garlic and a little salt and leave for 15 minutes.
In a wide pan or clay pot, layer half the onions, peppers and tomatoes. Sit the fish (and prawns) on top, then the rest of the vegetables. Add the paprika and chilli.
Pour over the coconut milk and dendê oil, bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 15-18 minutes without stirring much, so the fish stays whole.
Scatter over most of the coriander and simmer 2 minutes more.
Check for lime and salt and serve straight from the pot with rice.

name: Pav Bhaji
blurb: Mumbai street food: a spiced, buttery mash of mixed vegetables scooped up with griddled buttered rolls.
ingredients: 3 potatoes, 1 small cauliflower, 150g peas, 1 carrot — all boiled soft
1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp chilli powder
80g butter, plus extra for the pav
1 red onion diced, coriander and lemon wedges, to serve
method: Melt half the butter and fry the onions until soft, add the ginger-garlic paste and pepper for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook down to a paste, then stir in the pav bhaji masala and chilli powder for 1 minute.
Add all the boiled vegetables with a splash of their water and mash directly in the pan to a coarse, spreadable bhaji. Simmer 10 minutes, stirring, adding water to loosen.
Beat in the rest of the butter until glossy. Season with salt and lemon.
Split the rolls, griddle them cut-side down in butter until golden, and serve alongside the bhaji topped with raw onion, coriander and lemon.

name: Anda Bhurji
blurb: Indian-style spiced scrambled eggs with onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander, for toast or roti.
ingredients: 6 eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp garam masala
Buttered toast, roti or pav, to serve
method: Heat the oil and crackle the cumin seeds. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the ginger and chillies for 1 minute, then the tomato and turmeric and cook 2 minutes to a paste.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir over medium-low heat, folding, until just set and still soft.
Stir through the garam masala and most of the coriander.
Serve piled onto buttered toast or with warm roti, scattered with the rest of the coriander.

name: Chicken Pathia
blurb: A British curry-house favourite: hot, sweet and sour all at once, with tamarind and a touch of sugar.
ingredients: 3 tbsp medium curry paste (or 2 tbsp curry powder)
1 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp fenugreek
method: Fry the onions in 3 tbsp oil over medium heat for 12 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then the curry paste, chilli powder, paprika and fenugreek and cook out for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer 5 minutes, then blitz smooth for a classic curry-house texture if you like.
Add the chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the tamarind and sugar, balance to taste so it is hot then sweet then sharp, and serve with coriander and rice.

name: Kadhi Pakora
blurb: Silky, tangy gram-flour and yoghurt curry with soft onion fritters bobbing in it, over rice.
ingredients: For the pakora: 120g gram (chickpea) flour, 2 onions thinly sliced, 1 green chilli, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli, pinch bicarb, water to bind
For the kadhi: 60g gram flour, 400g natural yoghurt, 1.2 litres water
Tempering: 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 10 curry leaves, 2 dried chillies, pinch asafoetida
method: Mix the pakora ingredients to a thick, dropping batter. Fry heaped teaspoons in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until golden. Drain.
Whisk the gram flour into the yoghurt until smooth, then whisk in the water, turmeric, chilli powder and ginger-garlic paste.
Pour into a pot and bring to a simmer, whisking, then cook on low for 20-25 minutes, stirring often, until thickened and no longer raw-tasting.
Slip in the pakoras and simmer 5 minutes so they soak up the kadhi.
Heat the ghee and fry the tempering spices until they pop and the curry leaves crackle, then pour it sizzling over the kadhi. Serve with rice.

name: Maqluba
blurb: A Levantine 'upside-down' pot of spiced rice, chicken and fried aubergine, flipped out at the table.
ingredients: 2 onions, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom pods, 2 bay leaves
2 tbsp baharat or maqluba spice mix
500g basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 20 minutes
Toasted pine nuts and almonds, chopped parsley, to finish
Cucumber and yoghurt salad, to serve
method: Simmer the chicken with 1 onion, the whole spices and 1 tbsp baharat in water to cover for 30 minutes. Lift out the chicken; strain and keep 900ml of the stock.
Fry the aubergine and cauliflower in batches until golden; drain.

Rub a wide, heavy pot with oil. Arrange the chicken over the base, then layers of aubergine and cauliflower, then the drained rice mixed with the rest of the baharat and a sliced onion. Press down gently.
Pour the hot stock down the side to just cover the rice. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes. Rest, covered, for 15 minutes.
Put a large platter over the pot and, with confidence, invert it. Lift the pot away, scatter with nuts and parsley, and serve with the yoghurt salad.

name: Misir Wot
blurb: Ethiopian red lentils stewed low with berbere and caramelised onion into a rich, spicy purée.
ingredients: 3 tbsp oil (or niter kibbeh for the classic flavour)
4 garlic cloves and 1 thumb ginger, grated
method: Cook the onions in a dry pan over low heat, stirring often, for 12-15 minutes until deeply softened and starting to colour.
Add the oil, garlic and ginger and cook 3 minutes, then stir in the berbere and tomato purée and fry gently for 2-3 minutes until dark and fragrant.
Add the lentils and water, bring to a simmer and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a thick, spoonable stew.
Season with salt and loosen with a little water if needed.
Serve with injera or flatbread to scoop, ideally with a cooling side of chopped tomato and onion salad.

name: Suya Skewers
blurb: West African street skewers of thin beef rubbed in a spiced peanut 'yaji' and grilled over high heat.
ingredients: 600g sirloin or rump steak, sliced thin

For the yaji: 60g roasted peanuts blitzed to a coarse powder, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp ground ginger, 1 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp garlic granules, 1 tsp onion granules, 1 stock cube crushed, 1/2 tsp salt
Flatbreads and lime wedges, to serve
method: Mix all the yaji ingredients. Reserve a third for dusting at the end.
Toss the beef with the oil and two-thirds of the yaji and leave 15 minutes.
Thread the beef onto skewers in loose folds.
Grill, griddle or barbecue over a high heat for 2 minutes each side until charred at the edges but still juicy.
Dust with the reserved yaji straight off the heat and serve with sliced onion, tomato, flatbreads and lime.

name: Coronation Chicken
blurb: Poached chicken in a lightly curried, apricot-sweet mayonnaise with almonds — for a plate or a jacket.
ingredients: 600g cooked chicken, shredded (or poach 4 breasts and cool)
2 tbsp apricot jam or mango chutney
Rice salad or baked potatoes and dressed leaves, to serve
method: Warm the curry powder in a dry pan for 30 seconds until fragrant, then let it cool.
Whisk the mayonnaise, yoghurt, curry powder, apricot jam, tomato purée and lemon into a smooth, glossy dressing. Loosen with a little water if thick.
Fold in the chicken, sultanas and most of the almonds and season.
Chill for 20 minutes for the flavours to settle.
Serve over a rice salad or with baked potatoes and leaves, scattered with the rest of the almonds.

name: Roast Cauliflower Steaks with Chimichurri
blurb: Thick cauliflower slabs roasted golden and drenched in a punchy herb, garlic and chilli chimichurri.
method: Brush the cauliflower steaks with oil, season, and roast at 220C for 25 minutes, turning once.
Blitz or finely chop the herbs, garlic, chilli, vinegar and remaining oil.
Spoon the chimichurri generously over the roasted steaks.

name: Mushroom Stroganoff
blurb: Mixed mushrooms in a paprika-spiked soured cream sauce with brandy, over rice or pasta.
method: Fry the mushrooms hard in the butter until deep golden, add the onions and paprika.
Add the brandy and cook off, then the soured cream and Dijon.
Warm gently, season, finish with parsley; serve over rice.

name: Puy Lentil & Mushroom Cottage Pie
blurb: A savoury lentil and mushroom base under a cheesy potato-and-celeriac mash, baked until crisp.
method: Soften the veg, add the mushrooms, purée, soy, lentils and stock and simmer 30 minutes.
Boil and mash the potato and celeriac.
Top the lentils with mash and cheese and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

name: Aubergine Katsu with Sticky Rice
blurb: Panko aubergine slices, fried crisp, over rice with a mild vegan curry sauce and quick slaw.
ingredients: rice and shredded cabbage to serve
method: Salt the aubergine, pat dry, then coat in flour, plant-milk batter and panko.
Shallow-fry until deep golden and tender inside.
Make the sauce from onion, carrot, curry powder, flour and stock, blend, and serve over the sliced aubergine and rice.

name: Halloumi Fajitas
blurb: Charred halloumi, peppers and onions with smoky spice, folded into warm tortillas with lime and salsa.
ingredients: salsa and soured cream to serve
method: Fry the peppers and onion hard with the fajita seasoning until charred.
Add the halloumi for the last few minutes to colour.
Serve in warm tortillas with lime, salsa and soured cream.

name: Roast Butternut Risotto
blurb: Sweet roasted squash stirred through a sage-and-Parmesan risotto with a crisp squash-crisp topping.
method: Roast most of the diced squash; blend half to a purée, keep half whole.
Make a risotto with the onion, rice, wine and stock over 18 minutes, stirring in the squash purée near the end.
Beat in the butter and Parmesan, top with the roast squash and crisp fried sage.

name: Black Bean Burgers
blurb: Spiced black bean and oat patties, griddled firm, in a bun with chipotle mayo and avocado.
ingredients: 2 tins black beans, drained and dried
method: Mash the beans, mix with the oats, onion and spices, season and shape into 4 patties; chill.
Griddle 4 minutes a side until firm and crusted.
Build the burgers with chipotle mayo, avocado and lettuce.

name: Seven-Vegetable Tagine
blurb: A fragrant, lightly sweet braise of squash, carrot, courgette, pepper, chickpeas and apricots on couscous.
ingredients: 1/2 butternut squash, 2 carrots, 1 courgette, 1 pepper, all chopped
method: Soften the onions, add the ras el hanout.
Add all the veg, chickpeas, apricots and tomatoes and simmer 30 minutes.
Serve over couscous with coriander.

name: Spanakopita
blurb: Spinach, feta, herbs and egg baked between crisp layers of buttery filo. A generous Greek pie.
method: Mix the spinach, crumbled feta, eggs, herbs and spring onion.
Layer half the filo in a tin, brushing each sheet with butter, add the filling, then layer the rest on top.
Score into squares and bake at 180C for 40 minutes until deep golden.

name: Squash & Sage Gnocchi Bake
blurb: Gnocchi tossed with roasted squash, sage butter and mozzarella, baked until crisp on top.
method: Roast the squash at 210C for 25 minutes.
Boil the gnocchi, drain, toss with the sage butter and squash, tip into a dish.
Top with mozzarella and Parmesan and bake at 200C for 15 minutes.

name: Crispy Tofu Katsu Curry
blurb: Firm tofu pressed, crumbed and fried, sliced over rice with a mild Japanese curry sauce.
ingredients: 400g extra-firm tofu, pressed and halved into slabs
method: Coat the tofu slabs in flour, plant-milk batter and panko, then shallow-fry until golden.
Make the sauce with onion, carrot, curry powder, flour and stock; blend smooth.
Slice the tofu over rice and pour the sauce alongside.

name: Bean & Sweet Potato Enchiladas
blurb: Tortillas rolled around spiced sweet potato and black beans, baked under enchilada sauce and cheese.
method: Mix the roasted sweet potato with the beans and cumin.
Simmer the passata with the chipotle for a sauce; roll the filling in the tortillas and lay in a dish.
Pour over the sauce, scatter with cheese and bake at 190C for 20 minutes.

name: Caponata with Rigatoni
blurb: Sicilian sweet-and-sour aubergine with celery, capers, olives and raisins, over rigatoni.
ingredients: 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar
method: Fry the aubergine in oil until golden, remove.
Soften the onion and celery, add the tomatoes, capers, olives and raisins.
Return the aubergine, add the vinegar and sugar and simmer 15 minutes; toss with the pasta.

name: Mujadara
blurb: Lentils and rice cooked together, topped with a heap of deeply caramelised onions and a yoghurt swirl.
method: Fry the onions slowly in the oil for 30 minutes until dark and sweet.
Simmer the lentils until nearly tender, add the rice, spices and enough water, cover and cook 15 minutes.
Fold in half the onions, top with the rest and serve with yoghurt.

name: Thai Green Vegetable Curry
blurb: Aubergine, green beans, peppers and bamboo in a fragrant green coconut curry with Thai basil.
ingredients: 1 aubergine, 150g green beans, 2 peppers, 1 tin bamboo shoots
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and the aubergine, simmer 8 minutes, then the other veg.
Season with soy, sugar and lime and finish with Thai basil; serve with rice.

name: Leek & Potato Gratin
blurb: Sliced potato and softened leeks layered in garlic cream and Gruyère, baked until bronzed.
method: Warm the cream, milk, garlic and nutmeg.
Layer potato and leek in a dish, pouring over the cream as you go, and top with Gruyère.
Bake at 180C for 1 hour until tender and golden.

name: Crispy Tofu Peanut Bowl
blurb: Baked tofu, brown rice, shredded veg and greens under a lime-peanut dressing.
ingredients: 3 tbsp peanut butter, 1 lime, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp sriracha
method: Toss the tofu in cornflour and bake at 220C for 25 minutes until crisp.
Whisk the peanut butter with lime, soy, sriracha and water to a pourable dressing.
Build bowls with rice, tofu and raw veg and drizzle with the dressing.

name: Halloumi, Chickpea & Harissa Traybake
blurb: Chickpeas, peppers, red onion and halloumi roasted in harissa, finished with lemon and mint.
method: Toss the chickpeas, peppers and onions with the harissa and oil and roast at 210C for 20 minutes.
Add the halloumi and roast 12 minutes more.
Finish with lemon, mint and a spoon of yoghurt.

name: Quick Vegetable Biryani
blurb: A one-pan cheat's biryani with layered spiced veg, rice, fried onions and saffron. Weeknight-friendly.
method: Cook the veg in the yoghurt and biryani masala until nearly tender.
Par-boil the rice, then layer over the veg with fried onions and herbs, drizzle saffron milk.
Cover tightly and steam 20 minutes on low.

name: Green Shakshuka
blurb: Eggs baked in a pan of wilted spinach, chard, leek and herbs with feta and a squeeze of lemon.
method: Soften the leek and garlic with the cumin, add the greens and wilt down.
Make wells and crack in the eggs, cover and cook until just set.
Crumble over the feta, herbs and lemon.

name: Spinach & Ricotta Lasagne
blurb: Layers of pasta, spinach-ricotta and tomato sauce under béchamel and Parmesan. A meat-free classic.
method: Mix the spinach with the ricotta and nutmeg; simmer the tomatoes with the garlic to a sauce.
Make a béchamel.
Layer tomato, pasta and spinach-ricotta three times, finish with béchamel and Parmesan, bake at 190C for 40 minutes.

name: Loaded Veggie Chilli Fries
blurb: Oven fries piled with a quick bean chilli, melted cheese, jalapeños, soured cream and spring onion.
ingredients: pickled jalapeños, soured cream, spring onion
method: Bake the fries until crisp.
Simmer the beans, tomatoes, chipotle and cumin for 15 minutes to a thick chilli.
Pile the chilli over the fries, add cheese and grill to melt, then top with jalapeños, soured cream and spring onion.

name: Roasted Vegetable Orzo
blurb: Orzo tossed with tray-roasted courgette, pepper and tomato, feta, lemon and basil. Warm or room temp.
method: Roast the chopped veg with oil at 210C for 25 minutes.
Cook the orzo, drain and toss with the veg, lemon and oil.
Fold in crumbled feta and torn basil.

name: Cauliflower Cheese Jacket Potatoes
blurb: Fluffy baked potatoes split and loaded with a bubbling cauliflower cheese. Full-on comfort.
method: Bake the potatoes at 200C for 1 hour 10 until crisp.
Boil the cauliflower until just tender; make a cheese sauce with the butter, cornflour, milk, cheddar and mustard.
Split the potatoes, top with cauliflower and sauce and grill to bubble.

name: Squash, Spinach & Feta Filo Pie
blurb: Roasted squash, spinach and feta piled into buttered filo and baked into a shattering pie.
method: Mix the squash, spinach, crumbled feta, eggs and dill.
Layer the buttered filo in a tin, add the filling, and fold and scrunch the filo over the top.
Bake at 190C for 35 minutes until deep golden.

name: Sticky Gochujang Cauliflower
blurb: Roasted cauliflower tossed in a sweet-hot gochujang glaze with sesame and spring onion, over rice.
method: Roast the cauliflower in the oil at 220C for 25 minutes until charred at the edges.
Toss in the mixed gochujang, soy, maple and vinegar and roast 5 minutes more.
Scatter with sesame and spring onion; serve over rice.

name: Artichoke & Butterbean Paella
blurb: Saffron rice with artichoke hearts, butterbeans, peppers and peas cooked in one wide pan.
method: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic, add the rice and saffron.
Add the stock and butterbeans and simmer without stirring for 18 minutes.
Scatter over the artichokes and peas, rest 5 minutes, serve with lemon.

name: Loaded Sweet Potatoes with Black Beans
blurb: Whole roasted sweet potatoes split and piled with spiced black beans, avocado and lime crema.
method: Roast the sweet potatoes at 200C for 45 minutes until soft.
Simmer the beans with the chipotle and cumin for 10 minutes.
Split the potatoes, load with beans, mashed avocado, lime and coriander.

name: Lentil & Aubergine Moussaka
blurb: Layers of aubergine and spiced lentils under a baked béchamel. A vegetarian take on the Greek classic.
method: Roast the aubergine slices; simmer the lentils with the tomatoes and spices to a thick sauce.
Make an egg-enriched béchamel.
Layer aubergine and lentils, top with béchamel and Parmesan and bake at 190C for 45 minutes.

name: Broccoli & Cheddar Soup
blurb: A thick, comforting soup of broccoli and mature cheddar with a hint of mustard, served with bread.
method: Soften the onion in the butter, add the potato and broccoli stalks and the stock.
Simmer 15 minutes, add the florets for the last 5, then blend.
Stir in the cheddar, Dijon and cream off the heat.

name: Loaded Tofu Scramble Bowl
blurb: Turmeric tofu scramble with peppers, mushrooms, spinach and avocado over toast or grains. Vegan and fast.
method: Fry the pepper and mushrooms, add the tofu, turmeric and paprika.
Cook 5 minutes until golden and dry, then wilt in the spinach.
Pile onto toast with sliced avocado and hot sauce.

name: Vegetable Chow Mein
blurb: Egg noodles stir-fried with cabbage, carrot, pepper, beansprouts and a soy-oyster sauce.
method: Stir-fry the harder veg first, then the pepper and cabbage.
Add the noodles, beansprouts and sauces and toss over high heat.
Finish with spring onion and sesame oil.

name: Roast Parsnip & Chickpea Curry
blurb: Sweet roasted parsnips folded into a tomato-coconut chickpea curry with spinach and lime.
method: Roast the parsnips at 220C for 25 minutes.
Fry the onions, add the curry paste, then the tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer.
Fold in the chickpeas, parsnips and spinach, finish with lime.

name: Potato, Pepper & Manchego Frittata
blurb: A Spanish-leaning frittata thick with sautéed potato, peppers and salty Manchego, cut in wedges.
method: Soften the potato, pepper and onion slowly in the oil until tender.
Beat the eggs with the cheese and parsley, pour over and cook on low until almost set.
Finish under a hot grill until puffed; serve warm in wedges.

name: Mushroom Bourguignon
blurb: Big mushrooms braised in red wine with shallots, carrots and thyme, over mash. Deep and meaty, no meat.
method: Fry the mushrooms hard until browned, remove; soften the shallots and carrots.
Stir in the flour and purée, add the wine and stock and return the mushrooms with the thyme.
Simmer 30 minutes until thick; serve over mash.

name: Aubergine Katsu Sando
blurb: Crisp panko aubergine, cabbage and tonkatsu sauce pressed between soft white bread.
method: Coat the aubergine in flour, plant-milk batter and panko and shallow-fry until golden and soft.
Spread the bread with mayo and sauce, add cabbage and aubergine.
Press and slice off the crusts.

name: Vegetable & Bean Goulash
blurb: A paprika-rich stew of peppers, mushrooms, potato and beans, with a soured cream swirl.
method: Fry the onions, add the paprika and caraway off the heat so it doesn't burn.
Add the purée, peppers, mushrooms, potato and stock and simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in the beans, season, and serve with a swirl of soured cream.

name: Warm Halloumi & Giant Couscous Salad
blurb: Griddled halloumi over lemony giant couscous with roast peppers, chickpeas, rocket and mint.
method: Cook the giant couscous in stock, drain.
Toss with the peppers, chickpeas, lemon, oil, rocket and mint.
Top with griddled halloumi.

name: Mushroom Tinga Tacos
blurb: Shredded mushrooms braised in a smoky chipotle-tomato sauce, piled into tacos with avocado and lime.
method: Fry the mushrooms hard until browned, add the onion.
Blend the tomatoes and chipotle, add with the oregano and simmer 12 minutes to a thick sauce.
Fill warm tortillas with the tinga, avocado, lime and coriander.

name: Root Vegetable Pot Pie
blurb: Carrot, swede, leek and peas in a thyme cream sauce under a puff-pastry lid.
method: Soften the leeks, add the diced root veg and cook 10 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then the stock and cream, add the peas and thyme.
Tip into a dish, top with pastry, glaze and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

name: Miso-Glazed Aubergine (Nasu Dengaku)
blurb: Halved aubergines scored, roasted soft and lacquered with a sweet miso glaze, over rice.
method: Brush the aubergines with oil and roast cut-side up at 200C for 25 minutes until soft.
Mix the miso, mirin, maple and vinegar, spread over and grill 5 minutes until caramelised.
Top with sesame and spring onion; serve on rice.

name: Chilli Sin Carne
blurb: A hearty vegan chilli of three beans, lentils, peppers and dark spice, thick enough for jacket potatoes.
method: Soften the onions and peppers, add the chipotle, cocoa and spices.
Add the tomatoes, lentils, beans and a splash of water and simmer 25 minutes.
Season well and serve over baked potatoes or rice.

name: Black Bean Tofu & Pepper Stir-Fry
blurb: Crispy tofu and peppers in a savoury fermented black bean sauce over noodles.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fermented black beans, rinsed and mashed
method: Toss the tofu in cornflour and fry until crisp.
Stir-fry the peppers and onion, add the garlic, ginger and black beans.
Add the soy, sugar and a splash of water, return the tofu, and toss with cooked noodles.

name: Cauliflower Cheese Pasta Bake
blurb: Roasted cauliflower and pasta in a mustard cheese sauce with a crunchy Parmesan-crumb top.
method: Roast the cauliflower at 210C for 20 minutes; cook the pasta.
Make a cheese sauce with the butter, flour, milk, cheddar and mustard.
Combine, top with crumbs and Parmesan and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

name: Lentil Pie with Sweet Potato Mash
blurb: A rich lentil, carrot and mushroom base under a sweet potato mash lid, baked until the peaks crisp.
method: Soften the veg, add the mushrooms, purée, soy, lentils and stock and simmer 30 minutes.
Boil and mash the sweet potato with oil and seasoning.
Top the lentils with the mash, rough up the surface and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

name: Herb Tabbouleh with Grilled Halloumi
blurb: A parsley-heavy bulgur tabbouleh with tomato, mint and lemon, topped with charred halloumi.
method: Soak the bulgur in a little boiling water for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze.
Toss with the herbs, tomato, spring onion, lemon and oil.
Griddle the halloumi and lay it over the tabbouleh.

name: Massaman Potato & Peanut Curry
blurb: A mild, sweet-spiced coconut curry of potato, sweet potato, onion and roasted peanuts. Vegan comfort.
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, potatoes, sweet potato and onion and simmer 30 minutes.
Stir in the peanuts, season with soy, sugar and tamarind; serve with rice.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
blurb: Marinated grilled chicken in a creamy spiced tomato sauce.
ingredients: 3 tbsp tikka or tandoori spice mix
4 garlic cloves and 3cm ginger, crushed to a paste
method: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt and 2 tbsp of the spice mix, and leave for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry the chicken in batches over high heat until charred at the edges. Set aside.
Fry the onion in oil until golden, add the garlic-ginger paste and remaining spice mix for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato puree and passata and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened and darkened.
Return the chicken, add the cream and garam masala, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Scatter with coriander and serve with rice.

name: Butter Chicken
blurb: Mild, rich makhani sauce with tomato, butter, cream and fenugreek.
ingredients: 150g yoghurt, 1 tbsp garam masala, 1 tsp turmeric for the marinade
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt and spices for 30 minutes, then sear in a hot pan until browned. Set aside.
Melt the butter, fry the onion until soft, then add the garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the blitzed tomatoes, chilli powder and sugar, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until rich.
Blend the sauce smooth if you like, then return to the pan with the chicken.
Stir in the cream and crushed fenugreek and simmer gently for 8 minutes. Serve with rice or naan.

name: Lamb Rogan Josh
blurb: Kashmiri-style lamb braise with warm spices and a deep red sauce.
ingredients: 2 tsp ground fennel, 1 tsp ground ginger
6 cardamom pods, 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cloves, 2 bay leaves
method: Fry the whole spices in oil for 30 seconds, then add the onions and cook until deep golden.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the ground spices for 1 minute.
Add the lamb and brown, then stir in the yoghurt a spoon at a time.
Add the tomatoes and 200ml water, cover and simmer very gently for 1.5-2 hours until the lamb is tender.
Finish with garam masala and rest for 10 minutes before serving with rice.

name: Chana Masala
blurb: Chickpeas simmered with onion, tomato, amchur and warming spice.
ingredients: 2 tsp ground cumin, 2 tsp ground coriander
1 tsp amchur (dried mango) or squeeze of lemon
method: Fry the onion in oil until deep golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the ground spices, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook down for 8 minutes until thick and split.
Add the chickpeas and a splash of water, and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing some for body.
Stir in the amchur and garam masala, scatter with coriander and serve with rice.

name: Saag Paneer
blurb: Soft paneer in a silky spiced spinach sauce.
method: Fry the paneer in butter until golden on all sides, then set aside.
Fry the cumin seeds, then the onion until soft, then garlic, ginger and chilli.
Add the spinach and a splash of water and cook until wilted, then blitz to a coarse puree.
Return to the pan with the ground spices, cream and paneer, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season and serve with rice or roti.

name: Tarka Dal
blurb: Comforting yellow lentils finished with a sizzling spiced ghee tempering.
ingredients: 250g toor or yellow split lentils, rinsed
For the tarka: 3 tbsp ghee or oil, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 4 garlic cloves sliced, 1 dried red chilli, pinch of asafoetida
method: Simmer the lentils with the turmeric and 1 litre water for 25-30 minutes, skimming, until soft. Whisk to a loose porridge and season.
Heat the ghee and add the cumin seeds, then the garlic, cooking until pale gold.
Add the dried chilli, asafoetida, tomato and chilli powder and fry for 2 minutes.
Pour the sizzling tarka over the dal, stir through and finish with coriander and lemon.

name: Keralan Fish Curry
blurb: White fish poached in a tangy coconut sauce with curry leaves and tamarind.
ingredients: 600g firm white fish, cut into large pieces
1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig of curry leaves
1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp turmeric
method: Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add the curry leaves, then the onion and cook until soft.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the chilli powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook to a paste, then pour in the coconut milk and tamarind and simmer for 5 minutes.
Slip in the fish and poach gently for 6-8 minutes until just cooked. Season and serve with rice.

name: Aloo Gobi
blurb: Dry-fried potato and cauliflower with turmeric, cumin and ginger.
method: Parboil the potatoes for 5 minutes and drain.
Fry the cumin seeds in oil, add the ginger and green chilli, then the ground spices.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower, toss to coat, add a splash of water and cover.
Cook for 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender with some crisp edges.
Finish with coriander and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Prawn Balti
blurb: Fast, punchy tomato and pepper curry cooked hard in a wide pan.
ingredients: 3 tomatoes, chopped, plus 2 tbsp tomato puree
method: Fry the cumin seeds in oil over high heat, then add the onion and pepper and char slightly.
Add the garlic, ginger and balti paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and puree and cook hard for 5-6 minutes to a thick sauce.
Stir in the prawns and cook for 3-4 minutes until pink and just done.
Scatter with coriander and serve with rice or naan.

name: Chicken Biryani
blurb: Layered spiced chicken and basmati baked with fried onions and saffron.
ingredients: 800g chicken thighs, on the bone or boneless
3 onions, thinly sliced and fried until crisp
Large pinch of saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk
Handful each of mint and coriander
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt, garlic, ginger, spice mix and half the fried onions for 30 minutes.
Parboil the rinsed rice in salted water with a few whole spices until 70 percent done, then drain.
Cook the marinated chicken in a heavy pot for 10 minutes until part-cooked and saucy.
Layer the rice on top, scatter with the rest of the onions, herbs, saffron milk and dots of ghee.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat (or 160C oven) for 25 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then fork through gently.

name: Bengali-style Egg Curry
blurb: Fried boiled eggs simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy.
ingredients: 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tsp chilli powder
method: Rub the boiled eggs with a little turmeric and salt and fry until blistered. Set aside.
Fry the onions until deep golden, then add garlic and ginger.
Add the ground spices, then the tomatoes, and cook to a thick masala.
Add 250ml water, simmer for 8 minutes, then return the eggs and warm through.
Finish with garam masala and coriander; serve with rice.

name: Tandoori Chicken Traybake
blurb: Yoghurt and spice marinated chicken roasted with onions and peppers.
method: Mix the yoghurt, spice mix, garlic, ginger and lemon and coat the chicken. Marinate 30 minutes or overnight.
Heat oven to 220C fan. Spread the onions and peppers in a roasting tray and sit the chicken on top.
Roast for 30-35 minutes until the chicken is charred at the edges and cooked through.
Serve with rice, flatbreads or a chopped salad and extra lemon.

name: Vegetable Korma
blurb: Gentle, nutty cashew and coconut curry with mixed vegetables.
ingredients: 700g mixed veg (cauliflower, carrot, potato, peas, beans)
60g cashews, soaked and blitzed with a little water
2 tsp mild curry powder, 1 tsp garam masala
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the garlic and ginger, then the spices for 1 minute.
Add the firmer vegetables and 200ml water, cover and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the quicker vegetables, the cashew paste and coconut milk, and simmer for 8-10 minutes until tender.
Balance with the sugar and a little salt, and serve with rice.

name: Keema Matar
blurb: Spiced lamb mince with peas, quick enough for a weeknight.
ingredients: 2 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp chilli powder
method: Fry the cumin seeds in oil, add the onion and cook until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger, then the mince, browning it well.
Stir in the ground spices and tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes to a thick masala.
Add 150ml water and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the peas for the last 5.
Finish with garam masala and coriander; serve with rice or roti.

name: Paneer Tikka Skewers
blurb: Charred paneer and peppers in a smoky yoghurt marinade.
ingredients: 1 red and 1 green pepper, in chunks
1 tbsp oil, juice of half a lemon
method: Toast the gram flour in a dry pan for 1 minute, then mix with the yoghurt, spices, garlic, ginger, oil and lemon.
Fold through the paneer and vegetables and marinate for 20 minutes.
Thread onto skewers and grill or griddle for 8-10 minutes, turning, until charred.
Serve with mint yoghurt and flatbreads.

name: Chicken Jalfrezi
blurb: Stir-fried chicken with peppers, onions and green chilli in a dry-ish sauce.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp turmeric
method: Sear the chicken in hot oil until browned, then remove.
Fry the onions and peppers hard so they char at the edges, then add the chillies, garlic and ginger.
Add the ground spices, tomatoes and puree, and cook for 5 minutes to a thick sauce.
Return the chicken and cook for 5 minutes until done, finishing with garam masala. Serve with rice.

name: Masala Dosa (shortcut)
blurb: Crisp crepes from a shop-bought batter with a spiced potato filling.
ingredients: 1 tsp mustard seeds, sprig of curry leaves
method: Pop the mustard seeds in oil, add curry leaves, onion, ginger and chilli, and cook until soft.
Stir in the turmeric and the crushed potato with a splash of water; season and keep warm.
Heat a wide non-stick pan, ladle in batter and spread thin in a spiral. Drizzle with oil.
Cook until crisp and golden underneath, add a line of potato, fold and serve with chutney.

name: Red Lentil & Spinach Curry
blurb: Fast, cheap and nourishing: red lentils cooked down with tomato and spinach.
ingredients: 2 tsp curry powder, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp turmeric
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and 700ml water, and simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils collapse.
Stir through the spinach until wilted, season and add lemon.
Serve with rice or flatbread.

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
blurb: Slow-simmered beef and pork ragu with a glossy tomato sauce over spaghetti.
ingredients: Parmesan and olive oil, to serve
method: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pan and gently fry the onion, carrot and celery for 8-10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then turn up the heat and add both minces, breaking them up and browning well.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the chopped tomatoes, oregano and a splash of water. Season, cover and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente, then drain, saving a mugful of water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Serve with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of oil.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
blurb: Silky egg and pecorino sauce with crisp guanciale and lots of black pepper.
method: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente.
Meanwhile, fry the guanciale in a dry pan over medium heat until the fat renders and it turns crisp and golden.
Beat the eggs and yolk with the pecorino, Parmesan and black pepper in a bowl.
Drain the pasta, reserving a mug of the water. Take the pan of guanciale off the heat and add the pasta, tossing in the fat.
Pour in the egg mixture and toss quickly, adding splashes of pasta water until you have a glossy sauce that coats every strand.
Serve at once with extra pecorino and pepper.

name: Classic Beef Lasagne
blurb: Layers of rich ragu, creamy bechamel and pasta baked until bubbling.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, all finely chopped
method: Fry the onion, carrot and celery in oil for 10 minutes, add garlic, then brown the mince.
Stir in puree, wine, tomatoes and seasoning. Simmer gently for 45 minutes until thick.
For the bechamel, melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk a little at a time until smooth and thickened. Add nutmeg and half the Parmesan.
Heat oven to 190C fan. Layer ragu, pasta sheets and bechamel in a dish, repeating and finishing with bechamel.
Scatter over the remaining Parmesan and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Cacio e Pepe
blurb: Three ingredients, all technique: pecorino, pepper and starchy pasta water.
method: Toast the crushed pepper in a wide pan for 30 seconds, then add a ladle of water and let it simmer.
Cook the pasta in minimal well-salted water so it becomes very starchy, until just shy of al dente.
Transfer the pasta to the pepper pan with a little of its water and finish cooking, tossing.
Off the heat, add a splash more water and the pecorino in stages, tossing hard to form a creamy sauce.
Loosen with water as needed and serve immediately.

name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro
blurb: The purest tomato pasta: good oil, garlic, basil and a long gentle simmer.
method: Warm the oil with the garlic over low heat until fragrant but not coloured.
Crush in the tomatoes by hand, add a pinch of salt and the sugar, and simmer gently for 20 minutes until jammy.
Tear in most of the basil.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, then drain and toss through the sauce with a little pasta water.
Finish with the rest of the basil and a good drizzle of oil.

name: Penne all'Arrabbiata
blurb: Angry little tomato sauce with plenty of chilli and garlic.
method: Gently fry the garlic and chilli flakes in the oil until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt, and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Cook the penne until al dente and drain, keeping some pasta water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a splash of water, then stir in the parsley and serve.

name: Trofie with Basil Pesto
blurb: Fresh basil pesto with potato and green beans, the Ligurian way.
method: Blitz the basil, pine nuts, both cheeses, garlic and oil to a coarse pesto. Season.
Boil the pasta, adding the potato at the same time and the beans for the last 4 minutes.
Drain, saving a little water, and toss everything with the pesto, loosening with pasta water.
Serve straight away, without reheating the pesto.

name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
blurb: Guanciale, tomato and pecorino with a gentle chilli hum.
method: Fry the guanciale gently until crisp, then lift out half and set aside.
Add the chilli and wine to the pan, let it reduce, then add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the bucatini until al dente and drain.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with the pecorino and a little pasta water, then top with the reserved guanciale.

name: Mushroom Risotto
blurb: Creamy slow-stirred rice with mixed mushrooms, thyme and Parmesan.
method: Fry the mushrooms in a little butter over high heat until golden, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan, add garlic and thyme, then stir in the rice for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it absorb, then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is creamy and al dente (about 18 minutes).
Stir the mushrooms back in with the butter and Parmesan, cover and rest for 2 minutes.
Loosen with a little stock and serve.

name: Risotto alla Milanese
blurb: Golden saffron risotto, rich with butter and Parmesan.
ingredients: 1.2 litres hot chicken or vegetable stock
1 tbsp bone marrow or extra butter (optional)
method: Steep the saffron in a little warm stock.
Soften the onion in half the butter, then toast the rice for 2 minutes.
Add the wine, let it absorb, then add stock a ladle at a time, stirring constantly.
Halfway through, stir in the saffron stock. Continue until the rice is al dente and creamy.
Beat in the rest of the butter and the Parmesan off the heat, rest 2 minutes and serve.

name: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
blurb: Potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with molten mozzarella.
method: Fry the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt, and simmer 15 minutes until thick. Tear in most of the basil.
Boil the gnocchi until they float, then drain.
Fold the gnocchi through the sauce in an ovenproof pan, dot with mozzarella and scatter with Parmesan.
Grill or bake at 220C for 8-10 minutes until bubbling and blistered. Finish with basil.

name: Chicken Parmigiana
blurb: Crumbed chicken breast under tomato sauce and melted mozzarella.
method: Simmer the passata with the garlic and a pinch of salt for 15 minutes.
Coat each chicken piece in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumbs mixed with half the Parmesan.
Shallow fry for 3 minutes each side until golden, then transfer to a baking dish.
Spoon over the tomato sauce, top with mozzarella and the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake at 200C fan for 12-15 minutes until melted and bubbling. Finish with basil.

name: Melanzane alla Parmigiana
blurb: Baked layers of fried aubergine, tomato sauce and Parmesan.
method: Salt the aubergine slices for 20 minutes, then pat dry and fry in oil until golden on both sides. Drain on kitchen paper.
Make a quick sauce: fry the garlic, add tomatoes and basil, simmer 20 minutes and season.
Layer sauce, aubergine, mozzarella and Parmesan in a dish, repeating and finishing with Parmesan.
Bake at 180C fan for 35 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

name: Spaghetti Puttanesca
blurb: Punchy sauce of olives, capers, anchovy, garlic and chilli.
method: Melt the anchovies with the garlic and chilli in olive oil over low heat.
Add the capers, olives and tomatoes, and simmer for 12-15 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente and drain.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with parsley and a little pasta water.

name: Osso Buco with Gremolata
blurb: Braised veal shin in white wine and stock, with a bright lemon gremolata.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, finely diced
For gremolata: zest of 1 lemon, 1 garlic clove, handful parsley, all finely chopped
method: Tie each piece of shin around the middle, dust with flour and brown in oil in a casserole. Set aside.
Soften the vegetables in the same pan for 10 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then the stock, tomatoes and bay. Return the meat.
Cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours until the meat is falling from the bone.
Mix the gremolata ingredients and scatter over just before serving, with the sauce.

name: Minestrone
blurb: Chunky vegetable and bean soup with a handful of small pasta.
ingredients: Handful of kale or cabbage, shredded
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in olive oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and courgette.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and greens and cook for another 10 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Season well and serve with grated Parmesan or a spoon of pesto.

name: Pork Ragu Bianco with Pappardelle
blurb: A white ragu of slow-cooked pork with wine, milk and sage, no tomato.
ingredients: 800g pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
Few sage leaves and 1 rosemary sprig
method: Brown the pork all over in a casserole, then remove.
Soften the onion and garlic, return the pork, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the stock and herbs, cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Shred the meat in the pan, add the milk and simmer 15 minutes to a creamy sauce.
Toss with cooked pappardelle and plenty of Parmesan.

name: Tomato & Mozzarella Orzo
blurb: One-pan orzo cooked risotto-style with roasted tomatoes and torn mozzarella.
method: Fry the cherry tomatoes in the oil over high heat until blistered and starting to collapse.
Add the garlic and puree for 1 minute, then stir in the orzo.
Add the stock a third at a time, stirring, until the orzo is creamy and tender, about 12 minutes.
Off the heat, fold through the mozzarella and basil and serve.

name: Veal Saltimbocca
blurb: Thin veal escalopes with prosciutto and sage in a quick wine and butter sauce.
method: Lay a slice of prosciutto and 2 sage leaves on each escalope and press or secure with a cocktail stick.
Dust the meat side lightly with flour.
Fry prosciutto-side up in butter for 2 minutes, flip and cook 1 minute more. Remove.
Add the wine to the pan, scrape up the bits, bubble to a light sauce and finish with lemon and a knob of butter.
Spoon over the veal and serve straight away.

name: Tuna, Lemon & Chilli Spaghetti
blurb: Storecupboard hero: good tinned tuna, lemon, garlic and chilli.
method: Cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Gently warm the oil, garlic and chilli in a pan, then add the tuna with its oil, breaking it up.
Add the lemon zest and a splash of pasta water.
Toss the drained pasta through with the lemon juice and parsley, then serve.

name: Sausage & Fennel Rigatoni
blurb: Italian sausage meat, fennel seeds and a splash of cream on rigatoni.
method: Fry the sausage meat hard, breaking it into craggy pieces until deeply browned.
Add the fennel seeds, chilli and garlic for 1 minute, then the wine and reduce by half.
Stir in the cream and a splash of pasta water to make a sauce.
Toss with the cooked rigatoni and Parmesan, loosening with pasta water as needed.

name: Panzanella with Burrata
blurb: Torn sourdough soaked in tomato juices with basil, capers and creamy burrata.
method: Toss the tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and leave for 10 minutes to release their juices.
Soak the onion in the vinegar for 10 minutes.
Toast or griddle the bread until lightly charred, then toss with the tomatoes, onion, capers and oil.
Leave for 10 minutes so the bread softens, tear through the basil, then serve with burrata torn over.

name: Chicken Souvlaki with Pita
blurb: Lemon-oregano chicken skewers with warm pita, tzatziki and salad.
ingredients: Juice of 1 lemon, 3 tbsp oil, 2 tbsp oregano, 4 garlic cloves
Tzatziki: 300g yoghurt, half a grated cucumber, 1 garlic clove, vinegar
Tomato, cucumber and red onion salad
method: Marinate the chicken for 30 minutes, then thread on skewers.
Griddle for 10-12 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked.
Warm the pitas; mix the tzatziki and salad.
Stuff the pitas with chicken, salad and tzatziki.

name: Briam (Greek Roasted Vegetables)
blurb: Layers of potato, courgette, aubergine and tomato slow-roasted in olive oil.
ingredients: Feta and crusty bread to serve
method: Toss all the vegetables with the passata, garlic, oil and oregano in a large baking dish.
Season generously and level out.
Roast at 190C fan for 75-90 minutes, stirring once, until everything is soft and caramelised.
Serve warm with feta and bread.

name: Greek Prawn & Tomato Orzo (Youvetsi)
blurb: Orzo baked in a garlicky tomato sauce with prawns and feta.
ingredients: 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp chilli flakes
400g tin chopped tomatoes, 700ml hot fish or veg stock
method: Soften the onion, add the garlic and chilli, then a splash of ouzo.
Add the tomatoes and orzo, then the stock a third at a time, stirring, for 12 minutes.
Stir in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes until pink.
Crumble over the feta and dill; grill 3 minutes if you like.

name: Lamb Kleftiko
blurb: Lamb shoulder slow-cooked in a parcel with lemon, garlic, oregano and potatoes.
method: Rub the lamb with oil, oregano, garlic and lemon juice; marinate overnight if you can.
Sit on the potatoes and onions in a deep tray, add the wine and lemon halves, and seal tightly with foil.
Roast at 150C fan for 3.5 hours until the lamb falls off the bone.
Uncover and blast at 220C for 15 minutes to colour.

name: Spanakopita
blurb: Crisp filo pie of spinach, feta, spring onion, dill and mint.
ingredients: Handful each dill and mint, 3 eggs
method: Mix the spinach, feta, spring onions, herbs and eggs; season lightly.
Layer half the filo in a buttered tin, brushing each sheet.
Spread in the filling, then top with the rest of the filo, buttering as you go.
Score into portions and bake at 180C fan for 40-45 minutes until deep golden.

name: Gigantes Plaki (Baked Butter Beans)
blurb: Giant butter beans baked in a herby tomato sauce until creamy.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins chopped tomatoes, 2 tbsp tomato purée
1 tsp each oregano and cinnamon, handful of parsley and dill
method: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 10 minutes, add the garlic and purée.
Add the tomatoes, spices and a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes.
Fold in the beans, tip into a dish, drizzle with more oil.
Bake at 190C fan for 30 minutes; finish with fresh herbs and serve with bread.

name: Grilled Sea Bream with Ladolemono
blurb: Whole bream grilled and dressed with a lemon-oregano olive oil.
ingredients: 2 whole sea bream, gutted and scored
Ladolemono: 6 tbsp olive oil, juice of 2 lemons, 1 tbsp oregano, 1 small garlic clove
Greens or a simple salad to serve
method: Season the fish inside and out and stuff with lemon and oregano.
Grill or barbecue for 6-7 minutes each side until the skin blisters and the flesh flakes.
Whisk the ladolemono until thick.
Pour over the hot fish and serve with greens.

name: Tomato Keftedes with Feta Dip
blurb: Santorini-style tomato and herb fritters, crisp outside and soft within.
