ingredients: Big handful each mint and parsley
Dip: 150g feta, 100g yoghurt, squeeze of lemon, blitzed
method: Mix the tomatoes, onion and herbs; squeeze out excess liquid.
Stir in the flour and baking powder to a thick batter; season.
Fry spoonfuls in shallow oil for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Serve hot with the whipped feta dip.

name: Chicken with Tomatoes, Olives & Feta
blurb: Chicken thighs braised with cherry tomatoes, olives, oregano and feta.
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down in an ovenproof pan; set aside.
Fry the garlic, add the wine and reduce, then the tomatoes and oregano.
Return the chicken, scatter with olives, and bake at 200C fan for 25 minutes.
Crumble over the feta and parsley.

name: Fasolada (Greek Bean Soup)
blurb: The everyday Greek white bean soup with celery, carrot and lots of olive oil.
ingredients: 3 x 400g tins cannellini or haricot beans
6 tbsp good olive oil, parsley, lemon
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 12 minutes.
Add the garlic and purée, then the beans, oregano and stock.
Simmer 20 minutes, mashing some beans for body.
Finish with a big glug of oil, parsley and lemon.

name: Grilled Halloumi & Watermelon Salad
blurb: Sweet chilled watermelon, salty griddled halloumi, mint and a lime dressing.
ingredients: Half a red onion, thinly sliced
Dressing: juice of 2 limes, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp honey, pinch of chilli flakes
method: Griddle the halloumi for 1-2 minutes each side until bar-marked.
Arrange the watermelon, onion and mint on a platter.
Lay the hot halloumi over.
Whisk the dressing and spoon over just before serving.

name: Beef Stifado
blurb: Beef slow-braised with baby onions, red wine, cinnamon and clove.
ingredients: 300ml red wine, 3 tbsp red wine vinegar
2 tbsp tomato purée, 400g tin chopped tomatoes
method: Brown the beef in a casserole, then set aside.
Fry the whole onions until golden, add the garlic, then the purée.
Add the wine, vinegar, tomatoes, whole spices and the beef.
Cover and cook at 150C fan for 2.5 hours until the beef and onions are meltingly soft; serve with bread or rice.

name: Vegetarian Moussaka
blurb: Layers of aubergine, spiced lentils and potato under a baked béchamel.
ingredients: 3 aubergines and 3 potatoes, sliced and roasted
Béchamel: 60g butter, 60g flour, 700ml milk, 2 yolks, 60g Parmesan, nutmeg
method: Roast the aubergine and potato slices until soft and golden.
Fry the onion and garlic, add the purée, lentils, tomatoes and spices; simmer 20 minutes.
Make the béchamel and beat in the yolks and Parmesan off the heat.
Layer potato, lentils, aubergine, then béchamel; bake at 180C fan for 40 minutes. Rest 15 minutes.

name: Prawn Saganaki
blurb: Prawns baked in a tomato and ouzo sauce with melting feta.
ingredients: 50ml ouzo or white wine, 1/2 tsp chilli flakes, 1 tsp oregano
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the garlic and chilli, then the ouzo.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the prawns, crumble over the feta, and bake at 220C fan for 8-10 minutes.
Scatter with parsley and mop up with bread.

name: Imam Bayildi (Stuffed Aubergines)
blurb: Aubergines stuffed with sweet onion, tomato and garlic and baked in olive oil.
method: Fry the aubergine halves cut-side down in oil until browned; scoop a hollow in each.
Cook the onions slowly in oil for 20 minutes until sweet, add the garlic, tomatoes, passata and sugar.
Fill the aubergines, sit them in a dish with a splash of water and more oil.
Bake at 180C fan for 40-45 minutes; serve warm with parsley.

name: Turkish Köfte with Yoghurt & Sumac Onions
blurb: Spiced lamb köfte over flatbread with garlicky yoghurt and a tomato-butter drizzle.
ingredients: 1 onion grated, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, paprika, chilli
50g butter, 1 tbsp tomato purée, 1 tsp Aleppo pepper
method: Mix the lamb with the onion, garlic, spices and parsley; shape into fat fingers.
Griddle for 8-10 minutes, turning, until charred.
Lay torn flatbread on plates, spoon over the garlic yoghurt, then the köfte.
Melt the butter with the purée and Aleppo pepper and drizzle over; top with sumac onions.

name: One-Pot Lemon Chicken Orzo
blurb: Chicken thighs and orzo cooked together with lemon, garlic and spinach.
ingredients: 900ml chicken stock, zest and juice of 1 lemon
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down; set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic, stir in the orzo for 1 minute.
Add the stock and lemon, nestle the chicken back in, and simmer 15 minutes.
Fold through the spinach, Parmesan and dill.

name: Baked Cod with Chorizo & Cannellini
blurb: Cod roasted on smoky chorizo and beans with cherry tomatoes and parsley.
ingredients: 1 red onion, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp smoked paprika
method: Toss the chorizo, beans, tomatoes and onion with the oil and paprika in a tray.
Roast at 200C fan for 15 minutes until the chorizo oil runs.
Sit the seasoned cod on top and roast 10-12 minutes.
Finish with parsley and lemon.

name: Proper Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
blurb: Big chunks of tomato and cucumber, olives, onion and a whole slab of feta.
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano
method: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper and onion with a big pinch of salt.
Dress with plenty of oil, a splash of vinegar and lots of oregano.
Top with the olives and the whole slab of feta.
Dust the feta with more oregano and oil; serve with bread.

name: Warm Puy Lentil, Feta & Roast Tomato Salad
blurb: Earthy lentils with sweet roast tomatoes, feta, herbs and a sharp dressing.
ingredients: Big handful each parsley and mint
Dressing: juice of 1 lemon, 4 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp Dijon, 1 small garlic clove
method: Simmer the lentils for 20-25 minutes until tender but with bite; drain.
Roast the tomatoes with oil at 200C for 20 minutes.
Toss the warm lentils with the dressing, onion and herbs.
Fold through the roast tomatoes and feta; serve warm.

name: Chicken Gyros Traybake
blurb: Marinated chicken and onions roasted for wraps with tzatziki and chips.
ingredients: 150g yoghurt, juice of 1 lemon, 3 tbsp oil, 2 tbsp oregano, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 4 garlic cloves
Pitas or wraps, tzatziki, tomato, red onion, chips
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt, lemon, oil, spices and garlic for 1 hour.
Spread on a tray with the onions and roast at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes until charred.
Rest, then slice.
Serve in warm pitas with tzatziki, salad and chips.

name: Baked Feta with Honey, Chilli & Sesame
blurb: A whole block of feta baked until soft, then drizzled with hot honey — with bread and salad.
ingredients: 1 tbsp sesame seeds, 2 tbsp olive oil
Warm flatbread and a tomato salad to serve
method: Sit the feta in a small dish, drizzle with oil, scatter with herbs.
Bake at 200C fan for 15-18 minutes until soft and slightly molten.
Warm the honey with the chilli and pour over; scatter with sesame.
Serve straight away with flatbread and salad to scoop.

name: Greek Chicken & Potato Traybake
blurb: Lemon, oregano and garlic chicken thighs roasted with potatoes and olives.
ingredients: Juice of 2 lemons, 6 tbsp olive oil
4 garlic cloves, crushed, 2 tbsp dried oregano
method: Toss the potatoes and chicken with the lemon, oil, garlic and oregano in a large tray. Season well.
Roast at 200C fan for 35 minutes.
Scatter over the olives and roast 10-15 minutes more until the chicken is crisp and the potatoes tender.
Crumble over the feta and serve with the pan juices.

name: Moussaka
blurb: Layered aubergine, spiced lamb and potato under a baked bechamel.
ingredients: 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 2 tbsp tomato puree
1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp oregano, pinch of allspice
Bechamel: 60g butter, 60g flour, 700ml milk, 2 egg yolks, 60g kefalotyri or parmesan, nutmeg
method: Brush the aubergine and potato slices with oil and roast at 200C until soft and golden.
Fry the onion and garlic, brown the lamb, add the puree, tomatoes and spices, and simmer 25 minutes.
Make the bechamel, then beat in the yolks and cheese off the heat.
Layer potato, lamb, aubergine, then top with the bechamel.
Bake at 180C fan for 40 minutes until set and golden. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.

name: Spanish Chicken & Chorizo Rice
blurb: One-pan smoky rice with chicken thighs, chorizo, peppers and peas.
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down in a wide pan, then set aside. Fry the chorizo until its oil runs.
Soften the onion and pepper, add the garlic and paprika.
Stir in the rice, then the stock (and saffron), and nestle the chicken back in.
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, adding the peas for the last 5, until the rice is tender.
Rest 5 minutes and serve with lemon and parsley.

name: Seafood & Chicken Paella
blurb: Saffron rice with prawns, mussels, chicken and peppers, with a crisp base.
ingredients: 2 tbsp tomato puree, 1 tsp smoked paprika, large pinch saffron
1.1 litres hot fish or chicken stock
method: Brown the chicken in a wide paella pan, then set aside.
Soften the onion, pepper and garlic, add the paprika and puree.
Stir in the rice, then pour in the stock with the saffron. Add the chicken.
Simmer without stirring for 15 minutes, then arrange the prawns, mussels and peas on top.
Cook 8-10 minutes more until the mussels open and the base forms a socarrat. Rest, then serve with lemon.

name: Greek Salad with Grilled Halloumi
blurb: Tomatoes, cucumber, olives and feta with warm griddled halloumi.
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano
method: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber and onion in a bowl with a big pinch of salt.
Dress with plenty of oil, a splash of vinegar and lots of oregano.
Top with the olives and feta.
Griddle the halloumi for 1-2 minutes each side until bar-marked and lay it over the salad while hot.

name: Lamb Kofta with Tomato & Chickpeas
blurb: Spiced lamb meatballs baked in a garlicky tomato and chickpea sauce.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, cinnamon, 1/2 tsp chilli
1 small onion, grated, handful of chopped mint and parsley
method: Mix the lamb with the spices, onion, herbs and seasoning, and roll into small koftas.
Brown them in an ovenproof pan, then set aside.
Fry the garlic, add the tomatoes, chickpeas and sugar, and simmer 10 minutes.
Nestle the koftas back in and bake at 200C fan for 15 minutes.
Serve with flatbreads or rice and a dollop of yoghurt.

name: Prawn Saganaki
blurb: Prawns baked in a tomato and ouzo sauce with melting feta.
ingredients: Crusty bread and parsley to serve
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the garlic and chilli, then the ouzo and let it bubble.
Add the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the prawns, crumble over the feta, and bake at 220C fan for 8-10 minutes until the prawns are pink.
Scatter with parsley and mop up with bread.

name: Rice-Stuffed Peppers (Gemista)
blurb: Peppers and tomatoes filled with herby rice and baked in olive oil.
ingredients: 4 large peppers and 4 large tomatoes, tops cut off and reserved
Handful each of mint, parsley and dill
2 potatoes, cut into wedges (to pack around)
method: Scoop out the tomatoes, chop the flesh and keep it.
Fry the onion and garlic, add the rice, tomato flesh, passata, herbs and 150ml water, and cook 5 minutes.
Fill the peppers and tomatoes about three-quarters full and replace their lids.
Sit them in a dish with the potato wedges, drizzle generously with oil, add a splash of water, and bake at 180C fan for 55-60 minutes.

name: Piri Piri Chicken
blurb: Butterflied chicken marinated in a fiery piri piri sauce and grilled.
ingredients: Piri piri: 6 red chillies, 4 garlic cloves, 1 roasted red pepper, 3 tbsp red wine vinegar, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp oregano, juice of 1 lemon
method: Blitz all the piri piri ingredients to a loose sauce. Season.
Coat the chicken in half the sauce and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Roast at 200C fan for 40-45 minutes, or grill/barbecue, basting, until charred and cooked through (75C).
Rest, then serve with the reserved sauce and chips or salad.

name: Caponata with Pasta
blurb: Sweet-sour Sicilian aubergine stew with capers and olives, over pasta.
ingredients: 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar
method: Fry the aubergine in plenty of oil until golden, then set aside.
Soften the onion and celery, add the tomatoes, capers, olives, raisins and pine nuts.
Return the aubergine, add the vinegar and sugar, and simmer 15 minutes to a jammy stew.
Toss through cooked rigatoni and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Menemen
blurb: Soft eggs cooked in a spiced pepper and tomato sauce, scooped up with bread.
ingredients: 1 tsp Turkish pepper paste or tomato puree
1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper or chilli flakes
Butter and olive oil, crusty bread to serve
method: Soften the peppers in butter and oil for 6-8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, pepper paste and chilli, and cook down to a thick sauce.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently over low heat until just set but still soft.
Serve straight from the pan with lots of bread.

name: Baked Cod with Tomatoes & Olives
blurb: Cod fillets roasted on a bed of cherry tomatoes, olives and capers.
ingredients: Zest of 1 lemon, parsley to finish
method: Toss the tomatoes, olives, capers, garlic, oregano and oil in a baking dish and roast at 200C fan for 15 minutes until bursting.
Nestle in the seasoned cod, spoon over some juices.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until the fish flakes.
Finish with lemon zest and parsley; serve with bread or potatoes.

name: Spanakopita
blurb: Crisp filo pie filled with spinach, feta, herbs and spring onion.
method: Mix the spinach, feta, spring onions, herbs and eggs; season (go easy on salt).
Brush a tin with butter and layer in half the filo sheets, brushing each.
Spread in the filling, then top with the rest of the filo, buttering as you go. Tuck in the edges.
Score the top into portions and bake at 180C fan for 40-45 minutes until deep golden and crisp.

name: Lemon & Prawn Orzo
blurb: Creamy one-pan orzo with prawns, garlic, lemon and a handful of spinach.
method: Fry the garlic and chilli in butter, add the orzo and toast for 1 minute.
Add the stock a third at a time, stirring, until the orzo is creamy and nearly tender.
Stir in the prawns and cook 3-4 minutes until pink.
Fold through the spinach, lemon zest and juice, and finish with parmesan.

name: Carne Asada Tacos
blurb: Lime-and-chilli marinated skirt steak, charred and sliced, in warm tortillas.
ingredients: Marinade: juice of 3 limes, 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp each cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, 1 tsp chipotle, 3 tbsp oil
method: Marinate the steak for at least 30 minutes.
Sear in a screaming-hot pan for 3 minutes each side; rest 5 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Slice the steak against the grain and pile into tortillas with onion, coriander and salsa.

name: Chicken Mole
blurb: Chicken simmered in a deep, complex sauce of chilli, chocolate and spice.
ingredients: 2 dried ancho and 2 dried guajillo chillies, soaked
40g dark chocolate, 30g raisins, 30g almonds, 1 corn tortilla
method: Brown the chicken; set aside.
Blitz the soaked chillies with the onion, garlic, tomatoes, raisins, almonds, torn tortilla and spices to a paste.
Fry the paste in oil for 8 minutes until darkened, then add the stock and chocolate.
Return the chicken and simmer 40 minutes; serve with rice.

name: Cochinita Pibil
blurb: Achiote-and-orange marinated pork slow-roasted until it shreds, for tacos.
ingredients: 4 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano
Pickled red onion and corn tortillas to serve
method: Blitz the achiote, citrus juice, garlic and spices and coat the pork; marinate overnight.
Wrap tightly in foil in a deep tray with the bay leaves.
Roast at 150C fan for 3 hours until meltingly tender.
Shred, moisten with the juices, and serve in tortillas with pickled onion.

name: Beef Birria Tacos (Quesabirria)
blurb: Rich chilli-braised beef, folded into cheese-crisped tacos with a cup of consommé.
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo and 2 ancho chillies, soaked
1 tsp each cumin, oregano, cinnamon, 3 cloves
Corn tortillas, 200g grated cheese, white onion and coriander
method: Brown the beef, then blitz the chillies with the onion, garlic, tomatoes and spices.
Fry the paste, add the beef and stock, cover and simmer 2.5 hours until shreddable.
Shred the beef; keep the broth as consommé.
Dip tortillas in the fatty broth, fill with beef and cheese, and fry crisp on a griddle. Serve with a cup of consommé for dipping.

name: Rainbow Veg & Halloumi Fajitas
blurb: Charred peppers, onions and halloumi with fajita spice, to wrap at the table.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fajita spice mix, juice of 1 lime, 2 tbsp oil
method: Toss the vegetables with the spice mix, lime and oil.
Char in a screaming-hot pan until soft with black edges.
Fry the halloumi separately until golden and toss it through.
Serve sizzling with warm tortillas and toppings.

name: Chipotle Prawn Tacos
blurb: Smoky-sweet prawns with a crunchy lime slaw and avocado crema.
ingredients: 2 tbsp chipotle paste, 1 tsp honey, juice of 1 lime, 2 garlic cloves
1/4 white cabbage, shredded with lime and coriander
Crema: 1 avocado, 4 tbsp soured cream, juice of 1 lime, blitzed
method: Toss the prawns with the chipotle, honey, lime and garlic.
Sear in a hot pan for 3-4 minutes until pink and caramelised.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill with slaw, prawns and a drizzle of avocado crema.

name: Huevos Rancheros
blurb: Fried eggs on tortillas with a warm ranchero salsa and refried beans.
method: Fry the onion and jalapeño, add the garlic and spices, then the tomatoes; simmer 10 minutes.
Warm the beans with a little of the salsa.
Fry the eggs and lightly char the tortillas.
Layer tortillas, beans, eggs and salsa; top with feta, coriander and lime.

name: Pozole Rojo
blurb: A brothy red chilli and hominy soup with pork and a plate of crunchy toppings.
ingredients: To serve: shredded cabbage, radish, lime, oregano, tortilla chips
method: Simmer the pork in 2 litres water with half the onion and garlic for 1.5 hours; skim.
Blitz the soaked chillies with the rest of the onion and garlic and the spices.
Fry the paste, add to the pork broth with the hominy and simmer 30 minutes.
Serve with the topping plate for everyone to build their own.

name: Mexican Street Corn Bowl
blurb: Charred corn, black beans and rice with lime crema, cheese and chilli.
ingredients: 300g rice, cooked with lime and coriander
400g tin black beans, warmed with cumin
Crema: 3 tbsp mayo, 3 tbsp soured cream, juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp chilli powder
method: Char the corn in a dry hot pan until spotty.
Warm the beans with cumin.
Mix the crema.
Build bowls with rice, corn, beans, avocado, a drizzle of crema and crumbled cheese.

name: Chicken Enchiladas Verdes
blurb: Rolled tortillas filled with chicken, baked under a tangy tomatillo salsa verde.
ingredients: Salsa verde: 400g tin tomatillos (or green tomatoes), 1 onion, 2 jalapeños, 2 garlic cloves, handful coriander, blitzed
method: Simmer the blitzed salsa verde for 10 minutes; season.
Mix the chicken with a little salsa.
Fill and roll the tortillas, lay seam-down in a dish, cover with the rest of the salsa and the cheese.
Bake at 190C fan for 20 minutes; serve with soured cream and lime.

name: Cuban Black Bean Soup
blurb: Thick, smoky black bean soup with cumin, pepper and a squeeze of lime.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp oregano
1 tbsp red wine vinegar, juice of 1 lime
Soured cream, coriander, rice to serve
method: Soften the onion and pepper, add the garlic and spices.
Add the beans (with their liquid) and stock and simmer 20 minutes.
Blitz half for a thick texture; add the vinegar and lime.
Serve over rice with soured cream and coriander.

name: Arroz con Pollo
blurb: One-pot saffron-and-tomato rice with chicken thighs, peas and peppers.
ingredients: 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp cumin, pinch of saffron or 1 tsp turmeric
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down; set aside.
Soften the onion and pepper, add garlic and spices.
Stir in the rice, then the tomatoes and stock; nestle the chicken back in.
Simmer 20 minutes, adding the peas for the last 5; rest and finish with olives and coriander.

name: Baked Bean & Cheese Chimichangas
blurb: Stuffed tortillas brushed with oil and baked crisp instead of deep-fried.
ingredients: 1 onion and 1 pepper, fried with 2 tsp cumin and 1 tsp chipotle
method: Mix the beans, rice, fried veg and half the cheese.
Fill and fold the tortillas into tight parcels.
Brush with oil and bake at 220C fan for 15-18 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Serve with the rest of the cheese melted on top and the cold toppings.

name: Mexican Baked Eggs
blurb: Eggs baked in a smoky black bean and tomato sauce with cheese and avocado.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp chipotle
method: Fry the onion and pepper, add the garlic and spices.
Add the tomatoes and beans and simmer 12 minutes.
Make wells, crack in the eggs, scatter with cheese, cover and cook 6-8 minutes.
Top with avocado and coriander; serve with warm tortillas.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Carnitas
blurb: Pork shoulder slow-cooked with orange and cumin, then crisped under the grill.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp oregano, 2 bay leaves
Corn tortillas, white onion, coriander, lime, salsa
method: Put the pork in a slow cooker with the onion, garlic, spices, bay and squeezed orange halves.
Cook on low for 8 hours (or 140C oven for 4 hours) until falling apart.
Shred, spread on a tray with some cooking juices, and grill until crisp at the edges.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, coriander, lime and salsa.

name: Mushroom & Cheese Quesadillas
blurb: Griddled tortillas oozing with garlicky mushrooms and melted cheese.
ingredients: 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, pinch of chilli
method: Fry the mushrooms until golden, add the garlic, cumin and chilli.
Spread cheese over half of each tortilla, top with mushrooms and spring onion, and fold.
Toast in a dry pan for 2-3 minutes each side until crisp and molten.
Cut into wedges and serve with soured cream and salsa.

name: Ropa Vieja
blurb: Cuban shredded beef braised with peppers, onions, tomatoes and olives.
ingredients: 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 2 tbsp tomato purée
1 tsp each cumin, oregano, smoked paprika
Rice and black beans to serve
method: Simmer the beef in water to cover with a bay leaf for 1.5 hours until tender; reserve the broth and shred.
Soften the peppers and onions, add the garlic, spices and purée.
Add the tomatoes, 200ml of the beef broth and the shredded beef.
Simmer 30 minutes, stir in the olives, and serve with rice and beans.

name: Loaded Beef Nachos
blurb: A tray of tortilla chips under spiced beef, cheese, jalapeños and all the toppings.
ingredients: 1 onion, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tbsp tomato purée
Guacamole, soured cream, salsa, spring onions
method: Brown the mince with the onion, spices and purée; add a splash of water and simmer to a thick mixture.
Layer half the chips on a tray, half the beef and half the cheese; repeat.
Bake at 200C fan for 8-10 minutes until molten.
Pile on the cold toppings and eat straight from the tray.

name: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
blurb: Crisp tortillas topped with refried beans and smoky chipotle shredded chicken.
ingredients: 2 tbsp chipotle in adobo, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp cumin
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the tomatoes, chipotle, oregano and cumin; cook to a thick sauce.
Stir in the chicken and loosen with a splash of water.
Spread the tostadas with refried beans, then the tinga.
Top with avocado, lime and coriander.

name: Roast Veg Burrito Bowl
blurb: Cumin-roasted veg with coriander-lime rice, beans, guac and salsa.
ingredients: 1 sweet potato, 1 pepper, 1 red onion, 1 courgette, chopped
2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 2 tbsp oil
300g rice, cooked with lime and coriander
method: Toss the veg with the spices and oil and roast at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.
Stir lime and coriander through the rice; warm the beans.
Build bowls with rice, beans, roast veg and a selection of toppings.
Finish with lime and hot sauce.

name: Baked Chicken Taquitos
blurb: Tightly rolled tortillas filled with cheesy chicken, baked until crunchy.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cumin, smoked paprika, 1 tsp chipotle
Oil spray; soured cream, salsa, guacamole to serve
method: Mix the chicken with the cream cheese, grated cheese and spices.
Warm the tortillas so they roll without cracking; add a line of filling and roll tight.
Lay seam-down on a tray, spray with oil, and bake at 220C fan for 15-18 minutes until crisp.
Serve with soured cream, salsa and guacamole.

name: Fish Veracruz
blurb: White fish baked in a bright tomato sauce with olives, capers and chilli.
ingredients: 100g green olives, 2 tbsp capers, 1-2 pickled jalapeños
method: Fry the onion and garlic, add the tomatoes, olives, capers, jalapeños, oregano and bay.
Simmer 15 minutes to a rich sauce.
Nestle in the seasoned fish, spoon sauce over, and bake at 190C fan for 12-15 minutes.
Finish with coriander; serve with rice.

name: Beef Tacos
blurb: Spiced beef in soft tortillas with all the fresh toppings.
ingredients: 2 tsp each ground cumin and smoked paprika, 1 tsp oregano, 1/2 tsp chilli powder
To serve: shredded lettuce, tomato salsa, lime, hot sauce, coriander
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the mince and brown well, then stir in the puree and a splash of water and simmer for 8 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Fill with the beef and pile on the toppings; finish with lime and hot sauce.

name: Chicken Fajitas
blurb: Sizzling strips of chicken, peppers and onions to wrap at the table.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fajita spice mix (or cumin, paprika, oregano, garlic powder)
To serve: soured cream, guacamole, salsa
method: Toss the chicken with the spice mix, lime and oil.
Sear the chicken in a screaming-hot pan until charred and cooked, then remove.
Char the peppers and onions in the same pan until soft with black edges.
Return the chicken, toss together and serve sizzling with warm tortillas and toppings.

name: Chilli con Carne
blurb: Deep, smoky beef and bean chilli, better the next day.
ingredients: 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp cocoa, 1-2 tsp chipotle paste
Rice, soured cream and coriander to serve
method: Brown the mince hard, then remove. Soften the onions, add the garlic and spices.
Return the beef, add the tomatoes, stock cube, oregano and 200ml water.
Simmer gently for 40 minutes, then add the beans and cook 15 minutes more.
Season, rest a few minutes and serve over rice with soured cream and coriander.

name: Black Bean Enchiladas
blurb: Rolled tortillas filled with beans and cheese, baked under a chilli-tomato sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 500g passata, 1 tbsp chipotle paste, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp oregano
method: Fry the onion and pepper with the spices, add the beans and lightly mash. Season.
Simmer the sauce ingredients for 5 minutes.
Spread a little sauce in a dish, fill and roll the tortillas, and lay them seam-down.
Pour over the rest of the sauce and the cheese, and bake at 190C fan for 20 minutes until bubbling.

name: Pork Carnitas
blurb: Slow-cooked pork shoulder crisped in its own fat, for tacos.
ingredients: 1.5kg boneless pork shoulder, in large chunks
2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp oregano, 2 bay leaves
Corn tortillas, white onion, coriander and lime to serve
method: Put the pork in a heavy pot with the onion, garlic, spices, bay and the squeezed orange halves. Add water to barely cover.
Simmer very gently, covered, for about 2.5 hours until meltingly tender.
Uncover, remove the aromatics, and boil off the liquid until the pork fries in its own fat.
Let it crisp, shredding with forks, then serve in warm tortillas with onion, coriander and lime.

name: Cheese & Bean Quesadillas
blurb: Crisp folded tortillas oozing with cheese, beans and pickled jalapenos.
ingredients: Soured cream and salsa to serve
method: Spread beans over half of each tortilla, top with cheese, jalapenos and spring onion, and fold.
Toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes each side until crisp and molten.
Cut into wedges and serve with soured cream and salsa.

name: Huevos Rancheros
blurb: Fried eggs on tortillas with a warm ranchero salsa and black beans.
ingredients: 1 garlic clove, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika
Coriander, feta or crumbled cheese, lime
method: Fry the onion and jalapeno, add the garlic and spices, then the tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes to a salsa.
Warm the black beans with a little of the salsa and lightly mash.
Fry the eggs to your liking and lightly char the tortillas.
Layer tortillas, beans, eggs and salsa; top with coriander, cheese and lime.

name: Baja Fish Tacos
blurb: Crisp battered white fish in tortillas with slaw and lime crema.
ingredients: 120g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 180ml cold sparkling water, 1 tsp paprika
1/4 white cabbage, shredded, with lime and coriander
Crema: 4 tbsp soured cream, 2 tbsp mayo, zest and juice of 1 lime
method: Whisk the flour, baking powder, paprika and sparkling water into a thin batter.
Dip the fish and fry in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain.
Toss the cabbage with lime, salt and coriander; mix the crema.
Fill warm tortillas with slaw, fish and a drizzle of crema.

name: Chicken Burrito Bowl
blurb: Everything from a burrito, in a bowl: rice, beans, chicken, salsa, guac.
ingredients: 500g chicken thigh, sliced, with 2 tsp fajita spice
250g rice, cooked with lime and coriander
400g tin black beans, warmed with cumin
method: Toss the chicken in the spice and sear in a hot pan until charred and cooked.
Warm the beans; stir lime and coriander through the rice.
Build bowls with rice, beans, chicken and a selection of toppings.
Finish with lime and hot sauce.

name: Chicken Tinga Tostadas
blurb: Smoky chipotle shredded chicken piled on crisp tortillas.
ingredients: To serve: refried beans, avocado, lime, coriander
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the tomatoes, chipotle, oregano and cumin, and cook to a thick sauce.
Stir in the shredded chicken and warm through, loosening with a splash of water.
Spread the tostadas with refried beans, top with the tinga, and finish with avocado, lime and coriander.

name: Mexican Street Corn Rice
blurb: Charred sweetcorn folded through rice with lime, chilli and cheese.
ingredients: Juice of 1 lime, handful of coriander
method: Cook the rice and keep warm.
Char the corn in a dry hot pan until spotty and sweet.
Mix the mayo, soured cream, lime and chilli, then fold through the rice and corn.
Top with crumbled cheese and coriander.

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Chilli
blurb: A hearty meat-free chilli with sweet potato, three beans and chipotle.
ingredients: 2 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1-2 tsp chipotle paste
400g tin black beans and 400g tin kidney beans, drained
Rice, lime and coriander to serve
method: Fry the onion and pepper, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, beans and 200ml water.
Simmer for 25-30 minutes until the sweet potato is tender and the sauce is thick.
Season and serve with rice, lime and coriander.

name: Baked Lamb Koftas in Tomato with Tahini
blurb: Spiced lamb meatballs baked in tomato sauce, finished with a tahini drizzle.
ingredients: 1 small onion grated, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, cinnamon, paprika
2 x 400g tins chopped tomatoes, 1 tsp sugar
Tahini sauce: 4 tbsp tahini, juice of 1 lemon, water
method: Mix the lamb with the onion, garlic, spices and herbs; roll into koftas.
Brown in an ovenproof pan, then set aside.
Fry the garlic scraps, add the tomatoes and sugar, and simmer 10 minutes; return the koftas.
Bake at 200C fan for 15 minutes; drizzle with loosened tahini and serve with flatbreads.

name: Chicken Fattoush
blurb: Sumac chicken over a crunchy chopped salad with crisp pitta and pomegranate.
ingredients: 4 chicken breasts, 2 tbsp sumac, juice of 1 lemon, 2 tbsp oil
Dressing: 4 tbsp olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 1 tsp sumac, 1 garlic clove, pinch of cinnamon
method: Toss the chicken with the sumac, lemon and oil; griddle and slice.
Whisk the dressing.
Toss the chopped vegetables and herbs with the dressing.
Fold in most of the crisp pitta, top with chicken, the rest of the pitta and pomegranate.

name: Ful Medames
blurb: Stewed fava beans mashed with cumin, lemon, garlic and olive oil — dinner or breakfast.
ingredients: 2 x 400g tins ful (fava beans) or brown beans
To serve: chopped tomato, parsley, red onion, chilli, boiled eggs, flatbread
method: Warm the beans in their liquid with the garlic and cumin.
Roughly mash, adding the lemon juice and most of the oil.
Season well and loosen with a little water if needed.
Top with tomato, parsley, onion, chilli and a drizzle of oil; serve with flatbread and eggs.

name: Chicken & Freekeh Pilaf
blurb: Smoky green freekeh cooked with chicken, warm spice, almonds and herbs.
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down; set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic, add the spices, then the freekeh for 1 minute.
Add the stock, nestle the chicken back in, cover and simmer 25 minutes.
Rest, fluff, and top with almonds, parsley and pomegranate.

name: Batata Harra with Fried Eggs
blurb: Crisp fried potatoes tossed with garlic, coriander and chilli, topped with eggs.
ingredients: Juice of half a lemon, 4 tbsp olive oil
method: Parboil the potatoes 5 minutes, drain and steam-dry.
Fry in the oil until deep golden and crisp.
Add the garlic and chilli for 1 minute, then the coriander and lemon.
Fry the eggs and serve on top of the potatoes.

name: Spiced Lamb & Rice (Quick Mansaf-Style)
blurb: Tender lamb over spiced rice with a warm yoghurt sauce and toasted nuts.
ingredients: 2 tsp each cumin, coriander, 1 tsp each cinnamon, allspice, cardamom
50g toasted almonds and pine nuts, parsley
method: Brown the lamb, add the onion, garlic and spices, then water to cover; simmer 1.5 hours.
Cook the rice with a little of the lamb broth and a cinnamon stick.
Warm the yoghurt gently with the cornflour and a ladle of broth, whisking, so it doesn't split.
Pile rice on a platter, top with lamb, pour over the yoghurt sauce and scatter with nuts and parsley.

name: Green Shakshuka
blurb: Eggs baked in a herby spinach, chard and leek base with feta.
ingredients: 3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp coriander, pinch of chilli
Big handful each parsley, coriander and dill
method: Soften the leeks, add the garlic and spices.
Add the greens in batches until wilted, then most of the herbs; season.
Make wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook 5-7 minutes.
Crumble over the feta and the rest of the herbs; serve with bread.

name: Koshari
blurb: Egypt's national dish — rice, lentils and macaroni with spiced tomato sauce and crispy onions.
ingredients: Sauce: 400g tin chopped tomatoes, 3 garlic cloves, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1 tbsp white vinegar, chilli
3 onions, thinly sliced and fried until deep brown and crisp
method: Cook the rice, lentils and macaroni separately.
Simmer the sauce ingredients for 15 minutes to a spiced, slightly sharp tomato sauce.
Fry the onions slowly until dark and crisp.
Layer rice, lentils, macaroni and chickpeas; ladle over the sauce and pile with crispy onions.

name: Msakhan Rolls
blurb: Sumac-and-onion chicken rolled in flatbread and baked crisp, with pine nuts.
ingredients: 4 large onions, sliced and slow-cooked in olive oil
method: Toss the shredded chicken with the sweet onions, sumac and allspice.
Spread over the flatbreads and scatter with pine nuts.
Roll up tightly and brush all over with olive oil.
Bake at 200C fan for 15-20 minutes until crisp; cut into pieces.

name: Mujadara with Crispy Onions
blurb: Lentils and rice with warm spice and a mountain of caramelised onions.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, cinnamon, allspice
method: Simmer the lentils 15 minutes until nearly tender; drain.
Cook the onions slowly in the oil for 25 minutes until deep brown; remove half.
Add the spices to the pan, then the rice, lentils and 400ml water; cover and cook 12-15 minutes.
Rest, fork through, and top with the reserved onions, yoghurt and parsley.

name: Baharat Chicken & Rice One-Pot
blurb: Chicken thighs and rice cooked together with warm baharat spice and vermicelli.
ingredients: 2 tbsp baharat, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cardamom pods
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down; set aside.
Toast the vermicelli in the fat until golden, then soften the onion and garlic with the spices.
Stir in the rice, add the stock, and nestle the chicken back in.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes; rest and top with almonds and parsley.

name: Lamb, Apricot & Almond Tagine
blurb: Slow-cooked lamb with warm spice, dried apricots and toasted almonds, with couscous.
ingredients: 2 tsp each cumin, ginger, 1 tsp each cinnamon, turmeric, pinch of saffron
200g dried apricots, 50g toasted almonds, 1 tbsp honey
method: Brown the lamb in batches, then set aside.
Soften the onions, add the garlic and spices for 2 minutes.
Return the lamb, add the tomatoes and stock, cover and cook at 150C fan for 1.5 hours.
Stir in the apricots and honey and cook 30 minutes; scatter with almonds and coriander, serve with couscous.

name: Zaalouk with Baked Eggs
blurb: Smoky Moroccan aubergine and tomato dip with eggs baked on top.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cumin, smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp chilli
Big handful of coriander and parsley
method: Fry the aubergine in plenty of oil until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and spices, then the tomatoes, and cook down to a thick, jammy dip.
Stir in most of the herbs; make wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook 6-8 minutes; scatter with herbs and serve with flatbread.

name: Chicken Shawarma Rice Bowl
blurb: Spiced chicken over turmeric rice with pickles, salad and garlic sauce.
ingredients: 150g yoghurt, juice of 1 lemon, 2 tsp each cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, 1 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, cayenne
Chopped salad, pickled chillies and turnip
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt and spices for 1 hour.
Roast at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes until charred; slice.
Cook the turmeric rice.
Build bowls with rice, chicken, salad, pickles and a good drizzle of garlic sauce.

name: Butter Bean & Roast Pepper Stew
blurb: Creamy butter beans in a smoky roasted pepper and tomato sauce with feta.
ingredients: 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp cumin, pinch of chilli
method: Fry the onion and garlic, add the spices.
Add the blitzed peppers and tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Fold in the beans with a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes, mashing a few.
Crumble over feta and parsley; serve with flatbread.

name: Sabich
blurb: Pita stuffed with fried aubergine, boiled egg, hummus, salad and amba.
ingredients: 2 aubergines, sliced and fried until golden
Chopped salad of tomato, cucumber and parsley
Tahini sauce and amba (mango pickle) or hot sauce
method: Fry the aubergine slices in shallow oil until deep golden; drain.
Warm the pitas and open them up.
Spread with hummus, then layer aubergine, egg and salad.
Drizzle with tahini and a little amba or hot sauce.

name: Turkish Red Lentil Soup (Mercimek Çorbası)
blurb: Smooth red lentil soup finished with a mint-paprika butter and lemon.
ingredients: Butter with 1 tsp dried mint and 1 tsp paprika, lemon wedges
method: Soften the onion, carrot and potato, add the purée and cumin.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer 20 minutes until everything is soft.
Blitz completely smooth and season.
Melt the butter with the mint and paprika; swirl into each bowl and serve with lemon.

name: Chicken Kabsa
blurb: Fragrant Saudi spiced rice cooked with chicken, dried lime and warm spice.
ingredients: 2 dried limes (pierced), 1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom pods, 3 cloves, 1 bay leaf
2 tbsp kabsa spice mix (or baharat), 400g tin chopped tomatoes
method: Brown the chicken, then set aside. Soften the onion and garlic with the whole spices.
Add the spice mix and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add the stock and chicken and simmer 25 minutes; lift out the chicken and grill to crisp.
Cook the rice in the same broth for 15 minutes; serve topped with the chicken, nuts and raisins.

name: Shish Barak (Dumplings in Yoghurt)
blurb: Little lamb dumplings simmered in a warm garlicky yoghurt sauce with mint butter.
ingredients: 300g plain flour, 150ml warm water, pinch of salt (dough)
300g lamb mince, 1 small onion, 1 tsp each cumin, allspice, cinnamon, 30g pine nuts
method: Knead the dough and rest 30 minutes; fry the spiced lamb and pine nuts.
Roll the dough thin, cut small circles, fill and fold into tortellini shapes; bake at 200C for 10 minutes.
Whisk the yoghurt with the cornflour, garlic and a little water; heat gently, stirring, until thickened.
Add the dumplings and simmer 5 minutes; pour over the mint butter.

name: Roast Cauliflower, Chickpea & Tahini Bowl
blurb: Spiced roast cauliflower and chickpeas over herby couscous with tahini.
ingredients: 2 tbsp ras el hanout or baharat, 3 tbsp oil
250g couscous, big handful of parsley and mint
Tahini sauce: 4 tbsp tahini, juice of 1 lemon, 1 garlic clove, water
method: Toss the cauliflower and chickpeas with the spice and oil and roast at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.
Soak the couscous in boiling stock, fluff, and stir through the herbs.
Whisk the tahini sauce until pourable.
Build bowls with couscous, the roast veg and chickpeas, tahini, pomegranate and almonds.

name: Chicken Shawarma Traybake
blurb: Spiced yoghurt-marinated chicken thighs roasted with onions, for wraps.
ingredients: 150g yoghurt, juice of 1 lemon, 3 tbsp olive oil
2 tsp each cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, 1 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp cayenne
Flatbreads, garlic sauce, pickles, salad to serve
method: Mix the yoghurt, lemon, oil, spices and garlic and coat the chicken. Marinate 1 hour or overnight.
Spread on a tray with the onions and roast at 220C fan for 30-35 minutes until charred at the edges.
Rest, then slice.
Pile into warm flatbreads with garlic sauce, pickles and salad.

name: Lamb Koftas with Flatbread & Tahini
blurb: Grilled spiced lamb skewers with warm flatbread, tahini sauce and salad.
ingredients: 1 tsp each cumin, coriander, cinnamon, 1/2 tsp allspice
Handful of parsley and mint, chopped
Tahini sauce: 4 tbsp tahini, juice of 1 lemon, 1 small garlic clove, water to loosen
method: Mix the lamb with the onion, garlic, spices and herbs; season and knead well.
Shape around skewers or into fat fingers.
Grill or griddle for 8-10 minutes, turning, until charred and just cooked.
Whisk the tahini with lemon, garlic and water until creamy.
Serve the koftas in flatbreads with the tahini sauce and chopped salad.

name: Falafel Bowl
blurb: Crisp home-fried falafel with hummus, salad, pickles and flatbread.
ingredients: 1 onion, 4 garlic cloves, big handful each parsley and coriander
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1/2 tsp baking powder
To serve: hummus, chopped salad, pickled turnip, flatbread, tahini sauce
method: Drain the chickpeas and blitz with the onion, garlic, herbs and spices to a coarse, sandy paste. Chill 30 minutes.
Stir in the baking powder and shape into small patties.
Deep or shallow fry at 170C for 3-4 minutes until deep brown and crisp.
Build bowls with hummus, salad, pickles, falafel and a drizzle of tahini, with warm flatbread.

name: Shakshuka
blurb: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, with bread to dip.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp caraway, chilli to taste
method: Soften the onion and pepper for 8 minutes, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 12-15 minutes until thick.
Make wells and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook 5-7 minutes until the whites are set and yolks runny.
Crumble over feta, scatter with coriander, and serve with bread.

name: Persian Chicken with Jewelled Rice
blurb: Saffron chicken with barberry, pistachio and orange-zested basmati.
ingredients: Large pinch saffron in 3 tbsp warm water
150g yoghurt, 1 tsp turmeric, juice of 1 lemon
40g barberries or dried cranberries, 40g pistachios, 40g flaked almonds
Zest of 1 orange, 30g butter, 1 tsp sugar
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt, half the saffron water, turmeric and lemon for 1 hour.
Roast at 200C fan for 35-40 minutes until golden.
Parboil the rinsed rice for 6 minutes, drain, then steam in the pan with butter for 15 minutes until fluffy.
Fry the barberries, nuts, orange zest and sugar in a little butter for 2 minutes.
Fork the rest of the saffron water through the rice and top with the nut mixture. Serve with the chicken.

name: Mujadara
blurb: Lentils and rice with masses of sweet caramelised onions.
ingredients: 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp allspice
method: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 minutes until nearly tender, then drain.
Cook the onions slowly in the oil for 20-25 minutes until deep brown and jammy; remove half.
Add the spices to the pan, then the rice, lentils and 400ml water. Cover and cook 12-15 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes, fork through, and top with the reserved onions, yoghurt and parsley.

name: Fattoush with Grilled Halloumi
blurb: Crunchy chopped salad with sumac, mint and crisp pitta, plus halloumi.
ingredients: 2 pitta breads, torn and toasted or fried until crisp
3 tomatoes, 1 cucumber, 4 radishes, 1 romaine, all chopped
Bunch each of parsley and mint
Dressing: 4 tbsp olive oil, juice of 1 lemon, 1 tsp sumac, 1 small garlic clove, pinch of cinnamon
method: Whisk the dressing.
Toss the chopped vegetables and herbs with the dressing.
Griddle the halloumi until golden on both sides.
Fold most of the crisp pitta through the salad, top with halloumi and the rest of the pitta, and a final dusting of sumac.

name: Lamb & Apricot Tagine
blurb: Slow-cooked lamb with warm spices, dried apricots and almonds, with couscous.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp turmeric, pinch of saffron
1 tbsp honey, couscous and coriander to serve
method: Brown the lamb in batches in a casserole, then set aside.
Soften the onions, add the garlic and spices for 2 minutes.
Return the lamb, add the tomatoes and stock, cover and cook at 150C fan for 1.5 hours.
Stir in the apricots and honey and cook 30 minutes more until the lamb is very tender.
Scatter with almonds and coriander and serve with couscous.

name: Mezze Plate
blurb: A spread of baba ganoush, hummus, tabbouleh, olives and warm flatbread.
ingredients: 2 aubergines (for baba ganoush) with 3 tbsp tahini, 1 garlic clove, juice of 1 lemon
400g tin chickpeas with 3 tbsp tahini, garlic, lemon (for hummus)
Tabbouleh: 60g fine bulgur, big bunch parsley, mint, 3 tomatoes, lemon, olive oil
Olive oil and sumac to finish
method: Char the aubergines over a flame or under the grill until collapsed, then scoop the flesh and blitz with tahini, garlic and lemon.
Blitz the chickpeas with tahini, garlic, lemon and a little water until smooth for the hummus.
Soak the bulgur, then mix with masses of chopped parsley and mint, tomato, lemon and oil.
Spread everything on a board with olives, pickles and warm flatbread, finished with oil and sumac.

name: Chickpea & Spinach Stew
blurb: A quick, warming stew of chickpeas, spinach and tomato with cumin and lemon.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cinnamon
Juice of 1 lemon, flatbread and yoghurt to serve
method: Fry the onion until soft, add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer for 12 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas.
Stir through the spinach until wilted and finish with lemon.
Serve with flatbread and a spoon of yoghurt.

name: Musakhan
blurb: Sumac and onion roast chicken served over flatbread with pine nuts.
ingredients: 4 tbsp sumac, 1 tsp allspice, 1/2 tsp cinnamon
50g pine nuts, toasted, parsley to finish
method: Rub the chicken with 1 tbsp sumac, salt and oil, and roast at 200C fan for 35-40 minutes.
Meanwhile cook the onions slowly in the oil for 25 minutes until soft, then stir in the rest of the sumac and the allspice.
Lay the flatbreads on a tray, spread with the onions, and sit the chicken on top with its juices.
Return to the oven for 10 minutes, then scatter with pine nuts and parsley.

name: Aubergine Fatteh
blurb: Crisp pitta layered with fried aubergine, chickpeas and garlicky yoghurt.
ingredients: 2 aubergines, cubed and fried until golden
400g yoghurt, 1 garlic clove, juice of 1/2 lemon
1 tsp sumac, parsley and pomegranate seeds to finish
method: Beat the yoghurt with the garlic and lemon; season.
Layer the crisp pitta on a platter, then the warm chickpeas, then the fried aubergine.
Spoon over the garlicky yoghurt.
Fry the pine nuts in the butter until golden and pour over, then finish with sumac, parsley and pomegranate.

name: Big Batch Beef Chilli
blurb: A deep, cocoa-spiked beef chilli that feeds the family and freezes brilliantly.
method: Brown the mince in batches, then soften the onions.
Return the meat with the spices, tomatoes, beans and stock.
Simmer partly covered for 1 hour until thick. Serve with rice; freeze the rest.

name: One-Pot Chicken & Leek Casserole
blurb: Bone-in chicken braised with leeks, potatoes and mustard cream. A family one-pot.
method: Brown the chicken skin-side down, remove.
Soften the leeks, add potatoes, stock and thyme, sit the chicken back on top.
Cover and simmer 40 minutes, stir in the crème fraîche and mustard for the last 5.

name: Family Bolognese
blurb: A low-and-slow ragu made in a big pan for spaghetti tonight and lasagne later.
ingredients: 2 onions, 2 carrots, 2 celery sticks, finely chopped
method: Fry the pancetta and soffritto until soft, add the mince and brown.
Add the milk and let it cook away, then the wine, then the tomatoes.
Simmer very gently for 1.5-2 hours. Toss with spaghetti; freeze the rest.

name: Sausage & Butter Bean Casserole
blurb: Browned sausages simmered with butter beans, peppers and smoked paprika. Feeds four, freezes well.
method: Brown the sausages and set aside.
Soften the onion and peppers, add the paprika, tomatoes, beans and stock.
Return the sausages and simmer 30 minutes until rich.

name: Slow Dal Makhani
blurb: Black lentils simmered for hours with butter and cream until velvety. Batch-cook gold.
ingredients: 250g whole black urad lentils, soaked overnight
method: Boil the drained lentils and beans in fresh water until very soft, about 1 hour.
Add the tomatoes, ginger-garlic and garam masala and simmer 1 hour, mashing occasionally.
Stir in the butter and cream and cook gently 20 minutes more.

name: Big Pot of Minestrone
blurb: A clear-out-the-veg-drawer soup with beans, pasta and pesto. Makes a vat.
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery, add the courgette.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until tender. Serve with pesto and Parmesan.

name: Oven-Pulled Pork Shoulder
blurb: A spice-rubbed shoulder cooked low for hours until it shreds. Rolls, slaw, and leftovers for days.
ingredients: soft rolls and slaw to serve
method: Rub the pork all over with the mixed dry spices and sugar.
Sit in a deep tray with the cider, cover tightly with foil and cook at 150C for 5-6 hours.
Rest, then shred with two forks and moisten with the pan juices. Pile into rolls with slaw.

name: Big Batch Chickpea & Spinach Curry
blurb: A freezer-friendly tomato curry of chickpeas, sweet potato and spinach.
method: Fry the onions, add the curry paste and cook out.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and spinach until hot. Cool the extra for the freezer.

name: Beef Stew with Herb Dumplings
blurb: Slow-braised beef and root veg under fluffy suet dumplings. The Sunday-into-Monday classic.
method: Toss the beef in seasoned flour and brown, then soften the veg.
Add the stock and stout, cover and cook at 160C for 2 hours.
Mix the dumpling flour, suet, parsley and water, drop on top and cook 25 minutes uncovered.

name: Family Tray Mac & Cheese
blurb: A big dish of three-cheese macaroni with a crunchy top. Feeds six, reheats a dream.
method: Cook the macaroni. Make a roux, whisk in the milk to a smooth sauce, melt in the cheddar and mustard.
Fold in the pasta, tip into a big dish, top with breadcrumbs and Parmesan.
Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until bubbling and golden.

name: Lentil Shepherd's Pie
blurb: A hearty meat-free shepherd's pie with lentils, mushrooms and a fluffy mash lid.
method: Soften the veg, add the lentils, purée, soy and stock and simmer 30 minutes until thick.
Boil and mash the potatoes with oil and seasoning.
Spread the lentils in a dish, top with mash and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

name: Proper Chicken Noodle Soup
blurb: A whole poached chicken becomes stock, meat and a big pot of restorative noodle soup.
method: Cover the chicken with water, add halved veg and herbs, simmer gently 1.5 hours.
Lift out the chicken, strip the meat, strain the stock and skim.
Return the stock, add sliced veg, noodles, corn, peas and shredded chicken and simmer 10 minutes.

name: Slow Ratatouille
blurb: Aubergine, courgette and peppers stewed separately then together for a silky Provençal batch.
method: Fry each vegetable separately in oil until coloured, setting each aside.
Soften the onions and garlic, add all the tomatoes and herbs.
Fold everything back together and simmer very gently for 40 minutes.

name: Goan Coconut Fish Curry
blurb: A tangy, mild coconut curry you can build ahead and drop the fish into to serve.
method: Fry the onions until golden, add the ginger-garlic and dry spices.
Add the coconut milk, tamarind and curry leaves and simmer 15 minutes.
Slide in the fish and poach gently for 6-8 minutes. Serve with rice.

name: One-Pot Jambalaya
blurb: Chicken, smoked sausage and prawns with rice, peppers and Cajun spice in one big pot.
method: Brown the chicken and sausage, add the chopped veg and Cajun spice.
Stir in the rice, tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the prawns, cover and cook 5 minutes more until pink and the rice is tender.

name: Ham Hock & Split Pea Soup
blurb: A smoked ham hock simmered with split peas until thick and comforting. Big pot, small effort.
method: Cover the hock with water, add the split peas, veg and bay and simmer 2 hours.
Lift out the hock, shred the meat and discard the fat and bone.
Blend the soup partly for texture, return the ham and season with pepper.

name: Make-Ahead Butter Chicken
blurb: Marinated chicken in a smooth, mildly spiced tomato-cream sauce. Doubles and freezes beautifully.
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt and half the garam masala for an hour.
Fry the ginger-garlic in the butter, add tomatoes and remaining spice, simmer 20 minutes then blend smooth.
Add the chicken and cook 15 minutes, finish with cream and honey.

name: Chicken, Olive & Preserved Lemon Tagine
blurb: A fragrant North African braise for a crowd, better made the day before.
method: Brown the chicken, soften the onions with the ras el hanout and saffron.
Return the chicken with the stock, cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Add the olives and preserved lemon and reduce for 15 minutes. Serve with couscous.

name: Roast Vegetable Lasagne
blurb: Layers of roasted courgette, pepper and aubergine with tomato sauce and béchamel. A big family bake.
method: Roast the sliced veg with oil at 220C for 25 minutes; simmer the tomatoes to a sauce.
Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and milk.
Layer tomato veg, pasta and béchamel three times, top with cheese and bake at 190C for 40 minutes.

name: Pot-Roast Chicken with Vegetables
blurb: A whole chicken braised on a bed of veg so it stays juicy and makes its own gravy.
method: Brown the chicken all over in a casserole, remove.
Add the veg and garlic, sit the chicken on top, pour in the wine and stock.
Cover and cook at 180C for 1 hour 10, uncovering for the last 20 to colour.

name: Smoky Black Bean Soup
blurb: A thick, silky black bean soup with cumin and lime, topped with soured cream and coriander.
ingredients: soured cream and coriander to serve
method: Soften the onions and garlic, add the spices.
Add the beans and stock and simmer 20 minutes.
Blend most of the soup smooth, leave some whole, finish with lime and toppings.

name: Slow Massaman Beef
blurb: Beef shin simmered soft in a sweet, mild massaman curry with potatoes and peanuts. Batch it.
method: Fry the paste in a little coconut cream, add the beef and coat.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, cinnamon, fish sauce and sugar, simmer 1.5 hours.
Add the potatoes and peanuts and cook 30 minutes more until everything is tender.

name: Turkey & Lentil Ragu
blurb: A lighter Bolognese-style ragu bulked with lentils. Big pan, low cost, freezes fine.
method: Brown the turkey mince, soften the chopped veg.
Add the purée, lentils, tomatoes and stock and simmer 40 minutes until thick.
Season well and toss with pasta.

name: Weeknight Cassoulet
blurb: A shortcut French bean stew with sausage, bacon and a crisp breadcrumb crust.
method: Brown the sausages and lardons, soften the onion and garlic.
Add the beans, tomatoes, stock and thyme and simmer 30 minutes.
Scatter with breadcrumbs and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until crusted.

name: Vegetable Biryani
blurb: Layered spiced rice and vegetables steamed together until fragrant. A generous one-pot.
method: Par-boil the rice with whole spices until 70 percent done, drain.
Cook the vegetables in yoghurt and biryani masala until nearly tender.
Layer rice and veg with fried onions and herbs, drizzle saffron milk, cover and steam 25 minutes.

name: Classic Chilli Con Carne
blurb: The reliable family chilli — beef, beans, tomato and just enough heat. Doubles easily.
method: Brown the mince, soften the onions, stir in the purée and spices.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer 40 minutes.
Season and serve with rice; freeze what you don't eat.

name: Family Fish Pie
blurb: White fish, salmon and prawns in a dill sauce under cheesy mash. Feeds six, comforts all.
method: Poach the fish in the milk, lift out and flake; keep the milk.
Make a sauce with the butter, flour and poaching milk, stir in the herbs and fish.
Top with mash and cheese and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until golden.

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Chilli
blurb: A hearty vegan chilli built on roasted sweet potato and smoky chipotle. Great for meal prep.
method: Roast the sweet potato with oil at 220C for 25 minutes.
Soften the onions with the chipotle, cumin and cocoa, add the tomatoes and beans and simmer 20 minutes.
Fold in the sweet potato and serve over rice.

name: Braised Beef Shin (Osso Buco Style)
blurb: Cross-cut beef shin braised in wine and tomato until the marrow melts. A weekend batch.
method: Dust and brown the shin, remove, soften the diced veg.
Return the meat with the wine, tomatoes and stock, cover and cook at 150C for 3 hours.
Finish with a scatter of lemon-garlic-parsley gremolata over soft polenta.

name: Spiced Red Lentil Soup
blurb: A thick, warming lentil soup with cumin, carrot and lemon. Cheap, fast, freezer staple.
method: Soften the onions and carrots, add the spices.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer 25 minutes until collapsing.
Blend to your liking, sharpen with plenty of lemon.

name: Mild Chicken Korma for a Crowd
blurb: A gentle almond-and-coconut korma the whole table can eat. Scales and freezes well.
method: Fry the onions slowly until soft and golden, add the korma paste and whole spices.
Add the chicken and brown, then the coconut milk and almonds and simmer 25 minutes.
Stir in the yoghurt off the boil and serve with rice.

name: Big Pan Vegetable Paella
blurb: Saffron rice with artichokes, peppers, beans and peas cooked in one wide pan for a crowd.
method: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic, stir in the rice and saffron.
Add the stock and beans and simmer without stirring for 18 minutes.
Scatter over the artichokes and peas, rest 5 minutes, serve with lemon.

name: Slow Beef Rendang
blurb: Beef simmered in spiced coconut until dark, dry and intense. Make a lot; it only improves.
ingredients: 1 rendang spice paste jar or homemade
method: Fry the spice paste until fragrant, add the beef and coat.
Add the coconut milk, lime leaves, lemongrass and tamarind, simmer uncovered 2.5 hours, stirring more towards the end.
Stir in the toasted coconut when the sauce is almost dry and clinging.

name: Beetroot Borscht
blurb: A deep-magenta beetroot and cabbage soup with a swirl of soured cream and dill. Big batch.
method: Soften the onion and carrot, add the beetroot, potato, cabbage and purée.
Add the stock and simmer 40 minutes until everything is tender.
Sharpen with the vinegar and serve with soured cream and dill.

name: Oven-Baked Chicken & Rice
blurb: Chicken thighs and rice baked together in stock until the rice drinks it all up. Feeds four, one dish.
method: Brown the seasoned chicken in an oven dish, remove briefly.
Stir the rice, onion, paprika and stock into the dish, sit the chicken on top.
Cover with foil and bake at 190C for 35 minutes, add peas, uncover and finish 10 minutes.

name: Vegetable Moussaka
blurb: Layers of aubergine, potato and spiced lentils under a baked béchamel. A generous Greek bake.
method: Roast the aubergine and potato slices until soft.
Simmer the lentils with the tomatoes and cinnamon to a thick sauce.
Layer potato, lentils, aubergine, top with the egg-enriched béchamel and cheese and bake at 190C for 45 minutes.

name: Weekend Beef Pho
blurb: A long-simmered charred-onion and spice broth, poured over rice noodles and raw beef to serve.
ingredients: 2 onions and a thumb of ginger, charred
method: Blanch the bones, then simmer with the brisket, charred aromatics and toasted spices for 3 hours; strain and season with fish sauce.
Cook the noodles and divide between bowls with raw sliced sirloin.
Ladle the boiling broth over to cook the beef, serve with the herb plate.

name: Tuscan White Bean & Kale Stew
blurb: A rustic ribollita-style pot of beans, kale and bread, thick enough to stand a spoon in.
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery, add the tomatoes and stock.
Add the beans and kale and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in the torn bread and cook 10 minutes until thick; finish each bowl with olive oil.

name: Lancashire Lamb Hotpot
blurb: Lamb and onions under sliced potatoes, baked slow until the top crisps and the base falls apart.
method: Layer the lamb, onions and carrots in a dish, season each layer.
Pour over the stock and Worcestershire, then fan the potato slices on top and brush with butter.
Cover and bake at 160C for 2 hours, uncover and turn up to 200C for 30 minutes to crisp.

name: Chana Masala for the Week
blurb: A tangy, spiced chickpea curry that costs pennies and reheats better than it started.
ingredients: 1 tsp amchur (dried mango) or extra lemon
method: Fry the onions until deep golden, add the ginger-garlic and ground spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook down, then the chickpeas and a splash of water.
Simmer 20 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken, finish with amchur and garam masala.

name: Toad in the Hole with Onion Gravy
blurb: Sausages baked into a billowing Yorkshire batter, with a jug of dark onion gravy. Feeds four.
method: Whisk the flour, eggs and milk to a batter and rest.
Heat the fat with the sausages in a roasting tin at 220C until sizzling, pour in the batter and bake 30 minutes without opening the door.
Meanwhile caramelise the onions and simmer with the stock to a gravy.

name: Squash & Chickpea Tagine
blurb: Butternut, chickpeas and apricots in a fragrant, lightly spiced tomato braise. Vegan, big pot.
method: Soften the onions, add the ras el hanout for a minute.
Add the squash, chickpeas, apricots, tomatoes and stock and simmer 30 minutes.
Season and serve over couscous with coriander.

name: Soy-Braised Pork Belly
blurb: Cubes of belly pork braised in soy, sugar and spice until glossy and yielding. Serves six over rice.
method: Blanch the pork, then brown in a dry pan to render some fat.
Add all the remaining ingredients, bring to a simmer and cook gently 1.5 hours until tender and the sauce is syrupy.
Skim the fat and serve over rice with steamed greens.

name: Vegetable & Bean Gumbo
blurb: A dark-roux gumbo with okra, peppers and beans over rice. Cajun comfort by the potful.
method: Cook the flour and oil together, stirring, until the roux is milk-chocolate brown.
Add the chopped veg and Cajun spice, then the stock, okra, beans and bay.
Simmer 45 minutes until thick and serve over rice.

name: Chicken Tortilla Soup
blurb: A brothy tomato-chilli soup with shredded chicken, topped with crushed tortilla chips and avocado.
ingredients: tortilla chips, avocado, lime, coriander to serve
method: Soften the onions with the chipotle, add the tomatoes, beans, corn and stock.
Poach the chicken breasts in the soup for 20 minutes, then lift out and shred.
Return the chicken, season, and serve loaded with the crunchy toppings.

name: Beef & Barley Soup
blurb: Chunks of beef and pearl barley simmered with root veg into a thick, sustaining bowl.
method: Brown the beef, soften the diced veg, stir in the purée.
Add the stock, barley and bay and simmer 1.5 hours until the beef is tender and the barley plump.
Season and stir through plenty of parsley.

name: Jerk Chicken with Rice & Peas
blurb: Marinated, spiced chicken with coconut rice and kidney beans.
ingredients: Jerk marinade: 3 spring onions, 2 Scotch bonnets, 4 garlic cloves, 3cm ginger, 1 tbsp allspice, 1 tbsp thyme, 2 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp brown sugar, juice of 1 lime, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp nutmeg
Rice and peas: 300g rice, 400ml coconut milk, 400g tin kidney beans, 2 spring onions, 1 thyme sprig, 1 Scotch bonnet (whole)
method: Blitz the marinade ingredients and rub all over the chicken. Marinate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Roast at 200C fan for 35-40 minutes, or barbecue, until charred and cooked through, basting once.
For the rice and peas, simmer the beans, coconut milk, 200ml water, spring onions, thyme and the whole Scotch bonnet for 5 minutes.
Add the rinsed rice, cover and cook 15 minutes until tender. Remove the chilli and fluff up.
Serve the jerk chicken with the rice and peas.

name: Curry Goat
blurb: Slow-braised goat (or mutton) in Caribbean curry spice with potato.
ingredients: 1.2kg goat or mutton, on the bone, cut into pieces
1 onion, 4 garlic cloves, 3cm ginger, 4 spring onions
1 Scotch bonnet, 1 tsp allspice, 2 thyme sprigs
400ml water or stock, rice to serve
method: Toss the meat with 2 tbsp curry powder, salt and pepper, and leave 1 hour.
Bloom the rest of the curry powder in hot oil for 1 minute, then brown the meat.
Add the onion, garlic, ginger, spring onions, allspice, thyme and the whole Scotch bonnet.
Add the water, cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours until tender.
Add the potato for the last 30 minutes until it thickens the gravy. Serve with rice.

name: Jamaican Beef Patties
blurb: Flaky turmeric pastry filled with spiced, saucy beef mince.
ingredients: Pastry: 350g plain flour, 1 tbsp turmeric, 1 tsp curry powder, 175g cold block margarine or butter, 120ml iced water
1 onion, 3 spring onions, 2 garlic cloves, 1 Scotch bonnet
1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp thyme
method: Rub the fat into the flour and spices, add the water, bring together and chill for 30 minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic, spring onion and chilli, brown the mince, add the spices, stock and breadcrumbs, and cook to a thick, moist filling. Cool.
Roll the pastry thin, cut circles, add filling, fold into half-moons and crimp.
Glaze with egg and bake at 190C fan for 25-30 minutes until golden and flaky.

name: Pork Schnitzel with Potato Salad
blurb: Thin crumbed pork escalopes fried crisp, with a tangy warm potato salad.
ingredients: 4 pork loin steaks, flattened very thin
Oil and butter for frying, lemon wedges
Potato salad: 800g waxy potatoes, 1 small onion, 200ml hot stock, 3 tbsp white wine vinegar, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard, chives
method: Boil the potatoes, slice while warm, and toss with the finely chopped onion, hot stock, vinegar, oil and mustard. Rest.
Coat the pork in flour, egg then breadcrumbs, pressing lightly.
Fry in a generous amount of oil and butter for 2 minutes each side until deep golden, swirling the pan so the crumb souffles.
Drain, season and serve with lemon and the warm potato salad.

name: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut & Mash
blurb: Griddled bratwurst with braised sauerkraut, apple and mustardy mash.
ingredients: 1 tsp caraway seeds, 100ml cider or apple juice
900g potatoes, 60g butter, splash of milk, 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard
method: Fry the onion and apple in butter until soft, add the caraway, sauerkraut and cider, and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter, milk and the mustard; season.
Griddle or fry the bratwurst until browned and cooked through.
Serve the sausages over the mash with the braised sauerkraut.

name: Swedish Meatballs
blurb: Tender beef-and-pork meatballs in a creamy gravy with lingonberry.
ingredients: 1 small onion, grated, 50g breadcrumbs soaked in 60ml milk, 1 egg
40g butter, 30g flour, 500ml beef stock, 150ml double cream, 1 tsp soy
Mash and lingonberry or cranberry sauce to serve
method: Mix the minces with the onion, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, spices and seasoning, and roll into small balls.
Brown all over in butter, then set aside.
Stir the flour into the pan, then whisk in the stock and cream and simmer to a smooth gravy. Add the soy.
Return the meatballs and simmer for 10 minutes. Serve with mash and lingonberry.

name: Potato & Cheese Pierogi
blurb: Boiled-then-fried dumplings filled with mash and cheese, with buttery onions.
ingredients: Dough: 400g plain flour, 1 egg, 200ml warm water, 2 tbsp soured cream, pinch of salt
Filling: 500g mashed potato, 150g farmer's cheese or curd cheese, 50g grated cheddar, fried onion, salt and pepper
method: Knead the dough ingredients until smooth, then rest 30 minutes under a bowl.
Mix the filling. Roll the dough thin, cut circles, add a spoon of filling, fold and seal well.
Boil in batches for 3-4 minutes until they float, then drain.
Fry the onions slowly in the butter until deep gold. Toss the pierogi in the buttery onions until lightly crisp.
Serve with soured cream.

name: Loaded Nachos for Dinner
blurb: A big tray of tortilla chips under cheese, beans, jalapenos and all the toppings.
ingredients: To finish: guacamole, soured cream, salsa, spring onions, coriander
method: Heat oven to 200C fan.
Spread half the chips on a tray, dot with beans, scatter with cheese and jalapenos. Repeat with a second layer.
Bake for 8-10 minutes until the cheese is molten.
Pile on the cold toppings and serve straight from the tray.

name: Bacon & Maple Pancake Stack
blurb: Fluffy American pancakes with crispy bacon and lots of maple syrup.
ingredients: 200g self-raising flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tbsp sugar, pinch of salt
Butter for the pan, maple syrup to serve
method: Fry the bacon until crisp, then keep warm.
Whisk the dry ingredients, then beat in the egg, milk and melted butter to a thick batter.
Cook spoonfuls in a buttered pan over medium heat until bubbles form, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
Stack the pancakes with the bacon and drown in maple syrup.

name: Roast Veg & Halloumi Grain Bowl
blurb: Roasted vegetables, grains, halloumi and a lemony tahini dressing.
ingredients: 1 sweet potato, 1 red onion, 1 courgette, 1 pepper, all chopped
2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp cumin
Dressing: 3 tbsp tahini, juice of 1 lemon, 1 small garlic clove, water
method: Toss the vegetables with the oil and spices and roast at 200C fan for 25-30 minutes.
Warm the grains.
Griddle the halloumi until golden.
Whisk the tahini dressing until pourable.
Build bowls with grains, roast veg, rocket and halloumi, then drizzle with dressing and scatter with seeds.

name: Tomato Soup & Grilled Cheese
blurb: Silky roasted tomato soup with a crisp, molten cheese toastie to dunk.
ingredients: 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp olive oil
1 tbsp tomato puree, 1 tsp sugar, 500ml stock
Splash of cream or milk (optional), basil
Toastie: 8 slices bread, 200g mature cheddar, butter
method: Roast the tomatoes, onion and garlic with the oil at 200C fan for 25 minutes until charred.
Blitz with the puree, sugar and stock, then simmer and season. Loosen with cream if you like.
Butter the bread on the outside, fill with cheese, and griddle over medium heat until golden and molten both sides.
Serve the soup with the toastie cut into soldiers for dunking.

name: Halloumi Katsu Curry
blurb: Crisp panko halloumi with the same mild Japanese curry sauce and rice.
ingredients: 2 x 225g blocks halloumi, sliced into 1cm slabs
2 tbsp mild curry powder, 1 tbsp flour, 1 tbsp garam masala, 1 tsp turmeric
500ml vegetable stock, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tsp honey or maple
method: Soften the onion and carrot, add the garlic, ginger and spices, then the flour.
Whisk in the stock, soy and honey, simmer 15 minutes, then blitz smooth.
Coat the halloumi in flour, egg and panko, and shallow fry for 1-2 minutes each side until golden.
Serve the crisp halloumi sliced over rice with the sauce poured alongside.

name: Rigatoni alla Vodka
blurb: Rigatoni in a silky tomato-cream sauce sharpened with a splash of vodka and chilli.
method: Soften the shallot and chilli in the butter, fry the purée for 3 minutes.
Add the vodka and cook off, then the cream.
Toss the cooked rigatoni through with Parmesan and pasta water.

name: Orecchiette with Sausage & Broccoli
blurb: Fennel sausage crumbled through orecchiette with broccoli, garlic and chilli.
method: Boil the pasta, adding the broccoli for the last 4 minutes.
Fry the sausagemeat in the oil with the garlic and chilli until crisp.
Toss the drained pasta and broccoli through, mashing some broccoli in.

name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
blurb: Guanciale, tomato, pecorino and chilli clinging to hollow bucatini. A Roman staple.
method: Render the guanciale until crisp, remove some for topping.
Add the wine, then the tomatoes and chilli and simmer 12 minutes.
Toss the pasta through with pecorino and the reserved crisp bits.

name: Lamb Ragù Pappardelle
blurb: Slow lamb shoulder ragù with rosemary and red wine over wide ribbons of pappardelle.
method: Brown the lamb, soften the soffritto, add the wine and reduce.
Add the tomatoes, stock and rosemary and braise 2 hours until falling apart, then shred.
Toss with the pasta and plenty of Parmesan.

name: Spaghetti Puttanesca
blurb: A gutsy sauce of tomatoes, olives, capers, anchovy and chilli. Pantry to plate in 20.
method: Melt the anchovies with the garlic and chilli in oil.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer 12 minutes.
Toss with the spaghetti and parsley.

name: Stovetop Mac & Cheese
blurb: No oven — macaroni finished in an evaporated-milk and cheddar sauce until glossy. Fifteen minutes.
method: Cook the macaroni and drain, keeping a splash of water.
Return to the pan with the evaporated milk, cornflour and butter and warm.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar and mustard until smooth.

name: Penne Arrabbiata
blurb: An angry little sauce of garlic, dried chilli and tomato. Fast, fiery, meat-free.
method: Gently fry the garlic and chilli in the oil until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and simmer hard for 12 minutes.
Toss with the penne and parsley.

name: Creamy Mushroom Tagliatelle
blurb: Mixed mushrooms fried hard, deglazed with white wine and cream, tossed with tagliatelle.
method: Fry the mushrooms in oil until deep golden, add the shallot, garlic and thyme.
Add the wine and reduce, then the cream.
Toss the pasta through with Parmesan and pasta water.

name: Fettuccine Alfredo
blurb: Just butter, Parmesan and pasta water emulsified into a glossy cloak around fresh fettuccine.
method: Melt the butter with a ladle of pasta water in a wide pan.
Add the just-cooked pasta and toss.
Off the heat, add the Parmesan in handfuls, tossing hard to a creamy sauce; season with pepper.

name: Classic Beef Lasagne
blurb: Layers of slow beef ragù, béchamel and pasta baked until the edges frazzle. Feeds six.
method: Make a slow ragù with the mince, soffritto, milk and tomatoes, simmering 1 hour.
Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and milk.
Layer ragù, pasta and béchamel three times, top with cheese, bake at 190C for 40 minutes.

name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
blurb: Garlic sliced thin and gently fried in good oil with chilli, tossed with spaghetti and parsley.
method: Warm the oil with the garlic over low heat until pale gold, add the chilli.
Add the drained pasta and a splash of pasta water and toss.
Fold in the parsley and plenty of pepper.

name: Baked Ziti
blurb: Tubes of pasta in a herby tomato sauce with ricotta and mozzarella, baked bubbling. A family bake.
method: Simmer the tomatoes with the garlic and basil for 15 minutes.
Mix the cooked pasta with the sauce and ricotta, tip into a dish.
Top with torn mozzarella and Parmesan and bake at 190C for 25 minutes.

name: Spaghetti & Meatballs
blurb: Herby beef-and-pork meatballs simmered in tomato sauce over a tangle of spaghetti.
method: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg and Parmesan and roll into balls, then brown.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and simmer 25 minutes.
Serve over spaghetti with basil and more Parmesan.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
blurb: Guanciale, egg yolks, pecorino and black pepper — no cream, all technique.
method: Crisp the guanciale slowly; whisk the eggs with the pecorino and pepper.
Toss the hot drained pasta with the guanciale and its fat off the heat.
Add the egg mix, tossing and loosening with pasta water to a glossy sauce.

name: Salmon, Pea & Dill Penne
blurb: Flaked hot-smoked salmon, peas and dill folded through penne in a lemony crème fraîche.
method: Cook the penne, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Off the heat, stir the crème fraîche, lemon, butter and dill into the drained pasta.
Fold in the salmon gently and loosen with pasta water.

name: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
blurb: Gnocchi baked in tomato-basil sauce with pockets of melting mozzarella.
method: Simmer the tomatoes with the garlic and basil for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cooked gnocchi, tip into a dish, dot with mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until bubbling.

name: Chilli Prawn Linguine
blurb: Prawns fried with garlic, chilli and cherry tomatoes, tossed with linguine, lemon and parsley.
method: Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil, add the tomatoes and squash a little.
Add the prawns and cook 2-3 minutes until pink.
Toss the linguine through with lemon, parsley and pasta water.

name: Cheesy Pasta Bake with Greens
blurb: Pasta and broccoli in a mustardy cheese sauce, crumbed and baked. A no-drama family bake.
method: Cook the pasta, adding the broccoli for the last 4 minutes.
Make a cheese sauce with the butter, flour, milk, cheddar and mustard.
Combine, top with breadcrumbs and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

name: Tortellini in Brodo
blurb: Little filled pasta simmered in a clear, good chicken broth with Parmesan. Restorative, quick.
method: Bring the stock to a gentle simmer with the bay.
Drop in the tortellini and cook 3-4 minutes until they float and are tender.
Ladle into bowls with Parmesan, pepper and parsley.

name: Pesto Pasta with Beans & Potato
blurb: The Ligurian way — trofie with pesto, green beans and a few cubes of potato cooked in the pasta water.
method: Boil the pasta with the potato, adding the beans for the last 4 minutes.
Drain, keeping some water, and return to the pan.
Stir the pesto and Parmesan through, loosening with the reserved water.

name: Nduja Spaghetti with Burrata
blurb: A quick nduja-tomato sauce coating spaghetti, topped with a torn ball of cold burrata.
method: Melt the nduja with the garlic, add the passata and simmer 10 minutes.
Toss the spaghetti through with pasta water.
Top each bowl with torn burrata and basil.
